inventory.name: Audio length after loudness step (192 kHz trap)
inventory.how_found: Lesson 5: the first sound check came out 3 s short. ffmpeg's loudnorm quietly switches audio to 192,000 samples/s and the padding after it miscounted. One fix, checked: 23 s asked, 23.04 s delivered.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Resample to 48,000 right after any loudnorm (aresample=48000) and pad to an exact length with apad=whole_dur=<seconds>. Every kit audio file is 48 kHz.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:21-24 (lesson 5); film-kit/narration-tools/mix_voice_over_music.sh lines 7-8 and its filter chain
inventory.computable_from: the requested mix length (timeline end + 4.0 s tail)
inventory.proposed_calculation: After every audio step, read the duration with ffprobe and fail if |measured - requested| > 0.05 s, naming the step. Add this check to mix_*.sh and finish_film.sh.
inventory.already_automatic: The fix is written into mix_voice_over_music.sh and mix_narration_over_music.sh (both in the plugin kit). Nothing checks the length afterwards.
inventory.llm_tip: Never trust an audio filter chain's output length; measure it. If you add a loudnorm step, resample to 48 kHz straight after it.

inventory.name: Music level under the voice (ducking)
inventory.how_found: Lesson 6: the first ducking setting put the music 31 dB under Malina. Four settings were tried and measured. Decisions item 12: the user asked for 'slightly' louder music, so it went up 3 dB (-14 to -11 dB). That measured 18 dB under while she speaks (was about 21) and about 2 dB louder in the pauses.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Music -11 dB overall, EQ -4 dB at 2.5 kHz (width 1.2), sidechaincompress threshold 0.08, ratio 2.5, attack 30 ms, release 1100 ms. Target: music about 18 dB under the voice while she speaks and about 12 dB under in the pauses.
inventory.computable_from: narration track, soundtrack file, timeline (word spans = speaking, gaps = pauses)
inventory.proposed_calculation: measure_duck_gap: render the voice-only and the ducked music-only stems through the same chain. Over word spans take the median of (voice dB - music dB) = gap_speaking; over gaps longer than 0.4 s take the same = gap_pause. Set music_level_db += (gap_speaking - 18) and run once more (the relation is linear in dB). Print both gaps. A new soundtrack then gets its own level without hand-searching.
inventory.already_automatic: No. The constants are fixed in mix_narration_over_music.sh (plugin kit). The gap is never measured or printed, so a different soundtrack would need the same search again.
inventory.llm_tip: Talk about music level as 'dB under the voice while she speaks' (18) and 'in pauses' (12), and measure it. 'Slightly louder' was 3 dB.

inventory.name: Page loudness, float narration and final peak
inventory.how_found: Lesson 11: turning every page to -16 LUFS left peaks at +0.2 dB, which would clip. Fix: keep the narration in floating-point samples and let the final mix's limiter hold delivered peaks at -1.6 dB, measured. Decisions: level by plain volume change, never a compressor.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each page -16 LUFS by gain only. Narration stored as float WAV. Whole mix -15 LUFS. alimiter limit=0.84 (about -1.5 dBFS). Delivered true peak under -1 dB.
inventory.computable_from: the finished, encoded film
inventory.proposed_calculation: At the end of finish_film.sh run ebur128=peak=true on the sendable copy. Fail if integrated loudness is outside -15 +/- 0.5 LUFS or true peak > -1.0 dBTP. Measure the AAC file, not the WAV, because encoding can raise peaks.
inventory.already_automatic: Levelling and the limiter are automatic (plugin kit). The final measurement is a hand-typed command in the skill, not a gate.
inventory.llm_tip: Level pages by gain, not by compressor, and let only the final limiter touch the peaks. Report the measured LUFS and true peak of the encoded file.

inventory.name: Limiter look-ahead delay (5 ms)
inventory.how_found: Lesson 15: lining the film's sound up against the narration at every page showed it 5 ms late. The cause was the limiter's 5 ms look-ahead. Fix: the limiter's own delay compensation. Checked: 0.00 ms at all ten pages.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: alimiter ... latency=1. check_sound_alignment.py must read 0.00 ms (a few ms is tolerated).
inventory.computable_from: finished film + mix + timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: Make check_sound_alignment.py exit non-zero if any page offset is over 2 ms or its correlation score is under 0.8, and call it from finish_film.sh so it always runs.
inventory.already_automatic: The fix is automatic. The alignment check is a separate tool (plugin kit) that someone has to remember to run.
inventory.llm_tip: Any audio filter with look-ahead adds delay. Always run the alignment check after finishing and report the milliseconds.

inventory.name: Mix shape constants (first word, tail, fades)
inventory.how_found: Decisions, Claude's calls of 2026-10-11 and chapter 1: the soundtrack plays from its start and fades out over the last 4 s. These values are kept as constants in the tools.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: First word at 1.08 s. 4.0 s after the last word. Music fade-in 0.8 s, fade-out over the last 4 s. 30 frames a second.
inventory.computable_from: none needed (house constants)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Put the constants in one shared settings file (for example kit/film-settings.json) that assemble_chapter_narration.py, estimate_timeline.py, the mix scripts and make_captions.py all read. Today they are copied in two files and can drift apart.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, as constants, but duplicated across tools.
inventory.llm_tip: Don't change these per film. If one must change, change it in the shared settings so the estimated and real timelines agree.

inventory.name: A word spoken twice must be asked for by which time
inventory.how_found: Found three times. Lesson 12 (chapter 1: 'shells', 'in', 'a', 'its', 'it', 'and', 'prices', 'the'), lesson 28 ('war', 'get', 'prices') and lesson 46 ('machines'). Each time it was caught only by checking every lookup by hand against the recording or the page text before filming.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: kit.at('word', n) with n = which time it is spoken. The default n = 1 silently takes the first.
inventory.computable_from: timeline.json (each page's words) + the page files' kit.at / kit.end calls
inventory.proposed_calculation: lint_word_lookups: parse every page file for at('w'[, n]) and end('w'[, n]). For each call without n, count matches of key(w) on that page. If the count is above 1, fail and list every occurrence with its time and 3 words either side. Simpler still: make wordClock's find() throw when n is left out and the word occurs more than once.
inventory.already_automatic: No. wordClock only throws when a word is missing, never when it is ambiguous (cinema-kit.js and paper-kit.js, both in the plugin).
inventory.llm_tip: Always give the occurrence number for short or common words ('the', 'prices', 'it'), and run the lookup lint before drawing any stills.

inventory.name: Trailing dots when matching words
inventory.how_found: Lesson 45: 'arrives...' was not found as 'arrives'.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Drop trailing dots (and other punctuation) when matching words to times.
inventory.computable_from: timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already done: key = lowercase, strip [^a-z0-9'.], then strip /\.+$/.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, in cinema-kit.js and paper-kit.js (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Ask for words in plain lowercase, without punctuation.

inventory.name: Multi-word delivery cue, and a late first word
inventory.how_found: Lesson 17: the timing tool counted '[in a warm, steady New Zealand accent]' as spoken words. Lesson 18: on all ten pages, ElevenLabs placed the first word 0.03 to 0.32 s after the voice really starts (page 2 worst). Fix: find where her voice begins and move the first word back when the gap is over 0.03 s (9 of 10 pages corrected).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A cue is everything from '[' to ']'. FIRST_WORD_TOLERANCE = 0.03 s, with voice-onset detection.
inventory.computable_from: recordings + transcripts + narration script
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already done for the first word. Extend the same onset check to the first word after every silence longer than 0.5 s inside a page, where transcripts can also run late.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, extract_word_times.py (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Put exactly one bracketed cue at the start of each page; the tool handles its timing.

inventory.name: Longest rest with nothing new on screen
inventory.how_found: Lesson 16: a 0.7 s pause in typing was flagged as a freeze by the old skill's gate until it was declared as a rest. Decisions (chapter 1): a page rests while Malina speaks for no longer than 1.7 s, except 2.5 s on the end card.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: At most 1.7 s with no visual change while the voice speaks (2.5 s on the end card).
inventory.computable_from: timeline + each page's event times (kit.at calls, stillShot moves, graphics start times)
inventory.proposed_calculation: rest_check: collect every visual event per page (piece entrances, word pops, camera move starts and ends, graphics starts and ends, state cuts). For each gap between events that overlaps speech, report gaps over 1.7 s (2.5 s on the last page). Run it on the estimated timeline before recording, and again on the real one.
inventory.already_automatic: No kit tool. The old gate belonged to the anidoodle skill; camera_audit.py measures only the camera.
inventory.llm_tip: Plan each page as a list of visual events, each with its word. Where two events are more than 1.7 s apart while she talks, add a beat or a slow, named camera move.

inventory.name: Pause between pages, and page turn timing
inventory.how_found: Decisions (chapter 1): pages separated by 1.1 to 1.7 s for the page turn. Chapter 1 used 1.7, 1.4, 1.1, 1.5, 1.5, 1.3, 1.5, 1.4, 1.6, longer where the turn has more to do. The page turns 0.3 s after its last word, once the pieces have folded away.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Pause 1.1 to 1.7 s, default 1.4 (assemble). The turn starts 0.3 s after the last word.
inventory.computable_from: page files (pieces still standing at the last word, fold-away and peel durations) + timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: pause_after(page) = clamp(0.3 + foldaway_seconds(pieces standing at the last word) + 0.5 x peel_seconds, 1.1, 1.7). Add 4.0 s when the page ends on a guess (see 'Guess hold'). Write the list both as --pauses for assemble and as --pause-after for estimate_timeline.
inventory.already_automatic: Only defaults, and the two tools disagree: 1.4 in assemble, 1.5 in estimate_timeline. Chapter 1's per-page pauses were chosen by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Use one default in both tools, and lengthen a pause only where the page turn has more to fold away.

inventory.name: Narrator speed for planning length
inventory.how_found: Lesson 126 (log 33): planned at 140 words a minute, but Malina read 164, and the page carrying the key sentence was the second fastest (175). Lesson 35: the guide called chapter 1 about 2,500 words when it is about 520 spoken words (corrected from the word times).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Plan at about 160 words a minute, measured from her real recordings. estimate_timeline.py predicted 251.7 s of speech as 252 s.
inventory.computable_from: narration script + any earlier word-times file of the same voice
inventory.proposed_calculation: estimate_timeline prints per page: words, seconds and words a minute. Flag pages above 1.1 x the chapter median. Fail if the page marked as holding the key idea ("key": true in the script) is above the median. Total = sum of predicted word lengths + pauses + 1.08 + 4.0. Always take word counts from word times, never from a draft.
inventory.already_automatic: estimate_timeline.py exists in the film kit but is NOT in the plugin kit, and it does not flag fast pages.
inventory.llm_tip: Never plan with a generic 140 wpm; measure the narrator. Give the main idea a slower page with fewer words.

inventory.name: Guess hold after a question to the viewer
inventory.how_found: Lesson 129: each '...' gave Malina under a second, no longer than a full stop. A guess needs about 4 s held after the page ends.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Hold 4.0 s after a page that asks the viewer to guess (estimate_timeline --pause-after PAGE=4.0).
inventory.computable_from: script text (a question to the viewer, 'guess', 'think about it')
inventory.proposed_calculation: A script lint marks pages whose last sentence is a question to the viewer or contains guess-words. It sets pause_after = 4.0 for both timeline tools and reminds the page builder to hold the shot still through it.
inventory.already_automatic: Manual flag only.
inventory.llm_tip: A written pause is not thinking time. Hold the picture for about 4 s after a guess.

inventory.name: Voice steadiness gate
inventory.how_found: Decisions item 11: the accent switched and there was random shouting. Item 20: steadiness is checked by measurement, not by ear: pitch spread across pages 2.2 semitones (chapter 1, which sounded unsteady: 3.0), and no word much louder than the rest.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: find_loud_words: a word more than 6 dB above its page's typical word. find_raised_voice: a word 5 or more semitones above the page's typical pitch. compare_voice_steadiness: spread of typical pitch across pages (2.2 accepted, 3.0 not), and bursts more than 7 semitones up.
inventory.computable_from: recordings + word times
inventory.proposed_calculation: One gate script runs all three right after recording and prints PASS or RE-RECORD per page. Re-record a page when its typical pitch is more than 1.5 semitones from the chapter median, or when any unmarked word is over 6 dB or 5 or more semitones above its page.
inventory.already_automatic: The tools exist (plugin kit) with these defaults, but there is no single pass/fail gate.
inventory.llm_tip: Judge the voice by numbers, not by ear, and re-record only flagged pages. Each page is its own recording.

inventory.name: Script lint before paid recording (cue, capitals, names)
inventory.how_found: Decisions, voice fix: ElevenLabs offers no voice-level accent rules. So every page opens with one instruction, '[in a warm, steady New Zealand accent]', with no other cues. No capitals for emphasis (they make the voice push). Mattei is respelled in English sounds, 'muh-TAY-ee' (the Italian phonetic spelling pulled the accent).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: One leading bracket cue per page. No ALL-CAPS words. Names in English-sound respellings (the script's phonetic_names).
inventory.computable_from: narration script JSON
inventory.proposed_calculation: Lint each page: exactly one [..] at the start and no other brackets; no all-capital token of 2 or more letters except a whitelist (NZ, GDP); every name in phonetic_names appears only in its respelled form. Errors stop the paid recording step.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Run a script lint before spending any credits; a bad cue costs a whole re-record.

inventory.name: Download recordings at once
inventory.how_found: Workflows, chapter steps: ElevenLabs links stop working after 2 hours. The transcript (word times) is free.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Download each page into downloads/<voice>/chapterN/ straight away and ask for its transcript.
inventory.computable_from: the generation job result
inventory.proposed_calculation: A record_page wrapper does it in one call: generate, download, request the transcript, save pageN.mp3 and pageN-words.json under fixed names, then run extract_word_times (which already refuses a transcript that doesn't match the script).
inventory.already_automatic: Manual. Only the transcript-mismatch refusal is automatic.
inventory.llm_tip: Never leave a paid recording only as a link.

inventory.name: Re-recording one page shifts everything after it
inventory.how_found: Workflows: re-recording one page changes every time after it, so steps 2 to 7 are redone for the whole chapter. Pages ask for words, not seconds, so they retime themselves.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Rebuild word times, timeline, mix and captions, and re-film every chunk from the changed page onward.
inventory.computable_from: old timeline vs new timeline, plus the chunk list
inventory.proposed_calculation: A one-command rebuild (make-style) re-runs extract, assemble, mix and captions. It compares page start times between the old and new timeline and deletes only the film chunks whose frame range moved (every page from the first changed one, unless that page's pause absorbs the change).
inventory.already_automatic: No. Retiming of pages is automatic; the rebuild and the choice of chunks to re-film are manual.
inventory.llm_tip: Before re-recording page k, know that every page after k must be re-filmed unless its pause absorbs the length change.

inventory.name: Captions and the sendable copy
inventory.how_found: Decisions (chapter 1): captions come as a separate file because phone apps put their own captions and buttons over the bottom. Decision 16: a file sent in chat can't be over 30 MB.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Captions as .srt and .vtt: 42 letters at most, held 0.15 s after the last word, at least 0.8 s, new caption at each sentence end but not after an initial. Sendable copy 28 MB, two-pass H.264 with AAC 128 kbps; video kbps = (28 x 8000 x 0.97) / seconds - 128.
inventory.computable_from: timeline, film length
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, make_captions.py and finish_film.sh (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Don't burn captions into the picture; deliver the .srt and keep words on screen minimal.

inventory.name: Words on screen are short forms of what is said
inventory.how_found: Decisions (chapter 1, items 13 and 20): words on the pages are short forms of what Malina says, never more. Critics later caught on-screen words that added claims (lesson 53).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every on-screen word or number must be said within its page and near its moment, as the same word, a short form, or the numeral of a spoken number.
inventory.computable_from: page files (word, card and callout texts with their times) + timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: words_on_screen_check: for each on-screen text, split it into content words and numbers. For each, search the page's spoken words within +/- 6 s of its appearance (exact, stem, or number-to-words: '8 MILLION' = 'eight million'). List any that are not found for a human to accept as a short form or remove.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: If a word on screen isn't heard at that moment, it is a new claim. Cut it or get it said.

inventory.name: Hold the key number still
inventory.how_found: Lesson 53 critique: a key figure was still counting while it was said, then faded at once, so it was never read. The plugin guide records the rule.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A count must finish on its word and hold for at least 1 s afterwards.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:210-214; plugin/skills/build-cinema-page/guide.md ('Hold the key number still')
inventory.computable_from: page files (counter start, end and fade times) + timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: For every counter or number graphic: assert count_end <= at(word_of_number) + 0.1 and visible_until >= count_end + 1.0. Fail with the page and word.
inventory.already_automatic: No; it is prose in the plugin guide.
inventory.llm_tip: Finish counts on the spoken number and hold them at least a second.

inventory.name: Readable words: contrast and a dark band over busy sets
inventory.how_found: Lesson 53: pale labels on pale walls couldn't be read. Lesson 66: words over a busy set (chimneys, papers on a desk) need a soft dark band, as the street already had.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Use a dark plate behind the words (callout plate: true) or a soft dark band wherever the background is pale or busy.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:210-214, 260-261; plugin/skills/build-cinema-page/guide.md ('Pale words on pale surfaces vanish')
inventory.computable_from: a still at each word's moment + the word's screen box
inventory.proposed_calculation: For every on-screen text, take the still at mid-display. Measure the background behind its box (widened 20 px): the luminance contrast ratio (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) against the text colour, and how busy it is (std of a Laplacian). If contrast < 4.5 or the business is above the value measured behind chapter 2's accepted street titles, turn plate: true on automatically, or report it.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check every word at phone size against what is behind it, not on a plain test background.

inventory.name: Letters that change into other letters in cut-out fonts
inventory.how_found: Lesson 13: a cut-out T read as I ('THREE PARIS'), and a narrow I read as two lines or a slash. Serif fonts give the T a foot; outline and slanted fonts thin the I. Fix: those letters skip those fonts. Checked by redrawing every title and reading it at full size.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: T never in serif fonts; I never in outline or slanted fonts. Read every title letter by letter at full size.
inventory.computable_from: the rendered title pictures + their intended text
inventory.proposed_calculation: Render each title, run OCR (tesseract, single-line mode), and compare it with the intended text letter by letter. Any mismatch fails and names the letter and font.
inventory.already_automatic: No kit check (the fix lived in chapter 1's scrapbook label code; the paper and cinema looks use plain Inter).
inventory.llm_tip: Use one plain heavy font (Inter) for words. If you mix fonts, OCR every title.

inventory.name: Never use an image or video program's lettering
inventory.how_found: Lessons 92 and 103: Flux turned the dates into nonsense. Nano Banana Pro wrote 'FITE WILL DE CLOSED' and '1756'; Seedance wrote 'PRIDAY' and '1828'. Decisions item 12: video models can't be trusted to spell or count. Decision 34: no blank signs.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: All lettering comes from our own 3D or 2D code. In projected sets, signs keep their own surface (ownSurface), colour-matched to the painting where they stand.
inventory.computable_from: the set's material list (build scripts write lettering-sizes.json)
inventory.proposed_calculation: When a set is loaded, put every material whose texture comes from the lettering step (listed in lettering-sizes.json) into ownSurface automatically, with calibrate on. Warn if a group named sign, notice, placard or book has no lettered material.
inventory.already_automatic: ownSurface and calibrate exist in projected-set.js (film kit only; projected-set.js is NOT in the plugin kit). The list of lettered materials is written by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Ask painters for blank boards and draw every word yourself; keep lettered materials off the projection.

inventory.name: Camera rule: still, at most 3 named moves per shot
inventory.how_found: Decisions item 25 (the user's words) and lesson 57: most pages crept for their whole length (page 1: one 20 s push), which reads as restless on a phone. The rule was built into the engine and a checker was added.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: kit.stillShot holds still and allows only named moves (zoom in or out, pan left, right, up or down, move up or down; focus doesn't count), at most 3 per shot, never overlapping. camera_audit.py: moving = turning faster than 0.6 deg/s, or travelling more than 1.2% of the distance to the focus per second, or lens change over 1.2%/s. Moves less than 0.35 s apart count as one. A cut = a jump over a quarter of that distance or a turn over 8 deg. The audit must end '0 problem(s)'.
inventory.computable_from: page files (stillShot plans) + camera samples
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed. Add: fail when a single move lasts longer than its page's spoken sentence (a creep), or when a shot holds no still part at all.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, stillShot and camera_audit.py are in the plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: Name every move by why it happens; if a page needs a fourth move, cut to a new shot.

inventory.name: Measure camera moves against the focus distance
inventory.how_found: Lesson 58: in a painted room the camera aims at a point 30 units away, so a real one-unit move looked tiny to the first checker. Using the focus distance fixed it.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Measure travel as a share of the distance to the thing in focus, not to the aim point.
inventory.computable_from: camera samples (position, target, focus)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already: travel per second / focus distance > 1.2%.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes (camera_audit.py, plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Always give stillShot a focus point on the subject; the checker uses it.

inventory.name: Small camera moves inside a painted relief room
inventory.how_found: Lesson 48: moving far inside a painted room tears it: thin near things (pillars, cables) smear and the camera sees past the painting's bottom edge. Fix: moves of 1 to 2 units, a softer distance picture, and past the edge the painting is mirrored. Lesson 77: even a short move bends near upright posts and edges.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Keep moves inside a relief room to 1-2 units at chapter 2's room depths. Depth picture smoothed (prepare_relief.py --blur 3). Past the edge, mirror the painting.
inventory.computable_from: the relief's depth picture, near/far/fov, and the planned camera path
inventory.proposed_calculation: Parallax limit: f_px = 960 / tan(fov_v / 2). For a sideways or forward step t, the near-far shift is f_px x t x (1/z_near - 1/z_far), where z_near is the 5th-percentile depth inside the frame. Work out this number once for chapter 2's accepted 1-2 unit moves and use the largest as the cap for new rooms. Also project the frame's corners each sample and fail if any leaves the relief's edge.
inventory.already_automatic: No; the 1-2 units is prose.
inventory.llm_tip: In a painted relief room, push in with the lens rather than travelling, and keep travel small.

inventory.name: Plate wider than the film lens; how far the camera may turn or slide
inventory.how_found: Lesson 90 (log 29): with a 44-degree plate and the film's 40-degree lens, the camera could turn only about 1 degree each side before part of the frame had no painting (blue in the weights view). Workflows (built place, step 2): pick the plate's lens a little wider than the film's.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Plate 44 deg vs film 40 deg (vertical) allows about 1 deg of turn each side. Push in with the lens (a lens change uncovers nothing). Check the weights view at the end of each move: blue at a frame edge means no painting there.
inventory.computable_from: the page's stillShot moves (film camera path) + the projector camera.json
inventory.proposed_calculation: Horizontal fov H(v) = 2 x atan(tan(v/2) x 9/16). Allowed turn each side = (H(plate) - H(film)) / 2 (44 vs 40 gives about 1.25 deg). For a planned path: sample the film camera every 0.1 s, cast its four frame corners into the scene (ray to the set's surface), project those points into the projector, and require all to land inside [0.01, 0.99]. Return the smallest plate fov that passes: v_plate = 2 x atan(max |corner tan| / aspect factor) + 1 deg margin. Run it before rendering the plate.
inventory.already_automatic: No. The weights view (projected-set.js) has to be looked at by eye, and projected-set.js is not in the plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: Decide the camera path first, then choose the plate's lens from it, not the other way round.

inventory.name: Weights view: blue at the frame edge
inventory.how_found: Lesson 90 and the traps: a seam of plain surfaces showed where the camera had left the painting. Found by looking at the weights view (orange = painting, green = behind painting, blue = own surface).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No blue at any frame edge at the end of any move.
inventory.computable_from: weights-view stills at the end of each move
inventory.proposed_calculation: Render the weights view at every move's end and middle. Count pixels within 2% of each frame edge whose colour is nearest the blue code (0.05, 0.12, 0.5). Fail if more than 0.1% of the edge band is blue, and print the edge and the time.
inventory.already_automatic: No; the view exists, but it is judged by eye.
inventory.llm_tip: Never judge a projected-set move from the painted still; read the weights view.

inventory.name: Hand-over angle to the behind painting, and contact shadows
inventory.how_found: Lesson 96: round near props, the painting gave way to the props-removed painting only after the camera had swung 1.4 deg round a point; further up the road that took half the move, and ink lines showed meanwhile. Half a degree works. A soft 3D shadow faded in at the same time replaces the painted shadow the hand-over removes. The brazier floated until it had one.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Hand-over within about 0.5 deg (projected-set behind.quickMove = 0.00003). Every near prop gets a soft contact shadow, faded in as the camera starts to move.
inventory.computable_from: camera path + near-prop list
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already the default in projected-set.js. Add: for each prop in behind.hide, create its contact shadow automatically (an ellipse under its base, from shot_facts' bottom box) with its fade tied to the same quickMove amount.
inventory.already_automatic: The hand-over default is automatic (film kit only; projected-set.js is missing from the plugin kit). Contact shadows are added by hand per prop.
inventory.llm_tip: Every near prop that hides painted ground needs its own contact shadow.

inventory.name: Turn to aim, slide to move
inventory.how_found: Lesson 99 (clip 29): a turn during the move slid where the lines meet onto the colliery door at the frame edge and put the pithead out of frame. Lessons 106-107: a turn can't close the gap between where the lines meet and the subject (it moves both). Slide sideways to clear the phone buttons: near props slide more than far ones while the meeting point stays put.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Set the aim with the turn once. During moves the camera only slides (straight line, constant turn). To move the subject on screen relative to where the lines meet, slide the camera or move the subject.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:384-386, 407-411; film-kit/07 Composing a shot.md rule 11
inventory.computable_from: stillShot moves (position and target per move) + subject position
inventory.proposed_calculation: In projected or built sets, stillShot should refuse a move whose view direction changes by more than 0.5 deg (target moving out of line with position). Slide solver: to move the subject by dx (frame fraction) at depth z, slide sideways s = dx x 2 x z x tan(H/2), where H is the horizontal fov.
inventory.already_automatic: No. stillShot allows 'pan' moves (turns) in every set, and check_shot only reports turns.
inventory.llm_tip: In a built-and-painted set, never pan during a move; aim first, then slide.

inventory.name: Camera at a person's eye height
inventory.how_found: Lesson 100: a camera in the middle of an empty road belongs to no one. On the pavement at eye height, looking down into the drum and onto the seat, the view is a villager's.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Camera 1.5 to 1.9 m above the surface under it (1.7 default), standing where a person would stand.
inventory.computable_from: the set's ground height under the camera (Blender ray)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Placement helper: camera z = ground(x, y) + 1.7. check_shot already fails outside 1.5-1.9.
inventory.already_automatic: The check is automatic in check_shot.py (film kit; the plugin copy is an older version). Placement is manual.
inventory.llm_tip: Put the camera where a person in the story could stand; only then aim it.

inventory.name: Match the camera to a liked picture by landmarks
inventory.how_found: Lesson 105 (log 31): 'The lines don't converge the same way' was the camera, not the props. Matching the liked picture's landmarks (wheel hubs, chimney top, gate, roofline, kerbs) found our camera 0.42 m too high and 1 deg off. Fitted, the lines meet within 0.02 of the picture's.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Fit the camera to 5 or more landmarks before moving any prop. Where the lines meet must match within 0.03 of the frame.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:404-406; Decisions.md:586-587; check_shot.py check_camera_match and check_reference_lines (0.03 tolerance)
inventory.computable_from: landmark points read off the reference + the same points in Blender metres
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed (a camera pose fit in check_shot). It needs a 'camera_match' list in the check file.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, in check_shot.py (film kit; plugin copy older).
inventory.llm_tip: When a reference 'feels different', fit the camera first; prop moves come after.

inventory.name: Frame with numbers before rendering (edge margins)
inventory.how_found: Lesson 63: frame_check.py found price boards off the edge and cut-outs too wide before any still was made. Workflows 3b.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Keep things 140 px from the sides and top, and 380 px from the bottom (phone buttons), on 1080 x 1920. Anything to read stays left of 0.90 across; story props left of 0.95 where the buttons are.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:252-254; Workflows.md:110-111; film-kit/paper-film/tools/frame_check.py header; check_shot.py rule 12
inventory.computable_from: camera position, target, fov + object positions and sizes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Add the inverse: the camera distance at which an object of width W fills a share f of the frame width is d = W / (2 x f x tan(H/2)). frame_check should take the object's box (8 corners, from inspect_glb or shot_facts) rather than one point, so wide things are caught.
inventory.already_automatic: frame_check.py (point check) is in the plugin kit; check_shot does boxes. The inverse sizing is not computed.
inventory.llm_tip: Run frame_check with every important object's corners before drawing a single still.

inventory.name: A standing piece's edge must stay inside the frame at its own distance
inventory.how_found: Lesson 31: a piece standing in front of the page looks bigger than its size on the page (it is nearer the camera), so pieces placed to the page's edge poked out. Seven pieces were moved in or shrunk.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Keep a piece's edge within about 4.1 units of the middle at the page plane, less for pieces further forward.
inventory.computable_from: camera distance to the page D, the piece's stand-off z, its x position and half-width
inventory.proposed_calculation: Visible half-width at the piece's depth: w(z) = (D - z) x tan(H/2). Require |x| + half_width <= w(z) x (1 - 2 x 140/1080). Check every piece at every event time from the page's poses, and print the largest allowed |x| per piece.
inventory.already_automatic: No; the 4.1 figure is prose in the plugin docs.
inventory.llm_tip: Never place a standing piece by its position on the page alone; check it at its own distance.

inventory.name: In a tall frame, stack things in depth, not side by side
inventory.how_found: Lesson 64: three cut-outs in a row were 2.4 units wide and fell off both edges; staggered front to back, they fit large. Soft barrels, crates and a cart in the near corners fill the bottom third.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Stagger groups front to back; fill the bottom third with soft near props in the corners.
inventory.computable_from: camera + the planned row's widths and depths
inventory.proposed_calculation: Row fit: sum of widths + gaps must be <= 2 x w(z) x (1 - 2 x 140/1080) at the row's depth z. If it is too wide, spread the pieces in depth so each one's projected box fits and they overlap by 10 to 30% of the smaller width.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: A 9:16 frame is narrow: think in depth layers, not rows.

inventory.name: Main composition rule: the strong things agree on the subject
inventory.how_found: Lesson 98 (log 30): even weight left and right was not enough; clip 29 was as even as the liked picture and still looked scattered. Decision 36: measured, then tested by critics.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Where the lines meet, the brightest 3% of the frame, the biggest near props, the warm light and the cause-and-effect all point at the subject. The meeting point is within 0.03 of the frame width of the subject's edge.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:380-383, 517; film-kit/07 Composing a shot.md (main rule, rule 1); check_shot.py check_lines (gap <= 0.03)
inventory.computable_from: shot_facts (exact meeting point from the camera) + the finished still
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed by check_shot (3D) and measure_composition (picture).
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in check_shot.py and measure_composition.py. The plugin has an older check_shot and no check-shot tests or notice-corner example.
inventory.llm_tip: Run the shot checker on every composed frame. Fix the camera first, then the props, then the light.

inventory.name: Story props touch; work props small and far; nothing dark where the eye enters
inventory.how_found: Lesson 101: props that touch read as a story, props apart read as a list. Never put a big dark prop where the eye enters the frame (bottom left). Lesson 121: a check limited to story props missed a background near-touch (lamp post just meeting the dustbins; handcart overlapping by only 11 px).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Overlap story props clearly, or leave a clear gap; never let edges just touch. Work props small and far. No big dark prop at bottom left. Check background props for near-touches too.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:390-392, 452-454; check_shot.py rules 3, 4, 8 and check_dark_entry; 'pairs_also' in the check file
inventory.computable_from: shot_facts group pictures (ids.png, solo/*.png)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Rule 4 pairs check: make pairs_also default to ALL named groups (every pair within 40 px), not a hand list.
inventory.already_automatic: Rules 3, 4 and 8 and the dark-entry check are automatic in check_shot.py. The background pairs must be listed by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Put every prop group in the check file, background ones included.

inventory.name: The line-finder misses soft lines
inventory.how_found: Lesson 104: measure_composition.py found 47 street lines in the sharp picture but only 4 to 7 in clip 29's softer frames, so its meeting point was wrong.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Under about 15 lines found, don't trust it; trace kerbs and gutters by hand, or take the meeting point from 3D.
inventory.computable_from: the 3D scene's street direction + camera
inventory.proposed_calculation: Prefer shot_facts' exact meeting point (from the camera and the 'lines' directions in the check file). Use picture line-finding only for outside references, and refuse to report a meeting point when fewer than 15 lines are found.
inventory.already_automatic: measure_composition warns in its header text; check_shot uses the exact 3D point.
inventory.llm_tip: For our own shots, use the 3D meeting point; for pictures, count the lines first.

inventory.name: Factories page: start wide, on a diagonal, lower exposure, labels inside
inventory.how_found: Lesson 47: the first factories page was too close and too bright and cut its labels off (white boxes filled the frame). Fix: factories on a diagonal, camera starts wide, brick and panes printed on the card, lower exposure, every label keeps itself inside the frame.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Place big boxy models on a diagonal, open wide, and print detail on plain faces. Labels flip to the other side when they would run off the frame.
inventory.evidence: Lessons.md:190-193; film-kit/paper-film/scenes/graphics.js:126 ('keep the words inside the frame: flip')
inventory.computable_from: camera + label boxes; the still's luminance
inventory.proposed_calculation: Labels: already automatic. Exposure: measure the share of the frame above 0.95 luminance in a still; if it is over 2%, lower exposure by log2(p99 / 0.92).
inventory.already_automatic: Label flipping is automatic (graphics.js, plugin kit). Exposure is hand-tuned.
inventory.llm_tip: Large flat faces near the camera blow out; open wide and add printed detail.

inventory.name: Pieces read differently from a high camera (crane, open pages)
inventory.how_found: Lesson 37: the paper crane flattened into spikes from a high camera; fixed by turning it side-on, raising its neck and wings, and lowering the camera. Lesson 39: printed upright strokes on a flat page read as a wall; print shapes that only read as lying flat (an ellipse pond, garden rows).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Thin folded props face the camera side-on. Ground prints use flat-reading shapes, not upright strokes.
inventory.computable_from: camera tilt + prop orientation
inventory.proposed_calculation: Warn when the camera looks down more than 35 deg onto a prop whose main plane is horizontal (its silhouette area shrinks below 40% of its side-on area).
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check thin props from the actual camera, not from a model preview.

inventory.name: Layout collisions at each moment
inventory.how_found: Lesson 14: in close-ups, the BORN stamp covered a letter, a candle reached into the header strip, two posters overlapped, a flag was a tiny scribble, and the shells sat small and off-centre. Fixed by hand after looking at each page.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No two pieces or words overlap unless meant to; nothing enters the header strip; no piece smaller than readable on a phone.
inventory.computable_from: page poses at every event time + piece boxes
inventory.proposed_calculation: At each event time, project every visible piece's box. Report overlaps of text with anything, intrusions into the header band, and pieces under about 60 px tall on 1080 x 1920 (too small to read). Use room.clearance / boxesOverlap for 3D.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: boxesOverlap and room.clearance exist but are called by hand at chosen moments.
inventory.llm_tip: Run the overlap check at every word an item lands on, not just once per page.

inventory.name: Knocked-down pieces near the bottom of the frame
inventory.how_found: Lesson 30: a piece 'slapped flat' lies toward the camera like a shelf; seen from above, table legs and a flattened pay packet showed their plain paper backs as pale blobs. Fix: fold down and disappear.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Pieces in the lower part of the frame fold down and vanish rather than lying flat. Only high-in-frame pieces may stay flat.
inventory.computable_from: piece pose (fold angle) + screen position
inventory.proposed_calculation: Warn when a piece's fold passes 60 deg toward the camera while its centre is in the lower 40% of the frame and it stays visible for more than 0.3 s.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Anything knocked flat near the bottom shows its blank back; make it disappear.

inventory.name: Shadows from both faces, and the lamp-only check
inventory.how_found: Lesson 20: no shadows in the first paper test; flat sheets facing the lamp cast nothing (three.js draws shadows from back faces only). Found by lighting with the lamp alone and by a bare one-card test.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every sheet casts from both faces (shadowSide DoubleSide). Check with the lamp alone (check-shadows.mjs).
inventory.computable_from: one lamp-only still
inventory.proposed_calculation: Automatic test: render lamp-only and normal stills at one moment. Inside each piece's shadow zone (offset along the lamp direction), the lamp-only still must be at least 30% darker than the normal one; fail if any piece casts nothing.
inventory.already_automatic: The stage setting is automatic; check-shadows.mjs is in the plugin, but it is judged by eye.
inventory.llm_tip: A scene can look fine with no shadows at all; prove shadows with the lamp alone.

inventory.name: Soft shadow kind in the software renderer
inventory.how_found: Lesson 21: the smoothest soft shadows (VSM) need half-float filtering that the hidden browser's software renderer lacks; it failed silently.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Use PCFShadowMap with shadow.radius 5 (paper stage); 2048 map, radius 6, normalBias 0.02 (cinema kit).
inventory.computable_from: none (renderer capability)
inventory.proposed_calculation: At stage start, test for OES_texture_half_float_linear; if it is missing and VSM was asked for, switch to PCF and print a warning instead of failing silently.
inventory.already_automatic: PCF is the fixed default.
inventory.llm_tip: Don't change the shadow type; the software renderer can't do VSM.

inventory.name: How far pieces stand from the page so shadows show
inventory.how_found: Lesson 22: at 0.5 units the shadows hid behind each piece's paper margin and the dark cobbles. Pieces moved out (soldiers 0.7, back crowd 1.25, tank 1.95, front crowd 2.7, miner 1.6) and the lamp got a larger share of the light. Then the words' shadows read as a ghostly second word, so words moved in to 0.55. Lesson 32: falling words also at 0.55, with dust behind them.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Pieces 0.7 to 2.7 units out (bigger pieces further). Words 0.55, including falling words.
inventory.computable_from: lamp direction, piece height, paper margin width, letter height
inventory.proposed_calculation: Shadow offset on the page = d x tan(a), where a is the angle between the lamp and the page's normal. For pieces choose d so the offset >= margin + 0.1 x piece height: d_min = (margin + 0.1h) / tan(a). For words cap d so the offset <= 0.3 x letter height: d_max = 0.3 x h_letter / tan(a). Calibrate a from chapter 1's accepted values (words 0.55, pieces 0.7-2.7).
inventory.already_automatic: No; the values are typed in each page.
inventory.llm_tip: Words close to the page, pieces further out; a word's shadow must never read as a second word.

inventory.name: Folded props shading themselves dark
inventory.how_found: Lesson 36: folded-paper trees came out almost black. With shadows off they were lit, so they were shading themselves: the shadow push along the surface direction went into the tree, because faces were built facing inward.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No push along the surface (normalBias 0) for folded props; a slightly larger plain bias instead.
inventory.computable_from: the prop's mesh (face normals vs centre)
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each mesh, count faces whose normal points toward the mesh's centre. If more than 10% do (mixed winding), set normalBias = 0 and bias = -0.0005 x scene scale automatically, and print it.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: If a lit object stays dark, switch its shadows off once: if it brightens, it is shading itself.

inventory.name: Shadow ripple rings and second-light shadows
inventory.how_found: Lesson 40: faint rings rippled across the pages (lamp shadow set too tight), and the moon's shadows criss-crossed the lamp's.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A larger shadow margin (bias). Only one shadow-casting light; secondary lights (moon, fills) cast none.
inventory.computable_from: scene light list
inventory.proposed_calculation: Lint: if more than one light has castShadow, warn and keep it only on the key light. Pick the bias from shadow texel size: bias ≈ 1.5 x (shadow camera width / mapSize) / depth range.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: One lamp casts shadows; the others only light.

inventory.name: Reflections turned down inside paintings
inventory.how_found: Lesson 49: banknotes inside a dark painting came out as white bricks; the soft grey reflection room lit them far more than the painting's own light. Fix: a reflections setting, 0.3 inside paintings, and banknote edges printed as fine green lines.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: kit reflections (scene.environmentIntensity) = 0.3 inside painted rooms; default 1.
inventory.computable_from: the painted room's average luminance vs the environment's
inventory.proposed_calculation: reflections = clamp(mean luminance of the painting around the models / mean luminance of RoomEnvironment (≈0.5), 0.1, 1). A dark painting gives about 0.3.
inventory.already_automatic: The option exists (plugin kit), but the default is 1 and it is set by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Models inside a dark painting look white unless reflections come down.

inventory.name: Blender shadow memory (EEVEE)
inventory.how_found: Lesson 110: at '1024' the 1,536-wide plate ran out ('Shadow buffer full') and drew a false hard black wedge, which three critics blamed on the lighting. At '2048' this machine couldn't set it up ('Could not allocate shadow atlas') and drew no shadows.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: shadow_pool_size '1024' and shadow_resolution_scale = min(1, 1080 / width). Read the render log before judging light.
inventory.computable_from: render width + the render log
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed in set_dressing.render(). Make the render wrapper grep its own log and fail on either message.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in set_dressing.py and check_shot (with RENDER_LOG), film kit only. pit-village/ is NOT in the plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: Before blaming the lights, read the render log for shadow-memory errors.

inventory.name: Warm light kept to 3% of the frame; subject lit from below
inventory.how_found: Lessons 111-112: brightness hid warmth, so warmth is measured as a share of red against blue. A deeper orange fire spread warm light over 6.3% of the frame (limit 3%). FIRE_WATTS went 900 > 300 (4.4%) > 220 deep orange (6.3%) > 140 (4.5%) > 70. A separate narrow deep-orange spot lights only the notice.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Warm area: pixels with (R-B)/255 x grey > 0.18 must cover <= 3% of the frame. Lit from below: (R-B)/(R+B) of the subject's bottom 15% minus its top 15% >= 0.10 (the liked picture measures 0.17). Fire 70 W; notice spot 200 W, 50 deg, blend 0.9, no shadow, cutoff 1.4 m.
inventory.computable_from: Blender scene (lights, groups) + low-sample renders
inventory.proposed_calculation: Auto-tune each warm light by bisection on energy (EEVEE, 16 samples, 540 px wide): lower until warm share <= 3% and no burnt pixels on the subject; raise the subject's own spot until lit-from-below >= 0.10. Start from the inverse square: E = target irradiance x d^2. Cutoff distance = farthest target surface + 0.2 m, and below the nearest non-target surface in the beam (ray-cast along the cone).
inventory.already_automatic: The measurements are automatic (check_shot). The wattages were found by hand over 5+ renders.
inventory.llm_tip: Light the subject with its own narrow, linked spot and keep the fire's own light low; measure warmth as red against blue, not brightness.

inventory.name: A wide strong light burns white; small lamps near props
inventory.how_found: Lesson 118: 700 W in a 50-deg beam turned 8% of the notice pure white, and its bottom measured less warm (0.04 vs 0.09). Fix: spread wide only with power cut (200 W). The notice-corner script records the lantern going 60 > 15 > 5 > 3 > 2 > 1 W, because the seat right under it was the brightest thing in the frame.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Notice spot 200 W at 50 deg. Lantern 1 W (its flicker added live).
inventory.computable_from: light positions, distances to the subject and to nearby props
inventory.proposed_calculation: Keeping the same light per area when a cone widens: E2 = E1 x (1 - cos(c2/2)) / (1 - cos(c1/2)). A lamp close to a prop: E_lamp <= E_subjectlight x (d_lamp_to_prop / d_subjectlight_to_subject)^2. For the lantern: 200 x (0.15/1.1)^2 ≈ 3.7 W, so start at 2-3 W, not 60. check_shot's burnt-colour rule (> 0.02% of the frame and > 3% of a group) is the stop test.
inventory.already_automatic: The burnt check is automatic (check_shot); the starting wattages are not computed.
inventory.llm_tip: Work out a lamp's watts from distances before rendering; a lamp 15 cm from a seat needs only a few watts.

inventory.name: Light linking: a light reaches only its target
inventory.how_found: Lesson 120: the warm light meant for the notice lit the chair's top rail as brightly as the notice, and the lantern lit its own brass frame. Fix: Blender light linking (light_reaches). In Blender 5.2 a collection's light-linking entries don't name their object: pair them with the collection's objects in order.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: light_reaches(light, objects, only) for every accent light.
inventory.computable_from: the check file (subject, support) + light names
inventory.proposed_calculation: Every light named for a group in the check file ('lights': {'fire_glow_on_notice': ['notice', 'board']}) gets light_reaches automatically when the shot is dressed.
inventory.already_automatic: The helper exists (film kit only); it is called by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Give each accent light an explicit list of what it may reach.

inventory.name: Glowing things and flames
inventory.how_found: Lesson 89: the brazier's flames under the fire's lamp rendered as pale paper cones. Give glowing things a black base colour; better, leave flames out of the plate (painted, they read as cut-outs) and draw them live in the film. Workflows: tell the painter never to add flames, smoke, glows or new shadows round near props.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Emissive materials get a black base colour. Flames, smoke and glows are drawn live in the film, never in the plate or painting.
inventory.computable_from: material list
inventory.proposed_calculation: Lint: any material with emission > 0 and base colour luminance > 0.05 is set to black base automatically (glow_material in set_dressing). Plate scripts hide objects tagged 'flame' before rendering.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: set_dressing has glow_material/make_glow (film kit). Nothing enforces it.
inventory.llm_tip: Fire is a live effect, not a painted one.

inventory.name: No lamp on anything that shows the painting
inventory.how_found: Lesson 79: when stand-ins took some lamp and the background didn't, their edges showed as a brightness jump. Showing the painting exactly on both, with shadows on a see-through ground, matched them.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Projected surfaces show the painting at its painted brightness, with no stage lamp, shadow or haze. Model shadows fall on a see-through shadow-catcher ground.
inventory.computable_from: none
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already done in projected-set.js / painted-projection.js.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes (projected-set.js film kit only; painted-projection.js in the plugin).
inventory.llm_tip: Keep the painting's light; never add a lamp to projected surfaces.

inventory.name: Rooms by their own glow; dark rooms darken cut-outs
inventory.how_found: Lesson 81: each room shows its walls and cut-outs by their own light, scaled by a light level, instead of a dozen lamps: about 1.8 s a frame filming two at a time, and lights go out on a beat. Lesson 82: moonlight kept white paper edges glowing; scale colour as well as glow by the room's light.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Room light level scales both emissive and base colour of everything in the room.
inventory.computable_from: room light level per time
inventory.proposed_calculation: One setRoomLight(level) applies level to emissiveIntensity and multiplies base colour by (0.15 + 0.85 x level).
inventory.already_automatic: In the house sample only, not the shared kit.
inventory.llm_tip: Use self-lit rooms instead of many lamps; dim the cut-outs with the room.

inventory.name: Street needs its own light; solid back walls
inventory.how_found: Lesson 84: people just in front of lit rooms looked as if they were inside them; a lit pavement and a lamp pool separate the street. Lesson 42: light leaked out of the cottage's back windows onto the cypresses.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Give exteriors their own light pool on the ground; close the backs of lit buildings.
inventory.computable_from: still + group masks
inventory.proposed_calculation: Measure the pavement band's luminance in front of a lit room; warn if it is under 0.35 x the room's interior luminance.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Separate inside and outside with light on the ground.

inventory.name: Faces lit from the camera side (people check)
inventory.how_found: Workflows (log 34): check built figures lit by a lamp from the camera's side (figure_sheet.py); that light showed bald-looking heads (dark, shiny hair mirrored the lamps).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Check every figure in five lights (back, back lamp-lit high on the camera side, side, front, silhouette) at the distance they will stand (7 m).
inventory.computable_from: figure .glb files + planned distance
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a sheet. Add a number: per figure, the share of the head region above 0.9 luminance under the camera-side lamp; flag over 15% (shiny bald look).
inventory.already_automatic: figure_sheet.py exists (film kit only; figures/ is not in the plugin kit). Judged by eye.
inventory.llm_tip: Look at people from behind with a lamp on the camera side before using them.

inventory.name: Over-colourful faces and pieces
inventory.how_found: Decisions item 25 (user screenshot 1): one face was over-saturated next to the others. tone_piece.py measured it at about 1.7 times as colourful as the other people.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: tone_piece defaults: saturation 0.62, contrast 0.9, lift 0.03, the same on every layer of a piece (face, jaw, mouth).
inventory.computable_from: all cut-out pieces on a page
inventory.proposed_calculation: tone_piece --measure every piece. For any piece whose mean saturation is over 1.2 x the page's median, set saturation = median / piece's own value, and apply the same factor to all its layers.
inventory.already_automatic: Measure mode exists (plugin kit); the factor is chosen by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Measure saturation across all people on a page; match the loud one to the median.

inventory.name: Paper mouth: shape and loudness thresholds
inventory.how_found: Lesson 24: the first paper mouth looked like a black bar (wide rectangular jaw, tipped toward the camera), and it hung open because the loudness thresholds were too low. Fix: narrower jaw with rounded top corners, smaller drop, no tipping, opens only on louder syllables.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: make_mouth_track.py: closed at or below -25 dB, fully open at -11 dB, 40 ms slices, opens fast (0.8) and closes slower (0.55).
inventory.computable_from: the narration track for that page
inventory.proposed_calculation: Set the thresholds from the voice itself: QUIET = 40th percentile of voiced 40 ms slices (dB), LOUD = 90th percentile. Then the mouth is open past a fifth on about half the voiced frames for any narrator or level.
inventory.already_automatic: Fixed constants (plugin kit), tuned for Malina at -16 LUFS.
inventory.llm_tip: If the mouth hangs open or barely moves, the thresholds don't fit this voice; recompute them from percentiles.

inventory.name: Period figures in a present-day place
inventory.how_found: Lesson 52: 1920s out-of-work men stood in today's New Zealand street on page 10. Fix: a hundred-dot panel echoing page 2's 1915 panel.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every figure and prop has an era; it must match the page's era.
inventory.computable_from: cut list (if each piece carries 'era') + page plan (era per page)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Add 'era' to cut-list entries and page headers; lint any piece used on a page with a different era.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Tag every figure with its period and check it against the page.

inventory.name: No portraits of real people
inventory.how_found: Decisions (2026-10-11): drawn likenesses of real people are easy to get wrong and can mislead; real people appear as typed name cards.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Real people only as name cards; all drawn people invented.
inventory.computable_from: cut list / painting requests
inventory.proposed_calculation: Lint painting prompts and piece names against the research ledger's list of real people; any match stops the paid paint call.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Never paint a real person; type their name.

inventory.name: Dust and smoke placement
inventory.how_found: Lesson 25: the tank's landing dust burst behind the front crowd and was invisible; fix: it starts higher and in front of the tank, rising above the crowd's heads. Lesson 32: a falling word's dust burst in front of it; now it bursts behind.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Dust from a landing behind a crowd starts in front of the landing piece and above the crowd's top. Dust for words goes behind them.
inventory.computable_from: piece positions and sizes at the landing moment
inventory.proposed_calculation: Auto-place the emitter: if a nearer piece's box covers the landing point on screen, set the dust z just in front of the landing piece and its start height = the covering piece's top + 0.1 units. For words, z = word z - 0.1.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check effects in the actual frame; dust behind a crowd is invisible.

inventory.name: Effects belong to their page
inventory.how_found: Lesson 29: drawing moments out of order showed page 8's dust on pages 9, 10 and the last blank page; dust and smoke weren't put away with their page.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Make dust and smoke only through kit.effect(...), so they are hidden with their page.
inventory.computable_from: page source files
inventory.proposed_calculation: Lint: any 'new Dust(' / 'new Smoke(' / emitter outside kit.effect in a page file fails. Runtime: when a page hides, assert no visible object registered to it remains.
inventory.already_automatic: kit.effect exists (plugin kit); nothing stops direct use.
inventory.llm_tip: Always create effects through kit.effect.

inventory.name: Fading cut-outs snap off half way
inventory.how_found: Lesson 87: cut-outs are drawn only where at least half solid (alphaTest 0.5), and a piece first drawn solid keeps a recipe that ignores see-through. So the strike crowd stayed solid, then vanished in one frame. Fix in the house sample: setFading. The shared kit has the same fault.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Build fading pieces see-through once (transparent = true, needsUpdate) and lower alphaTest to about 0.02 while they fade.
inventory.computable_from: none (code fix)
inventory.proposed_calculation: In the kit's cut-out .set({opacity}): when opacity < 1, switch materials to transparent with alphaTest 0.02 and needsUpdate once; switch back at 1.
inventory.already_automatic: No. Only house-sample/page-1.js has setFading; cinema-kit.js (and the plugin kit) still snap.
inventory.llm_tip: Until the kit is fixed, copy setFading for any fading cut-out.

inventory.name: Page-turn ghosts; check page turns in one run
inventory.how_found: Lesson 51: one page's words showed on the next during page turns, but only when frames were drawn in sequence; a single test frame looked clean. Fix: the graphics layer is copied per page and reset. Workflows step 5: check page turns at each last word + 0.7 s.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Stills at every page's last word + 0.7 s, drawn in ONE run of the whole chapter.
inventory.computable_from: timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: A tool prints (or runs) the --stills list: for each page, t = last word end + 0.7, plus 0.3 and 1.2 s around it, all in one render-paper-film call.
inventory.already_automatic: The fix is automatic; the still list is typed by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Never check page turns with one still at a time.

inventory.name: Still times must be space-separated
inventory.how_found: Lesson 50: '43.2,47.5' was read as one broken number and the second still failed.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: --stills T1 T2 ... separated by spaces.
inventory.computable_from: none
inventory.proposed_calculation: Split each argument on commas too (rest.slice(1).flatMap(s => s.split(',')).map(Number)), and fail on NaN.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Separate still times with spaces.

inventory.name: Automatic still lists for checking pages
inventory.how_found: Workflows (paper step 7 and cinema step 4): check every entrance, word, mouth and page turn at full size. Built place step 6: four stills before filming (projector view, end of move, middle, weights view). Lesson 53: get the critique BEFORE filming.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Stills at every event, plus the four projected-set views per shot.
inventory.computable_from: page files (kit.at calls, stillShot moves) + timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: make_still_list PAGE: run the page in an 'events' mode that records every kit.at time and every move's from/to; output those times + 0.25 s, the move middles, the projector view (t at shot start), and the weights view at each move end. Then call render-paper-film --stills and a contact sheet.
inventory.already_automatic: No; times are picked by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Let the page's own events choose the stills; never pick times by eye.

inventory.name: Clearance and overlap checks at landing moments
inventory.how_found: Workflows 4b: room.clearance(thing) (negative = poking through) and boxesOverlap(a, b) at the moments things land or move. Lesson 65: corner checks missed a flat card's middle; now points are sampled across every face, and hidden parts are ignored. Decisions item 25: price tags clipping, coins through the ground.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Clearance >= 0 everywhere, sampled across faces; no overlaps of visible boxes.
inventory.computable_from: page poses at event times
inventory.proposed_calculation: Run clearance for every registered model against the room, and boxesOverlap for every pair, at every event time and at 0.1 s steps during moves. Print the worst negative value per pair.
inventory.already_automatic: The functions are in the kit; they are called by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Check clipping at landing moments and during moves, not only at rest.

inventory.name: Check the film in motion
inventory.how_found: Lesson 86: pieces popping in for one frame, things passing through floors and flat pale cards only showed in the moving film. A frame-to-frame difference measure finds them.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: find_jumps.py: a frame whose change is over 4 x the median of the 5 frames either side (and over a floor) is listed. Planned cuts are given so they aren't flagged.
inventory.computable_from: finished film + planned cut times (stillShot boundaries, page turns)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Pass the planned cut list automatically from the camera file (shot changes) and the timeline (page turns), so only unplanned jumps are reported.
inventory.already_automatic: find_jumps.py exists (plugin kit); planned cuts are typed by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Always run the jump finder on the filmed result before calling it done.

inventory.name: Critique before filming, from fresh critics
inventory.how_found: Lesson 53: seven critics and a skeptic found price boards cut off, pale labels, a key figure still counting, a dial sliding as if rates were cut, a broken transition, a party-coloured tie and a caricature adding a claim. Each cost a re-film; get the critique BEFORE filming. Decision 22: a second check confirmed the fixes and caught four new problems they caused. Lesson 125: a fix can make its own fault.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Critique the stills before filming. After fixes, a fresh check of every fix.
inventory.computable_from: stills + page plans
inventory.proposed_calculation: Make the filming script refuse to start unless a critique report newer than every page file exists (compare file times), and its findings are all marked fixed or accepted.
inventory.already_automatic: The workflows exist in the plugin; nothing stops filming without them.
inventory.llm_tip: Run critique-film before filming and check-fixes after fixing; re-check the fixed film.

inventory.name: Phone-size reading of details
inventory.how_found: Lesson 68: stone blocks beside gutter ends looked like little cameras, dark glass made reading glasses look like sunglasses, and figured wood looked like a contour map. A before-and-after judge in the real film frame caught all three.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Judge details at phone size in the real frame, before and after.
inventory.computable_from: stills
inventory.proposed_calculation: Produce phone-size copies (390 px wide) and 2x crops of each hero prop next to each other for critics automatically.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Ask 'what else could this read as on a phone?' for every new detail.

inventory.name: Check pictures against the history, not only words
inventory.how_found: Lesson 83: gold dropping into an empty vault said 'Britain gained gold', and a shrinking kitchen pay packet said 'every family's pay fell'. Lesson 94: critics caught snow-like blotches on the road on 1 May, coal heaps in a lockout when coal was scarce, sacks reading as clay jars, a sign cut to stray letters. Lesson 19: video samples drew Second World War tanks.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Give the facts checker the pictures and the narration at that moment.
inventory.computable_from: contact sheet at event times + timeline text
inventory.proposed_calculation: verify-facts gets a sheet of stills at each event time, each captioned with the sentence being said and the page's ledger ids.
inventory.already_automatic: No; the plugin's fact-checker reads text only.
inventory.llm_tip: A picture makes claims too; check what it implies.

inventory.name: Tool version and changing inputs during a check
inventory.how_found: Lesson 113: helpers checking a tool that was still changing saw six versions; now each report says which version made it. Lesson 124: the music was raised after one helper measured it; the skeptic noticed from file times.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each report carries the tool's hash (check_shot VERSION). Freeze tools while they are checked; note changes made during a check.
inventory.computable_from: file hashes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Every check tool hashes its inputs at start and end; if any changed, it prints which and marks the report stale.
inventory.already_automatic: Version hash in check_shot only.
inventory.llm_tip: Don't edit files while helpers are checking them.

inventory.name: Follow a tool's advice once to test it
inventory.how_found: Lesson 108: a helper who did exactly what the reports said found 'lower the lantern 0.47 m onto the seat' would have dropped it to the pavement (the chair had moved). Fixes are now worked out from the support's own top. Lesson 109: one downward line slipped between the seat's planks; now five spots, keep the highest.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Fixes measured from the support's top. Five rays under each prop, keep the highest. Rerun the checker tests (run-checker-tests.sh) before trusting a change.
inventory.computable_from: Blender scene
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed. Add an 'apply' mode to check_shot that makes the first fix in Blender and re-measures, proving the advice.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in shot_facts/check_shot (film kit). run-checker-tests.sh and notice_corner_test_scene.py are NOT in the plugin kit (it has only break_scene.py).
inventory.llm_tip: Test advice by following it once.

inventory.name: Edges by colour as well as brightness
inventory.how_found: Lesson 117: a rusty orange drum against a blue-grey road is about as bright as the road, so the checker took a correct picture for an out-of-date one. Now edges are found by colour too, and a picture is called out of date only when a prop lines up clearly better when slid.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Edges by colour and brightness; 'out of date' only on a clear improvement.
inventory.computable_from: picture + shot_facts outlines
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already in check_shot.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes (check_shot.py, film kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Don't trust brightness-only edge tests on coloured props.

inventory.name: Measure the model before using a helper's size
inventory.how_found: Lesson 116: a sooty lining for the drum was 0.365 m radius; the drum is 0.296 m, so it stuck out as a flat orange band and brought the drum's edge to 9 px from the notice.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Measure the model in Blender before using any size worked out from a picture.
inventory.computable_from: the .glb / Blender object bounds
inventory.proposed_calculation: Any part made to fit a model (lining, lid, cloth) takes its size from the model's measured bounds (inspect_glb.py or obj.dimensions), never from a typed number. Fail if a fitted part exceeds its host's bounds by more than 2%.
inventory.already_automatic: No; inspect_glb.py exists to measure.
inventory.llm_tip: Sizes from pictures are guesses; read the model's real dimensions.

inventory.name: Rays down hit whatever is above first
inventory.how_found: Lesson 88: the notice board's posts were placed by casting down from the sky; one landed on the board itself, and the other at the street's start because the board's new place hadn't been worked out yet.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Start the ray under the thing; update Blender's scene (view_layer.update()) before reading positions.
inventory.computable_from: Blender scene
inventory.proposed_calculation: place_prop always casts from just below the prop's own lowest point (start = low), after view_layer.update(), ignoring the prop's own objects.
inventory.already_automatic: In set_dressing.place_prop and shot_facts (film kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Cast placement rays from below the object, after updating the scene.

inventory.name: Second copy of a prop gets '.001' names
inventory.how_found: Lesson 119: importing a prop a second time gave its parts the first one's names with '.001', so the checker and the film page took the second gas lamp for the first.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Rename a second copy's parts at once.
inventory.computable_from: object names after import
inventory.proposed_calculation: place_prop(name=...) renames every imported child to '<instance>-<part>'; check_shot fails if a group's pattern matches objects from two imports.
inventory.already_automatic: Done by hand in one script.
inventory.llm_tip: Give every placed copy its own name prefix.

inventory.name: Model facing direction
inventory.how_found: Lesson 114: the chair model faced the other way from what its turn assumed: at 140 deg its back faced the fire and hid the lantern; -40 deg was right (a critic's find).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: CHAIR_TURN_DEGREES = -40 (back to the board, seat to the fire).
inventory.computable_from: prop library metadata (front axis) + target positions
inventory.proposed_calculation: Store each library prop's front axis in its metadata. turn = atan2(target - prop) - front_axis_angle. Check by measuring which side is nearer the target after placing.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Never assume a model's front; check it.

inventory.name: Coplanar surfaces flicker
inventory.how_found: Lesson 85: a room's ceiling sat exactly on the slab above and swapped colour in one frame at the start of a move.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Keep built surfaces a hair apart (about 0.01 units).
inventory.computable_from: model meshes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Scan each .glb for pairs of faces from different objects within 1e-4 of the same plane with overlapping area; report them and suggest a 0.01 offset.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Never put two surfaces exactly on top of each other.

inventory.name: Sheet must be bigger than what is drawn on it
inventory.how_found: Lesson 38: the oak's sheet was narrower than its crown, so leaves past the edge were missing (cut off in a straight line). Fix: wider sheet, tree shape measured from its height.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Sheet = drawing's bounding box + margin; shape sized from height.
inventory.computable_from: the drawn content's alpha bounds
inventory.proposed_calculation: Compute the drawing's alpha>0 bounding box and set the sheet to that plus a 4% margin; fail if any drawn pixel touches the sheet edge.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Size the sheet from what is drawn, not the other way round.

inventory.name: Baked corner shading settings
inventory.how_found: Lesson 61: Blender's default reach (10 units) darkened whole walls, and 2048 px at 48 samples took 12 minutes. Reach 0.6, 1024 px, 32 samples took 2 minutes and looks right. A part left out of the bake must not share a material with a baked part (the kerb turned dark brown).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: AO reach 0.6, 1024 px, 32 samples, margin 4. Unbaked parts get their own material.
inventory.computable_from: model size, on-screen size
inventory.proposed_calculation: Defaults are set. Add: texture size = next power of 2 above 2 x the model's largest on-screen size in px (cap 1024). Lint for unbaked parts sharing a material with baked ones.
inventory.already_automatic: Defaults in model_kit.py (plugin kit). The shared-material lint is missing.
inventory.llm_tip: Keep corner shading local; give skipped parts their own material.

inventory.name: Blender quality rules from the MCP guidance
inventory.how_found: Lesson 67: bevels shaded as hard facets (harden normals off), and cut brick walls had razor corners. Joining parts by material (232 to 19) made each works about 34,000 triangles. Sandbox refuses read_factory_settings (use read_homefile(use_empty=True, use_factory_startup=True)). Default renderer crashes without a graphics card (switch to Cycles before any render). Blender needs --online-mode for the add-on. Lesson 62: Blender adds '.glb' to any name not ending in it.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Harden normals on bevels; join by material; about 22,000-34,000 triangles per detailed building; output names end in .glb.
inventory.computable_from: the .blend / .glb
inventory.proposed_calculation: model_lint: count objects per material (>1 = join); bevel modifiers without harden_normals; triangle count against the budget; any export path not ending in .glb fails.
inventory.already_automatic: Notes in the plugin skill; no lint.
inventory.llm_tip: Run a model lint before export; the MCP's own guidance catches real faults.

inventory.name: Drawing time comes from surfaces, not shapes
inventory.how_found: Lesson 70: profile_frame.mjs showed the realistic materials of the works and town were most of page 3's 12 s a picture; matte halves it but looked flatter, so the time was accepted. Lesson 59: 22,000-triangle factory is still light enough.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Model pages 12-15 s a frame vs about 2.7 s for others; matte materials about halve it.
inventory.computable_from: profile_frame.mjs per page
inventory.proposed_calculation: Profile one frame of every page before filming and keep a table of seconds per frame; it feeds the filming-time estimate.
inventory.already_automatic: profile_frame.mjs exists (plugin copy is older).
inventory.llm_tip: Profile before filming; surfaces cost more than triangles.

inventory.name: Held shots are fast (draw the set once)
