inventory.how_found: Workflows (log 34): a page whose camera holds returns still: true from pose(t) and marks its moving things with kit.moving(...); the stage draws the painted set once and only the moving things each frame: 1.2 s a frame against 5.7 on the notice corner.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: still: true (or a key that changes when the set changes) on held shots.
inventory.computable_from: stillShot plan (between moves the camera is still)
inventory.proposed_calculation: stillShot returns still: true automatically for times outside its moves, with a key = shot name + state picture id, so page builders can't forget it.
inventory.already_automatic: Manual per page (film kit); not in the plugin's render tool.
inventory.llm_tip: Mark held moments still; it speeds filming about 5x.

inventory.name: Workers per machine
inventory.how_found: Lesson 34: two browsers on a 2-processor machine took as long as one. Workflows traps: on 4 processors two at once is about 17% faster (1.44 vs 1.68 s a frame); three not worth it.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: 1 worker on 2 processors; 2 on 4.
inventory.computable_from: nproc
inventory.proposed_calculation: WORKERS default = 1 if nproc <= 2 else 2.
inventory.already_automatic: No; WORKERS defaults to 2.
inventory.llm_tip: Check the processor count before choosing workers.

inventory.name: Fit filming into the 2-hour limit and survive restarts
inventory.how_found: Lesson 69: background jobs stop after 2 hours; chapter 2's 5-hour filming lost two pieces. Lesson 71: the machine restarted at 02:53 and lost about 30 minutes. Fix: FILM_FROM/FILM_TO stretches and 60-frame pieces (at most about 13 minutes lost on the slowest page).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Stretches that fit under 2 hours; PIECE_FRAMES 60; rerun carries on.
inventory.computable_from: render-paper-film --info (page frame ranges) + profiled seconds a frame per page + workers
inventory.proposed_calculation: plan_stretches: for pages in order, add frames until sum(frames x s_per_frame(page)) / workers reaches 6,600 s (2 h minus 10 min). Print the FILM_FROM/FILM_TO commands. PIECE_FRAMES = floor(900 s / s_per_frame of the slowest page) to cap loss at 15 minutes.
inventory.already_automatic: The pieces are automatic; the stretches are chosen by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Compute stretches from measured speed before starting a long film.

inventory.name: Watching and stopping filming jobs
inventory.how_found: Lesson 56: filming stopped silently for 90 minutes after a restart; the watcher only looked for 'finished'. Lessons 54 and 115: pkill -f with the script's name killed this session's own shell (exit 144), twice.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The watcher also stops when the script is no longer running. Stop jobs only by their own process number.
inventory.computable_from: PID file + log
inventory.proposed_calculation: The filming script writes out/SCENE.pid and a heartbeat line every minute; a 'status' command reports running, stalled (no heartbeat for 5 min) or stopped; a 'stop' command kills by the saved PIDs.
inventory.already_automatic: Documented, not built in.
inventory.llm_tip: Never use pkill -f; stop by the PID you saved.

inventory.name: Filming time estimates
inventory.how_found: Workflows: paper film about 0.85 s a frame (about 95 minutes for chapter 1). Cinema chapter 2: 35 chunks, two at a time, about 6 hours with detailed models. Lesson 60: Blender's renderer 35-90 s a frame (80-200 hours for a chapter), so Blender builds and the stage films. Plate in EEVEE about 10 minutes at 1536 x 2730. Rooms by glow 1.8 s.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Paper 0.85 s/frame; cinema 1.4-2.4 s; model pages 12-15 s; held shots 1.2 s; plate 10 min.
inventory.computable_from: timeline length x 30 fps + per-page profile
inventory.proposed_calculation: estimate = sum over pages(frames x profiled s/frame) / workers x 1.1, printed before filming along with the number of 2-hour stretches.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Tell the user the filming time before starting.

inventory.name: Lazy chapters need the newer renderer
inventory.how_found: Workflows (log 34): buildCinemaChapter({lazy: true}) builds only the pages a moment shows; film with PIECE_FRAMES=240. The film kit's render-paper-film.mjs calls window.prepareFrame for this; the plugin's copy does not.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: lazy: true + PIECE_FRAMES=240; renderer must call prepareFrame(t) before each frame.
inventory.evidence: Workflows.md:249-250; diff of film-kit vs plugin render-paper-film.mjs (prepareFrame lines)
inventory.computable_from: none
inventory.proposed_calculation: Sync the plugin's render-paper-film.mjs with the film kit's.
inventory.already_automatic: In the film kit only.
inventory.llm_tip: Use the film kit's renderer for long chapters.

inventory.name: Painting and service costs
inventory.how_found: Workflows and Decisions: Flux 3 big pictures about 10 US cents, small objects about 2.5; Flux 3 edit repaint about 10; Nano Banana Pro 15; MiniMax video 6 s samples about 90 cents for five; chapter 1: 47 pictures for about US$2.55 (planned 70 for US$5-8); chapter 2: 11 paintings about US$1.06; narration about US$1.10 a chapter (chapter 1 about 3,000 credits); Seedance draft at 480 px can be finished within 7 days without re-making; Flux takes at most ten pictures.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Budget per film = backgrounds x 0.10 + objects x 0.025 + repaints x 0.10 x 2 (main + behind) + Nano sketches x 0.15 + narration about 1.10, plus retries.
inventory.computable_from: shot plan (painting list) + script length
inventory.proposed_calculation: cost_estimate reads the shot plan's paintings by type and multiplies by the price table, adds 10% for retries (chapter 1 threw away 2 of 47; Flux strength reruns), and compares with the budget. Read prices live from the service where possible; the table is a fallback.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Show the cost estimate and get approval before any paid call.

inventory.name: Reuse one painting across pages
inventory.how_found: Decisions item 15: 47 pictures were painted, not 70: one painting can serve several pages, and words, cards, signs and boards are drawn by code.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Paint each recurring thing once; draw text things in code.
inventory.computable_from: page plan (prop list per page)
inventory.proposed_calculation: List every prop across pages, merge duplicates, and remove anything that is text (cards, signs, boards) from the paint list before costing.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Count unique things to paint, not pages.

inventory.name: Spending ledger and approval
inventory.how_found: Decision 40: a new budget of US$20 from log 34 covers narration and paintings; spending is reported in each log entry; paid steps were refused by the safety check and wait for approval. Decision 30: 'That's ok' was not a yes to spending. Decision 31: helpers were told US$3 by mistake.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every paid request recorded (00-requests.json); running total vs budget in every report; ask before spending.
inventory.computable_from: 00-requests.json files
inventory.proposed_calculation: spent = sum of recorded costs since the budget's start date; print remaining before any paid call and refuse when the call would exceed the budget.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Keep a running total and quote it; never treat a vague reply as approval to spend.

inventory.name: Contact sheets before cutting
inventory.how_found: Lesson 26: shells came out like rifle cartridges and a tank an odd shape; found on contact sheets before cutting. Lesson 19: video samples added flags and wrong-era tanks.

inventory.name: Masks over magenta, and remover repairs

Share of alpha between 0.1 and 0.9 inside the hull > 3% = see-through; lower the solid threshold. More than 3 separate pieces = print on a card.

inventory.name: Depth picture spread and blur
inventory.how_found: Lesson 41: the built-in distance drawing squeezed near and far into a few shades, and a strong blur turned leaves and hills to mush. Fix: custom depth spread evenly, gentler blur. Workflows: prepare_relief --blur 3.

inventory.name: Fitting shapes to AI paintings

Faces seen nearly edge-on must still wear the painting or they draw dark. Lesson 74: models wearing the projected painting brought back its glow and brushwork. Lesson 75: SAM 3D files have no normals. Lesson 76: fit the ground from around the base.

inventory.name: Stand-ins and near upright things

inventory.name: Program composition as a sketch only

inventory.name: Scrapbook engraving rules
inventory.how_found: Lessons 7-10 (scrapbook look, later set aside): square-grid shadows read as graph paper; three crossings read as chain-link; columns flat with a spiky top; a closed ring read as a drawn circle. Lesson 3: a sample was mislabelled 'two-ink'.

inventory.computable_from: judgement only
inventory.proposed_calculation: judgement only (this look is not in use)

inventory.name: Hero props need full detail
inventory.how_found: Lesson 55: the card house looked unfinished ('sparse in detail'); rebuilt as a detailed villa after two critics. Lesson 59: plain card boxes look poor beside paintings. Decision 34: no blank signs, book covers or plain boxes.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A hero prop needs as much detail as the paintings around it; every sign carries real lettering.
inventory.computable_from: model stats
inventory.proposed_calculation: Warn when a model covering more than 10% of the frame has under about 5,000 triangles or one material.
inventory.already_automatic: No.

inventory.name: Research and script honesty rules
inventory.how_found: Lesson 127: 'new money mostly gets more things made' was contradicted by the film's own Japan case; say rules exactly as broadly as their evidence. Lesson 128: 'banks', 'pay' and 'price' each meant several things. Lesson 131: a line about our Reserve Bank rested on Powell's speech. Lesson 4: facts only a blocked page could confirm stay out.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Scope each rule to its evidence; one word, one meaning; name whose words stand behind 'they say'; unconfirmed facts stay out.
inventory.computable_from: script + research ledger (claims with ids and sources)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Term table: list every repeated noun with each sentence it appears in, for a check that one word has one meaning both ways. Speaker check: for each 'X says/argues' line, the ledger id's source author or institution must match X.
inventory.already_automatic: No; the test-script-with-newcomers workflow covers it by judgement.
inventory.llm_tip: Say a rule only as broadly as its evidence, and check whose words you quote.

inventory.name: On-screen numbers recomputed from the ledger
inventory.how_found: Decision 21: checkers changed UP TO +25% and the hundred-dot panel (1915 was 0.95%), and kept x4 for oil ($2.90 to $11.65 is 4.02 times).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every on-screen number is backed by ledger raw values and rounds honestly.
inventory.computable_from: page files' numbers + ledger raw values
inventory.proposed_calculation: Each on-screen number names its ledger id; a tool recomputes ratios and percentages from the raw values and flags any rounding error above 5%.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Recompute every number on screen from its source.

inventory.name: Meaningful colours and symbols
inventory.how_found: Decision 22: a blue tie read as a party colour in an election period; the top-hatted caricature added a claim. Decision 24: the price tag climbs in arrows, not pounds, until the film reaches New Zealand. Lesson 19: placards and flags with real political meaning.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Charcoal, grey or ivory for invented officials; blank placards; no currency before the place is set.
inventory.computable_from: page files + cut list
inventory.proposed_calculation: Lint currency symbols against the page's place; measure the dominant hue of officials' clothing and flag party colours.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Neutral colours for officials, blank placards.

inventory.name: Newcomer test
inventory.how_found: Lesson 130: testers given the notes understood too much; the last newcomer tester saw only what a viewer hears and sees. Workflows log 33.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Testers get only the spoken words and the on-screen words, never the notes.
inventory.computable_from: script
inventory.proposed_calculation: The workflow strips notes automatically, passing only spoken text and on-screen text.
inventory.already_automatic: The workflow exists in the plugin.
inventory.llm_tip: Test on what the viewer sees, not your notes.

inventory.name: Public repository saving
inventory.how_found: Lesson 72: the repository is public, so the soundtrack stayed out and new files were searched for keys; when the safety check blocks, take out what it likely objects to and ask. Decisions 27 and 30: GitHub refuses files over 100 MB; batches under 400 MB; no audio or video; no other people's work.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Check visibility; scan for secrets; under 100 MB per file; batches under 400 MB; no audio or video.
inventory.computable_from: git status + file list
inventory.proposed_calculation: pre_push: read visibility (gh repo view); refuse audio and video extensions; regex-scan text files for keys and tokens; split into batches under 400 MB; list files over 100 MB.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check what you push and ask when the safety check blocks.

inventory.name: Rebuild from a fresh copy

inventory.final_value_or_rule: Pixel-compare stills from a fresh clone; check every path in the notes exists.
inventory.computable_from: notes + repository
inventory.proposed_calculation: path_check: extract backticked paths from docs and test that each exists.
inventory.already_automatic: No.

inventory.final_value_or_rule: One source of truth, synced by hash.
inventory.computable_from: file hashes of both trees
inventory.proposed_calculation: kit_sync: hash both trees; list files that differ or are missing in the plugin; copy on request.

inventory.name: Setup checks
inventory.how_found: Lesson 1: a skill pointed to a missing folder. Lesson 2: a helper needed a file the setup tool didn't copy. Lessons 43-44: the browser refused old headless mode; a module path needed an import map. Workflows: copy the soundtrack before mixing.

inventory.computable_from: file system
inventory.proposed_calculation: Setup also checks Blender, the soundtrack file and every path named in the skills.

inventory.name: Project file conventions
inventory.how_found: Workflows traps: never reuse a log number; never 'final' or 'v2' in names; the timing file is tool-made. Lesson 35: a ledger filed shells as a figure by its number prefix.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Files start with their log number; no 'final' or 'v2'; generated files aren't edited by hand; filing uses an explicit kind field.
inventory.computable_from: file names + project story log
inventory.proposed_calculation: Lint names; get the next log number from the story; stamp generated files with a hash and warn if edited.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Follow the naming rules; never edit generated timing files.

inventory.name: Music level under the voice (ducking depth)
inventory.how_found: Three rounds over three logs, measured by hand. Log 04: the first mix dipped the music 31 dB under the voice, so it nearly vanished; retuned to about 18 dB. Log 07: measured page by page, 18 to 21 dB under while she speaks and about 12 dB in pauses. Log 10: the user asked for the music 'slightly' louder, so it was raised 3 dB (music_level_db -14 to -11), back to about 18 dB under.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Music sits about 18 dB (plus or minus 1) under Malina while she speaks and about 12 dB under in pauses. Current constants: music_level_db=-11, sidechaincompress threshold 0.08, ratio 2.5, attack 30 ms, release 1100 ms, makeup 1; the music gets a -4 dB EQ cut at 2500 Hz (Q 1.2); music fades in over 0.8 s and out over 4 s.
inventory.computable_from: the soundtrack file, the levelled narration track, the timeline's word times
inventory.proposed_calculation: Render the ducked-music stem and the voice stem separately. Using the word times, measure the music's short-term LUFS inside speech windows and inside pauses of 0.5 s or more. Change music_level_db by (measured speech gap - 18 dB) and repeat until within 1 dB (2 or 3 ffmpeg passes). Report the pause gap and flag it outside 10 to 14 dB. If the user asks for 'slightly louder', move the target gap by 3 dB.
inventory.already_automatic: No. The -11 dB is a hand-set constant (its comment says 'was 14 until you asked for it slightly louder'), and the 18 and 12 dB gaps were measured by hand. The mix scripts are in the plugin kit (kit/narration-tools/mix_narration_over_music.sh) but have no measuring loop.
inventory.llm_tip: Never assume a fixed music gain fits another soundtrack. Measure the gap under speech and aim for about 18 dB. 'Slightly louder' means about 3 dB.

inventory.name: Mix length after the loudness step (sample-rate trap)
inventory.how_found: Log 04: the mix came out 3 seconds short. The cause was ffmpeg's loudnorm, which silently switches the audio to 192,000 samples a second.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Add aresample=48000 after every loudnorm. The output must be as long as the narration.
inventory.computable_from: the narration file and the finished mix
inventory.proposed_calculation: After every mix, assert |duration(mix) - duration(narration)| < 1/30 s, else stop with an error.
inventory.already_automatic: The resample fix is in both mix scripts (plugin kit). No length check exists.
inventory.llm_tip: After any ffmpeg loudness filter, resample to 48 kHz and compare the output length with the input.

inventory.name: Peak limiter ceiling and true peak of the sent copy
inventory.how_found: Log 07: levelling pushed the voice's peaks past full scale, so a limiter was added holding them at -1.6 dB. Log 08 measured -1.5 dB after encoding; later films measured -1.7 and -1.6.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: alimiter limit=0.84 (about -1.5 dBFS), attack 5 ms, release 60 ms, latency=1. The true peak of the encoded sendable copy stays below -1 dBTP (measured -1.5 to -1.8).
inventory.evidence: story L385-386 (log 07), L397-398 and L405-406 (log 08), L477 (log 13), L622 (log 19); mix_narration_over_music.sh line 33
inventory.computable_from: the encoded film
inventory.proposed_calculation: After finish_film.sh, run ebur128=peak=true on the sendable copy. If the true peak is above -1.0 dBTP, lower the limiter by (peak + 1.2 dB) and re-encode only the sound.
inventory.already_automatic: The limiter is a fixed constant in the plugin kit. The peak is measured by hand (film-and-finish SKILL.md step 3).
inventory.llm_tip: Measure true peak on the final AAC copy, not on the WAV. Encoding raises peaks by a few tenths of a dB.

inventory.name: Sound delay from the limiter's look-ahead
inventory.how_found: Log 08 compared the film's sound with the mix and found it 5 ms late at every page (the limiter's look-ahead). Fixed, and measured 0.00 ms on every film since.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: alimiter latency=1 (compensated). check_sound_alignment.py must read 0.00 ms, or a few ms, at the first word of every page.
inventory.evidence: story L396-397, L405 (log 08), L478 (log 13), L621 (log 19); narration-tools/check_sound_alignment.py header
inventory.computable_from: the film, the mix and the timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: This is already a calculation: cross-correlate 0.5 s of the mix at each page's first word with the film's sound. Make finish_film.sh run it automatically and fail above 10 ms.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes: check_sound_alignment.py is in the plugin kit, but it is run by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Run the alignment check on every sendable copy. More than about 10 ms means some filter added delay.

inventory.name: Loudness targets: voice -16 LUFS per page, whole mix -15 LUFS
inventory.how_found: Settled in logs 07 and 08, then measured again in logs 13, 19 and 20 (always -15.0 or -15.1 LUFS). Each page is levelled to the same loudness so no page sounds louder than the next.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each page's voice is set to -16 LUFS by a plain volume change. The whole narrated mix is -15 LUFS integrated. The soundtrack itself is about -13 LUFS, so it must always be turned down.
inventory.evidence: story L383-384, L397-398, L477, L559, L622, L680, Traps L1412; film-kit/narration-tools/assemble_chapter_narration.py line 27 (VOICE_LOUDNESS=-16); mix_narration_over_music.sh line 18 (target -15)
inventory.computable_from: the recordings
inventory.proposed_calculation: Keep measure-then-gain as now. Also print each page's applied gain and flag any page needing more than 4 dB either way (a sign of a different delivery).
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, in the plugin kit (assemble_chapter_narration.py and mix_narration_over_music.sh).
inventory.llm_tip: Use -15 LUFS for narrated films. Never re-level the narration a second time inside the mix.

inventory.name: Loudness of music-only clips
inventory.how_found: Log 27 (the house) was at -17 LUFS and log 29 at -17.7. In log 32 a helper found -17.7 faint on a phone speaker, so it was raised to -14 (measured -13.7).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak at most -1 dB, for clips with music and no narration.
inventory.evidence: story L905 (log 27), L978 (log 29), L1234 and L1242 (log 32); paper-film/tools/add_music_bed.sh default LOUDNESS=-14
inventory.computable_from: rule (a constant)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Keep -14 as the default and check afterwards with ebur128.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes: add_music_bed.sh defaults to -14 (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Music-only clips need to be about 1 dB louder than narrated mixes (-14 against -15 LUFS) or they sound faint on a phone.

inventory.name: Which stretch of the soundtrack to use, and its fades
inventory.how_found: Log 27: the music came in at once, so a 2-second fade-in was added. Log 32: a quiet stretch starting at 3 min 36 s was chosen by its loudness, not by ear (nobody can listen here).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The notice corner uses the music from 216 s. Fades: in 0.8 s (2 s on the house), out 1.5 s.
inventory.evidence: story L900-902 (log 27), L1223-1224 and L1251-1252 (log 32); add_music_bed.sh defaults FADE_IN=0.8, FADE_OUT=1.5
inventory.computable_from: the soundtrack file, the clip's length and the mood wanted (quiet or tense)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Compute 3-second short-term loudness along the soundtrack. Pick the window of the clip's length whose loudness is within 2 LU of the mood's target and varies least. Snap its start to the nearest detected onset so it doesn't start mid-note. Fade in 0.8 s when it starts on an onset, otherwise 2 s.
inventory.already_automatic: No. START is chosen by hand and passed to add_music_bed.sh.
inventory.llm_tip: Pick the music stretch by measurement and say so, since you can't listen. Never start music at full level.

inventory.name: Pause between pages, and music before the first word
inventory.how_found: Log 07 laid the pages end to end with pauses of 1.1 to 1.7 s, chosen gap by gap: longer where the page turn has more to do.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Default 1.4 s (estimate_timeline uses 1.5). Per-gap range 1.1 to 1.7 s, for example --pauses 1.7,1.4,1.1,1.5,1.5,1.3,1.5,1.4,1.6. The first word comes 1.08 s into the music. The estimate adds a 4.0 s tail after the last word.
inventory.evidence: story L382 (log 07); assemble_chapter_narration.py lines 9-12, 27-31; estimate_timeline.py lines 18-19 and --default-pause
inventory.computable_from: the page files (what the outgoing page does on its turn) and the join kind and length
inventory.proposed_calculation: pause = clamp(join.after + join.length + settle + 0.2 s × pieces folding away first, 1.1, 1.7). The defaults are join.after 0.3 s, a 0.85 s peel and 0.3 s to settle (about 1.45 s). For a held guess, use 4.0 s instead (see the guess item).
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: a default of 1.4 s and a hand-typed --pauses list. Nothing reads the join lengths from the page files.
inventory.llm_tip: Pauses are not cosmetic: a page turn needs about 1.2 s. Never set a gap below 1.1 s.

inventory.name: First word placed late by ElevenLabs
inventory.how_found: Log 10 found that ElevenLabs' transcript put each page's first word up to 0.32 s after the voice really starts. Nine pages were corrected.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The first word's start is moved back to where the voice really begins in the recording.
inventory.computable_from: the recording and its transcript
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a calculation: detect where the voice's energy starts before the first word.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, in extract_word_times.py (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Always get word times through extract_word_times.py. Never use ElevenLabs' raw first-word time.

inventory.name: Bracketed delivery instructions are not spoken
inventory.how_found: Log 07 checked that no cue was read aloud (each lasts under a fifth of a second and sits in a pause). Log 09: the timing tool counted the words of the long accent instruction as spoken; fixed so everything in brackets counts as the instruction.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Everything in [brackets] is an instruction, not speech. A bracket word that shows up in the transcript, or lasts more than about 0.2 s, means it was read aloud.
inventory.computable_from: the narration file and the transcript
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each page, compare the transcript's words with the script text minus the brackets. Any bracket word or extra word in the transcript means that page is re-recorded.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: extract_word_times.py skips bracketed text (plugin kit). Nothing checks for instructions read aloud.
inventory.llm_tip: Use only the one accent instruction per page, and check the transcript doesn't contain it.

inventory.name: A steady voice across pages (accent and pitch)
inventory.how_found: Log 09 measured the pages at very different pitches (page 3 about 5 semitones above page 4), caused by mixed mood cues and capitals. The narration was rewritten so the same New Zealand accent instruction opens every page, with no other cues and no capitals: the gap fell from 5.3 to 1.8 semitones. Log 19 measured 2.2 semitones (chapter 1: 3.0).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: One identical accent instruction at the start of every page; no mood cues, no capitals; Mattei written in English sounds. Aim for a spread of typical pitch across pages of about 2.2 semitones or less. Flag words 5 or more semitones above the page's typical pitch, or 6 dB or more louder.
inventory.computable_from: the recordings and word times
inventory.proposed_calculation: After recording, run compare_voice_steadiness on every page and take the median typical pitch m. Flag pages more than 1.5 semitones from m, and words above the raised-voice or loud-word limits. Propose re-recording only the flagged pages, with their credit cost.
inventory.already_automatic: The tools are in the plugin kit but run by hand, with no pass/fail limit on the spread.
inventory.llm_tip: Fix voice consistency in the script (the same instruction every page, no capitals, no mood tags), not with retakes.

inventory.name: Speaking speed, and estimating the length before recording
inventory.how_found: Log 33 measured Malina at 164 words a minute against the 140 planned, and the three fastest pages carried the most new ideas. Log 34 built a timeline estimator from word lengths and pauses measured on her real recording: tested on the old recording it gave 252 s against the real 251.7 s.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Plan at about 160 words a minute for this voice. Each word lasts base + per_letter × letters + an extra for its ending (full stop, comma, question mark, '...'); gaps are the median; everything is scaled so the measured recording comes out at its real length.
inventory.evidence: story L349 (word list), L1270-1271 (log 33), L1317, L1356-1358 (log 34); film-kit/narration-tools/estimate_timeline.py
inventory.computable_from: the narration file plus any earlier word-times file of the same voice
inventory.proposed_calculation: Use estimate_timeline.py as it is. Also print each page's words a minute and flag pages above 150, or with more than 3 new terms per 30 s.
inventory.already_automatic: estimate_timeline.py is in the film kit but NOT in the plugin kit (plugins/explainer-film/kit/narration-tools lacks it).
inventory.llm_tip: Build and check every page on the estimated timeline before paying for the voice. Pages ask for words, not seconds, so they retime themselves once the real recording exists.

inventory.name: Recording cost (ElevenLabs)
inventory.how_found: Logs 04, 07, 19 and 33, worked out from bills: about 1 credit per letter (2,950 credits for pages 2 to 10; 4,300 credits for about 75 US cents; 6,300 credits planned for about US$1.10). Transcripts were free, and later re-recordings showed 0 credits charged.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Credits are about the number of letters of page text sent, including the accent instruction. US$ is about credits × 0.000175.
inventory.computable_from: the narration JSON
inventory.proposed_calculation: credits = sum of len(page text including the instruction); cost = credits × 0.175 / 1000 USD. Print both before asking the user.
inventory.already_automatic: No tool. The rule of thumb is prose in the plugin skills (make-explainer-film SKILL.md line 43, record-narration SKILL.md line 17).
inventory.llm_tip: State the credits and dollars and get a clear yes before any ElevenLabs call. Download each recording at once: the links expire after 2 hours.

inventory.name: Picture and model costs (fal), and the spend ledger
inventory.how_found: Learnt from bills, logs 10 to 34. Log 12 planned 70 pictures for about US$5 (up to US$8); log 13 actually painted 47 for US$2.55, with 2 failures (about 4%). Log 26 had told helpers about US$3 was left when about US$8.70 was; corrected.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: 2k painting about 10 US cents; 1k about 2.5 cents; cut-out mask about 0.2 cents; depth map a fraction of a cent; Flux 3 edit repaint about 10 cents (may also charge for the pictures sent: 20 to 45 cents for two); Nano Banana Pro about 15 cents a picture; Seedance 2.5 10-second draft about US$2.06 (480 px wide, finishable at full size within 7 days); MiniMax 6-second video about 18 cents; SAM 3D about 2 cents; Tripo 20 to 40 cents (never its free plan); World Labs about US$1.26 a world with a US$5 minimum. Allowances: 'up to $10' from chapter 2's start, then a new US$20 from log 34.
inventory.computable_from: the shot plan (plates to paint, masks, edits, videos) and a price table
inventory.proposed_calculation: Projected cost = sum over kinds of count × unit price × 1.25 (re-paint margin). Keep a ledger summed from fal's request history, with spend counted from the date the current allowance began. Refuse to plan beyond what is left.
inventory.already_automatic: No. Prices are prose in the plugin skills (paint-and-cut SKILL.md line 20, make-explainer-film SKILL.md line 44, make-3d-models SKILL.md lines 129, 140).
inventory.llm_tip: Keep a running spend ledger against the user's current allowance. Recompute what is left from the allowance's start date, never from memory.

inventory.name: Script measures that keep newcomers following
inventory.how_found: Log 33 audit of the recorded chapter 2: 164 words a minute; the main rule said only once, 3 minutes in, as one 28-word sentence; 8 cases changing direction in time 8 times; 48 words a newcomer might not know; 'price' used for six different things; '...' pauses under a second. Three rounds, 22 helpers, about 3 h 20 min.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Sentences of about 9 words. The main rule said twice in identical words. 4 real cases in time order. About 28 spoken figures (down from 37). Every unfamiliar word explained or cut. The stakes within the first 30 seconds. About 7.25 minutes for 1,021 words.
inventory.computable_from: the script text, the research ledger and a common-word list
inventory.proposed_calculation: A script linter: mean words per sentence (flag above 12, or any sentence above 20); spoken figures per estimated minute (flag above 4); years mentioned in order, counting reversals (flag above 1); words outside the 5,000 most common English words with no explanation within 2 sentences; the rule sentence present exactly twice, verbatim; a stake in the first 30 estimated seconds.
inventory.already_automatic: No. The test-script-with-newcomers workflow (plugin 1.2.0) relies on helpers' judgement only.
inventory.llm_tip: Run cheap counts before the helper testers. They catch most 'too fast, too many terms' problems.

inventory.name: Hold for a guess and thinking pauses
inventory.how_found: Log 33: each '...' pause gave under a second, no time to think. The new script holds about 4 s after 'Have a guess'.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: At least 4 s held after a question to the viewer. A '...' pause of at least 1 s.
inventory.computable_from: the script's punctuation and the timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: In estimate_timeline and assemble, add 4.0 s automatically after any page ending with a viewer question. In the real recording, check that the gap after '...' is at least 1.0 s; if not, add silence.
inventory.already_automatic: Manual: estimate_timeline.py --pause-after.
inventory.llm_tip: A guess needs about 4 seconds of calm picture. Say it in the page file, not by stretching narration.

inventory.name: Caption line length and splitting
inventory.how_found: Log 13: captions remade from the new word times; 'Clara E. Mattei' had been split at the 'E.'.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: At most 42 letters a caption, split at a comma near the middle or else the middle word, never after a single initial. Chapter 1 had 121 lines.
inventory.computable_from: the timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a calculation. The limit could instead come from the caption font: floor(usable width / average letter width).
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, make_captions.py (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Always make captions from the same timeline the film was made from.

inventory.name: Planned rests and frozen stretches
inventory.how_found: Log 08: the drawing skill's quality gate flagged 18 one-second stretches where only a thin red-pen line or small typing moved, because it looks at a quarter-size picture. A typing pause was declared as a rest.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A planned rest lasts at most 1.7 s (2.5 s on the end card). Measure motion at full size.
inventory.computable_from: the filmed frames and the page files' declared rests
inventory.proposed_calculation: Mean frame-to-frame change per second at full resolution. Any stretch over 1.7 s below a small floor (about 0.2 levels) that is not a declared rest or held shot is flagged.
inventory.already_automatic: Only the anidoodle quality gate (scrapbook look). Nothing in the plugin kit for the cinema look: find_jumps.py looks for jumps, not freezes.
inventory.llm_tip: Declare rests and held shots in the page file. A check that shrinks frames will miss thin moving lines.

inventory.name: Page turn timing
inventory.how_found: Log 11: a page turn that swung like a door left white strips, so it became a corner peel with pieces folding away first. Log 13: the turn starts 0.3 s after the page's last word.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: TURN_AFTER_LAST_WORD 0.30 s. Cinema DEFAULT_JOIN is a peel 0.3 s after the last word, lasting 0.85 s. Pieces fold away first.
inventory.evidence: story L449-450 (log 11), L469-470 (log 13); paper-film/scenes/paper-chapter.js line 22; cinema-chapter.js line 15
inventory.computable_from: the timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already automatic. Add a check that each join ends at least 0.1 s before the next page's first word.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, in both engines (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Don't hand-time page turns. Set a join kind only where a page needs a dissolve or a dip.

inventory.name: A cue word spoken twice on a page
inventory.how_found: Log 08: marks tied to the wrong word where a word is spoken twice. Log 13: 'war', 'get' and 'prices' were looked up by their first time.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Ask for a word together with its occurrence number.
inventory.evidence: story L392-393 (log 08), L471 (log 13); paper-film/scenes/cinema-kit.js line 60 (occurrence n)
inventory.computable_from: the page text and the words each page file asks for
inventory.proposed_calculation: When a page is built, list every requested word that occurs more than once on that page without an explicit occurrence, with all its times, as a warning.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: the occurrence argument exists, but nothing warns when it is missing.
inventory.llm_tip: When a cue word appears twice in a page's narration, always pass its occurrence.

inventory.name: Words on screen in step with cuts, moves and narration
inventory.how_found: Log 19: one page's words showed on the next during a page turn. Log 27: the 1925 title lingered through the move down. Log 32: the end titles arrived with a small pop at 8.9 s (the move stops by 8.4 s). Log 34 round 4: words end exactly on each cut, and every word on screen matches the narration.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each title ends at or before its shot's cut and clears as the camera moves. No title from page N shows after its turn starts. On a held end frame, titles fade in after the camera has stopped.
inventory.evidence: story L581-582 (log 19), L900-902 (log 27), L1247-1248 (log 32), L1378-1380 (log 34); L1324-1325 (log 33: picture notes putting years and prices on screen that Malina never says)
inventory.computable_from: the page files (title start and end), shot cut times, camera move times and the narration text
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each 2D title: assert end ≤ next cut; on held shots, start ≥ the last move's end + 0.3 s; fade-in at least 0.3 s (9 frames). Fuzzy-match the title's text to the narration within 3 s of its start; numbers must equal spoken numbers.
inventory.already_automatic: Not known to be a tool. Checked by helpers in round 4.
inventory.llm_tip: Every on-screen word should be something Malina says within a few seconds. Never show a year or price she doesn't say.

inventory.name: Numbers on screen held still and true to the ledger
inventory.how_found: Log 19: page 10's 5.6% never held still. The fact recheck changed UP TO +25%, LOWEST SINCE 1986 and the last of the hundred dots (0.95%), and kept ×4 (4.02 times) and 'about ½% a year' with reasons.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A number stops moving long enough to read. Shown figures stay within rounding of the ledger value and keep its qualifiers ('up to', 'about').
inventory.computable_from: the page files and the research ledger
inventory.proposed_calculation: Each on-screen number must hold still for at least 0.5 s + 0.15 s per character (about 1.5 s for '5.6%'). Map it to a ledger id; |shown - ledger| must be at most half its last shown digit. Flag a missing qualifier.
inventory.already_automatic: No. The verify-facts workflow relies on judgement.
inventory.llm_tip: Put the ledger id next to every on-screen figure in the page file.

inventory.name: Camera rule: still unless essential, at most three moves a shot
inventory.how_found: The user's rule (log 20). Before it, 9 shots broke it: page 1 crept for 20 seconds; pages 3 and 8 never held still. The engine now refuses a fourth move, and a checker measures every shot in about 10 seconds. After: 21 shots, 0 problems; page 6 was split into two shots.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: At most 3 named moves a shot (zoom in or out, pan left, right, up or down, move up or down). Audit limits: the camera counts as moving above 0.6 degrees/s of turn, 1.2%/s of travel (as a share of its distance to the subject) or 1.2%/s of lens change. Moves less than 0.35 s apart count as one. A jump of more than 0.25 of the distance, or a turn of more than 8 degrees, is a cut.
inventory.evidence: story L633-637, L681-682 (log 20); film-kit/paper-film/scenes/cinema-kit.js line 356; paper-film/tools/camera_audit.py lines 13-26
inventory.computable_from: the page files' stillShot moves
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already automatic. Run camera_audit automatically after every page build.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes: the cinema-kit stillShot refusal and camera_audit.py, both in the plugin kit (the plugin's cinema-kit.js is an older copy).
inventory.llm_tip: Plan each shot as a stillShot with named moves. If you need a fourth move, cut to a new shot.

inventory.name: Move without turning (slide toward the subject)
inventory.how_found: Log 29's clip turned while it moved. Both rounds of critics in log 30 found the turn slid where the lines meet toward the colliery door, and slid the pithead out of frame. Seedance's draft showed the better move: one approach, barely turning, a long slowdown. Log 32: a 1.5 m slide that stops by 8.4 s of 13; helpers confirmed the camera never turns.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Only the position changes during a move, never the direction. Where the lines meet drifts no more than 0.02 of the frame's width between the first, middle and last frames. Ease in and out (smoother step) with a long slowdown, then hold.
inventory.evidence: story L1022-1025 (log 30), L1056-1060 (log 30), L1221-1226 (log 32); film-kit/07 Composing a shot.md rule 11 (lines 125-134)
inventory.computable_from: the camera path (position and target keys)
inventory.proposed_calculation: For every move, take the rotation between the first, middle and last frames. Drift = tan(change of facing angle) / (2 tan(hfov/2)) in frame widths; flag above 0.02. Also check that position and target move by the same vector.
inventory.already_automatic: No. check_shot.py states it does not check rule 11; camera_audit names turns but doesn't apply this limit.
inventory.llm_tip: Move the camera and its target together by the same vector. Never animate the target alone during a slide.

inventory.name: Painted rooms tear when the camera rises during a pan
inventory.how_found: Log 26 found that the petrol station's tear in chapter 2 came from the camera rising during a 'pan down'. Pure turns and pure zooms never tear a painted room. Logs 22 to 24 saw the same tearing on pushes and side steps.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: In a painting with depth, a pan is a pure turn about the camera's own centre and a zoom is a lens change. Camera travel is kept to a minimum.
inventory.computable_from: the page file's camera path and the painted room's depth range
inventory.proposed_calculation: In painted-room scenes, measure the camera's travel during each move. Parallax shift in pixels = f_px × travel × (1/z_near - 1/z_far); flag above about 8 px (calibrate on the station test).
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: In a painted room, pan by turning and push by zooming. Keep camera travel for real 3D sets.

inventory.name: How far the camera may go on a painted-over 3D set (plate coverage)
inventory.how_found: Log 29: turning showed a strip of unpainted houses at the frame's edge, because the plate was only a little wider than the frame; the push was made mostly a lens zoom. In the weights view, blue at a frame edge means the camera has left the painting.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every frame's view stays inside the plate's view, allowing a 0.03 fade band. The notice corner's plate was drawn from where the slide starts and is bigger than the frame.
inventory.evidence: story L948-949 (log 29), L323 (word list), L1203-1205 (log 32); paper-film/scenes/projected-set.js frameEdge 0.03 (line 521)
inventory.computable_from: the plate (projector) camera, the shot's camera path and the set's depth
inventory.proposed_calculation: For sample frames along the move, cast rays through the frame's corners and edge midpoints onto the set and project the hit points into the projector. Needed overscan = the largest normalised position found, plus 0.03. Draw the plate at that lens, or reject the move.
inventory.already_automatic: No. The weights view (showWeights in projected-set.js) is a manual debug view, in the film kit only.
inventory.llm_tip: Draw the plate from the start of the slide, wide enough for the whole move, and check the weights view for blue at the edges.

inventory.name: Matching the camera of a picture the user liked
inventory.how_found: Log 31: the user said 'the lines don't converge the same way'. The camera was matched by landmarks (winding-wheel hubs, chimney top, gate, roofline, kerbs): ours stood 0.42 m too high and was turned 1 degree too little. The shot checker then gave the same fix by itself: 'Lower 0.42 m; move 0.29 m left; turn 1.0 degrees left'.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Matched, the lines meet at 0.684 across, 0.440 down, against 0.706, 0.424 in the reference. The final camera is within 0.02 m of the best match.
inventory.computable_from: the reference picture's landmarks (in pixels) and the same landmarks in Blender metres
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a calculation: check_shot.py fits the camera to camera_match landmarks and states the fix in metres and degrees.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, check_shot.py. The plugin's copy is older (1,807 against 1,838 lines).
inventory.llm_tip: When the user points to a picture they like, match its camera by landmarks before moving any prop.

inventory.name: Aiming the street at the subject, and clearing the button strip by sliding
inventory.how_found: Logs 30 and 31: where the lines meet must sit at the subject's edge. A turn moves that point and every prop together; a slide moves near props more. The notice in the button strip was fixed by sliding the camera 0.14 m right without turning (the checker's own fix; the critics worked out 0.12 m by hand).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Turn first to place where the lines meet (1 degree is about 0.027 of the frame's width at a 60-degree vertical lens), then slide to bring the subject's edge to it.
inventory.evidence: story L1126-1128 (log 31), L1056-1060 (log 30); 07 Composing a shot.md rule 1 (lines 52-61)
inventory.computable_from: the camera's lens and the subject's depth
inventory.proposed_calculation: Turn = atan((x_target - x_meet) × 2 tan(hfov/2)). Slide in metres = shift on screen (as a share of width) × 2 × depth × tan(hfov/2).
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, inside check_shot.py's fixes (plugin copy older).
inventory.llm_tip: Never close a composition gap by turning: a turn moves everything together.

inventory.name: Camera height and level
inventory.how_found: Log 30: the two rounds of critics disagreed on the camera's height (1.5 or 1.85 m); a picture drawn in Blender settled it. Seedance's hip-height camera looked wrong. Log 31: the checker had the camera's lean sign wrong (fixed).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Standing eye height, 1.5 to 1.9 m above the pavement under the camera. In Blender, X rotation exactly 90 and Y rotation 0 (level, no lean). High enough to see into the drum and onto the chair's seat.
inventory.evidence: story L1026-1027, L1073-1075 (log 30), L1116 (log 31); check_shot.py eye_height (docstring line 24); 07 rule 2
inventory.computable_from: the camera and the ground height
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already checked. Add the least height that shows a top surface as an oval: h ≥ z_top + d × tan(10 degrees).
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, check_shot camera checks (plugin kit, older copy).
inventory.llm_tip: Stand the camera where a person would stand on the pavement, never in the middle of an empty road.

inventory.name: Camera distance from figures (no faces for the painter) against filling the frame
inventory.how_found: Log 34 plan: the waiting workers are seen from behind and never nearer than about 6 m, so the painter has no faces to paint. Round 4's critic found the story small and high over bare paving, so round 5 moves the cameras about 3 m nearer.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Figures about 6 m or more away and seen from behind. Cameras about 3 m nearer than in round 4.
inventory.computable_from: the figures' positions, the camera and the lens
inventory.proposed_calculation: Head height on screen = 0.23 m × f_px / distance, where f_px = (H/2) / tan(vfov/2). Keep it under a limit set by the people test (about 40 px is a guess to calibrate) for figures facing the camera. Then pick the nearest camera that meets both that limit and story_reaches_down ≥ 0.70.
inventory.already_automatic: No (story_reaches_down exists in the film kit's checker only).
inventory.llm_tip: Choose the camera's distance from two numbers together: how big faces get (keep small) and how far down the frame the story reaches (at least 0.70).

inventory.name: Fill the bottom of the tall frame
inventory.how_found: Log 20 research on miniatures and vertical video: low, close cameras; subjects stacked in depth; chimneys and sky in the top third; barrels, crates and a cart in the near corners. Log 26 review: in about 70% of frames the bottom fifth was more than 30% darker than the middle, which came from the painting prompts' rule 'the lower quarter of the picture is the empty floor'. Log 34 round 4: bare paving in the bottom third.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Some story prop or the subject reaches at least 0.70 down the frame (the notice corner's drum, chair and pail fill 0.45 to 0.8 down). The bottom fifth is not more than 30% darker than the middle. Never tell a painter to leave the lower quarter empty.
inventory.evidence: story L643-649 (log 20), L829-831 and L847-848 (log 26), L1382-1383 (log 34); 07 Composing a shot.md lines 214-219
inventory.computable_from: rendered frames and the shot facts
inventory.proposed_calculation: Per frame, compare mean brightness of the bottom 20% with rows 40 to 60%; flag below 0.7. Use check_shot story_reaches_down 0.70; if it fails, lower the camera or move it nearer until the nearest story prop's lowest point lands at 0.70 of the height or more.
inventory.already_automatic: story_reaches_down is in the film kit's check_shot.py only, NOT in the plugin copy. The bottom-fifth ratio is not automated.
inventory.llm_tip: Fill the lower frame with the story itself, not dark filler: rule 8 forbids a big dark thing in the bottom left.

inventory.name: Words clear of phone buttons (safe area)
inventory.how_found: Log 06 kept the bottom of the page quiet. Log 19: price boards cut off at the right edge; a label pushed off screen by a camera change. Log 20: the SUPPLY SHIPS SUNK label and a $$$ tag sat where apps put their buttons. Log 30: the liked picture's notice reached 0.91 across, chair and pail 0.96 to 0.97. Log 31: the notice was slid out of the strip.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: frame_check.py and the plugin keep 140 px clear at the sides and top and 380 px at the bottom of 1080 × 1920. The composing guide says anything to read stays left of 0.90 across (unimportant edges up to 0.95). The two rules disagree (140 px is 0.87 across).
inventory.evidence: story L374-376, L596, L601-602, L670-673, L1068-1070, L1126-1128; paper-film/tools/frame_check.py lines 3-4; 07 rule 12; plugin skills/make-explainer-film/SKILL.md line 58, build-cinema-page/camera-and-framing.md line 85
inventory.computable_from: the camera, named props and points, and the 2D overlay positions
inventory.proposed_calculation: One shared safe-area constant used by frame_check, check_shot's must_read and the graphics: x from 0.13 to 0.87 of W (or 0.90, once decided), y from 0.073 to 0.80 of H. Run frame_check on every label and callout automatically whenever a camera changes.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: frame_check.py and check_shot must_read (both in the plugin kit) use different limits, and neither runs by itself after a camera change.
inventory.llm_tip: Re-check every label after every camera change: in round 19 one camera tweak pushed a label off screen.

inventory.name: Main composing rule: every strong thing points at the same place
inventory.how_found: Log 30 measured the liked picture with measure_composition.py, then five critics and a skeptic. In the liked picture about half to two thirds of the brightest parts fall on the notice; in our clip about a fifth. Log 31's rebuilt frame: the notice 3.1 times the frame's average and 60% of the brightest parts; every strong thing within 0.11 of the frame's width of the others.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Where the lines meet, the centre of the brightest 3% (after a slight blur), the centre of the warm light and the centre of the story props all fall in a box at most 0.40 W by 0.50 H that holds the subject. At least 3/4 of the brightest parts in the story box and 2/5 on the subject. Subject at least 1.8 times the frame's average. Sky dim.
inventory.evidence: story L1038-1052 (log 30), L1135-1141 (log 31); 07 lines 25-48 and rule 5
inventory.computable_from: a render and the shot facts
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed by check_shot.py.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes: check_shot.py and measure_composition.py, both in the plugin kit (check_shot is an older copy).
inventory.llm_tip: Fix the one strong thing pointing elsewhere first; it matters more than any other change. Rule-of-thirds reasons were tested and thrown out (log 30).

inventory.name: Story props as one touching group; work props small and far
inventory.how_found: Logs 30 and 31: the chair faced the wrong way (its back to the fire, hiding the lantern) and was turned round; lantern on the seat; pail at the chair's feet. Clip 29's sacks covered about 7% of the frame.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each story prop touches or overlaps another; together they fit a box at most 0.40 by 0.50. The chair stands directly below the notice, seat visible, lantern lit on it. Each work prop covers at most 2% of the frame and is darker than average.
inventory.computable_from: the shot facts
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed by check_shot (rule 9 only partly).
inventory.already_automatic: Yes for rules 3 and 8 (check_shot.py). Rule 9 mostly not.
inventory.llm_tip: Props that touch read like a sentence; props spaced apart read like a list.

inventory.name: Edges that just touch (near-touch)
inventory.how_found: Log 30 found three pairs touching in the liked picture. Log 31 removed a far lamp touching the board's post right where the lines meet. Log 32: an over-wide drum lining brought the drum's edge to 9 px from the notice; the drum's side ran 2 px in front of the post for 113 px, fixed by moving the post 4.5 cm. The checker now measures the longest touching stretch and includes background props.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: On a frame 1,536 px wide: overlaps of at least 20 px and gaps of at least 25 px, scaled to the frame's width.
inventory.computable_from: the flat-colour id pictures from shot_facts.py
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed. The fix in metres is pixels × depth / f_px.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, check_shot.py (the plugin copy is older and may lack the longest-stretch and background-prop parts).
inventory.llm_tip: List background props under pairs_also. Posts running along another prop's edge are easy to miss by eye.

inventory.name: Weight of the quiet side
inventory.how_found: Log 30: an even weight is not the reason the liked picture works (clip 29 is 46 to 54, the liked picture 43 to 57). Log 31: the quiet left half held 34% (aim 40), so a soft cool light was put on the left-hand houses (about 0.6 of the sky's brightness), sacks and bins moved into view and a dim lit window added. Log 32: 38%; then 46% on the film's end frame.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The quiet side holds 40 to 48% of the weight; none of its lights is as bright as the subject; no prop there covers more than 2% of the frame.
inventory.computable_from: a render and the shot facts
inventory.proposed_calculation: If the quiet weight w is below 0.40, multiply the quiet side's fill-light energy by 0.40/w and/or light one more window; re-render small and re-measure (1 or 2 rounds).
inventory.already_automatic: Measured by check_shot. The size of the fix is not computed.
inventory.llm_tip: Fill the quiet side with fine dim detail and one or two small lights, never a second bright place.

inventory.name: Amount and place of warm light
inventory.how_found: Log 30: the liked picture had 2.3% warm, clip 29 had 0.5%. Log 31: 2.9%, nearly all round the story props. Log 32: in the painted end frame, lamps and lit windows spread it (43% round the story props).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Warm light covers 1.5 to 3% of the frame, most of it round the story props.
inventory.computable_from: a render (and the painted frame)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Measured already. Add: scale the warm practical lights by target share / measured share.
inventory.already_automatic: Measured by check_shot.py.
inventory.llm_tip: Painted lamps and windows spread warm light: check the painted frame too, not only the plate.

inventory.name: Subject lit from below by the story's own light
inventory.how_found: Log 31: a narrow warm light just over the coals, aimed at the notice's lower part; it reached 0.07 warmer at the bottom (needs 0.10; the reference 0.17). Log 32: 0.08 on the still. On the film page, with a copy of the warm light under the notice, it reached 0.23.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The subject's bottom is at least 0.10 warmer than its top; aim about 0.17. A notice that keeps its own surface needs its own copy of the warm light in the film page.
inventory.computable_from: a render and the subject's mask
inventory.proposed_calculation: Measure the warmth gradient. If it is below 0.10, raise the linked under-light by 0.17/measured and re-render. In the stage, add the same light under any own-surface sign.
inventory.already_automatic: Measured by check_shot. Not adjusted automatically.
inventory.llm_tip: Signs that keep sharp lettering are not painted, so give them the warm light separately in the film page.

inventory.name: Power of practical lights and the overall exposure
inventory.how_found: Log 31 critics: everything near white (notice, board, chair seat, drum top). The fire went from 900 to 160 W and was raised, the lantern from 60 to 5 W, and the board's timber was darkened by half. Log 32: the frame was a third darker than the reference, so the dusk sky went from 1.4 to 1.96; the chair's paint was lightened to 0.25 (legs had been darker than the pavement), still darker than the notice.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Fire 160 W, lantern 5 W, timber albedo halved, sky strength 1.96, chair paint 0.25. The subject is the brightest thing, at about 3.1 times the frame's average.
inventory.evidence: story L1122-1125 (log 31), L1177-1179 (log 32), L1071 (log 30, spotless white chair)
inventory.computable_from: a render, the list of practical lights, the subject mask and the reference's average brightness
inventory.proposed_calculation: An exposure loop on small renders (270 × 480). For each practical light, find the brightest non-subject surface it lights; if that is brighter than 0.8 × the subject, scale the light by (0.8 × subject / that). Scale the sky so the frame's average matches the reference, keeping the top third under 0.6 × the subject. Clamp near props' albedo between 1.1 × the ground under them and 0.8 × the subject. 2 or 3 rounds.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: When near props go white, cut the practical light and lift it away; don't darken the whole frame.

inventory.name: Light linking (which light reaches what)
inventory.how_found: Log 32: the warm notice light lit the chair's top rail as bright as the notice; the lantern's light lit its own brass frame and made the glass milky; the fire's light, 0.4 m over the rim, made the rim and chair back as bright as the notice. The live flames light the drum in the film instead.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The warm key reaches only the notice and its board. The lantern's light skips the lantern. The fire's light skips the drum and the chair.
inventory.computable_from: the scene's lights and which objects each light is meant for
inventory.proposed_calculation: A light inside, or within 0.2 m of, an object's outline box skips that object. A key light named for a subject reaches only the subject's group and its support.
inventory.already_automatic: set_dressing.py light_reaches exists (film kit pit-village only, not in the plugin), and the checker reads it. Nothing chooses the links by itself.
inventory.llm_tip: Every practical light must skip its own housing.

inventory.name: A lit prop must not outshine the subject
inventory.how_found: Log 32: a flame lights about 6% of the lantern as bright as the notice; a glowing glass lights 18 to 22%. Log 27: the miners' lamps glared over their faces.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Flag a light-prop when more than 10% of it is as bright as the subject.
inventory.computable_from: a render and the prop masks
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, check_shot lights_in_story.
inventory.llm_tip: A small bright flame is fine; a bright glass or body is not.

inventory.name: Render shadow memory
inventory.how_found: Log 31: a hard black wedge across the road turned out to be a render fault, not the lighting: Blender had run out of shadow memory ('Shadow buffer full' in its log). The checker now reads the render log.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No 'Shadow buffer full' or 'Could not allocate shadow atlas' in the render log; otherwise the light rules are not judged.
inventory.computable_from: the render log, the number of shadow-casting lights and the resolution
inventory.proposed_calculation: Before rendering, raise EEVEE's shadow pool when there are many lights. After rendering, read the log; if a fault is found, double the pool and render again.
inventory.already_automatic: Found, yes (check_shot.py with RENDER_LOG). Fixed by itself, no.
inventory.llm_tip: Always keep the render log. A black wedge is often a renderer fault, not your lighting.

inventory.name: Two surfaces on the same plane flicker
inventory.how_found: Log 27: the kitchen ceiling changed colour in one frame. Each room's ceiling sat exactly on the slab above it, which flickers as the camera moves. Fixed by setting them a hair apart.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Surfaces never share a plane; keep them a hair apart.
inventory.computable_from: the scene's geometry
inventory.proposed_calculation: Look for pairs of faces facing the same way, less than 0.1 mm apart and overlapping. Offset them by the larger of 1 mm and 0.0001 × their distance from the camera.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Never stack two surfaces on the same plane.

inventory.name: Fades and appearances (no one-frame switches)
inventory.how_found: Log 27 motion checks: the crowd rose out of a pale flat card and sank through the floor; the scissors jumped in one frame; the padlock appeared in mid-air with a glow that switched on in one frame; a crowd vanished half way through fading out (a cut-out first drawn solid stays solid, then vanishes at half opacity), fixed for every fading piece; crossfades overlapped like a double exposure.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: People fade in and out standing up. Fades run one after another. Every fading piece is see-through from its first frame. Glows build over a few frames. Objects travel; they don't jump.
inventory.computable_from: the page files' animations
inventory.proposed_calculation: Lint the page animations: any opacity, light or position change over fewer than 3 frames (0.1 s) that isn't at a planned cut is flagged. Any material that ever goes below full opacity is marked see-through when built. Overlapping crossfades of the same area are made sequential.
inventory.already_automatic: The half-opacity fix is in the engine. The lint is not.
inventory.llm_tip: Check in motion, not on stills: these faults only show between frames.

inventory.name: Finding unplanned jumps between frames
inventory.how_found: Logs 27 and 29: frame-to-frame scans found jumps the stills missed. Log 29's scan found nothing but the planned cut at 7.3 s. Log 32 made find_jumps.py. Logs 13 and 20 measured the joins between chunks as smooth as any two frames in a row.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A frame is a jump if its change is more than 4 times the middle value of the 5 frames either side, and over a small floor. Planned cuts are listed.
inventory.evidence: story L895-897, L969-970, L980-981, L476, L679-680; paper-film/tools/find_jumps.py
inventory.computable_from: the film, plus the cut times from the camera plans and page joins
inventory.proposed_calculation: Fill the planned cuts in automatically from the stillShot changes, camera_audit's cuts and the page joins. Run on every filmed piece and every chunk join.
inventory.already_automatic: find_jumps.py is in the plugin kit; the planned cuts are typed by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Scan every finished film for jumps and explain each one as a planned cut or a fault.

inventory.name: Handing a painted set over to the 'behind' painting (ghost outlines)
inventory.how_found: Log 29: moving the camera uncovered the painter's outlines of the sacks and cart left on the road (pale jagged copies, then dark ink lines). Fixed with a props-removed painting handed over round the props as soon as the camera moves. Finding why the handover didn't work took three tries: it waited for too much camera movement, and a helper step was half thrown away by leftover depth in a working picture. Painted clouds had nowhere to land, then the sky showed a pale double edge, so the painted sky went alone on a far card.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: projected-set.js defaults: the behind painting is used round near props out to reach 0.05 of the frame height, handed over at quickMove 0.00003 (about half a degree); seam fades full at moveAngle 0.01 (about 8 degrees); frontStretch [1.3, 1.9]; edgeWidth 0.006; stretch [2.5, 5]; frameEdge 0.03; unseen surfaces darken 0.75, tint 0.6, fill 0.35; sky on its own far card.
inventory.evidence: story L946-955 (log 29), L322 and L325 (word list); film-kit/paper-film/scenes/projected-set.js lines 512-545
inventory.computable_from: the set and the plates
inventory.proposed_calculation: Keep the defaults. Work out reach from the measured width of the painter's outlines: reach = (outline px + 10 px) / H.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in the film kit's projected-set.js. NOT in the plugin kit (the plugin has only painted-projection.js).
inventory.llm_tip: Hand over to the behind painting at the first movement, not after a threshold.

inventory.name: Lining a painting up with its plate
inventory.how_found: Log 32: the shot checker's new test showed every prop lining up better once slid about 4 px. The painter had stretched the picture by 0.65% and shifted it 3 px. align_painting.py undoes it: 96% of outlines then sit on the painting's edges, against 70% before.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Always line up the main painting with its plate, then the behind painting against the lined-up main one. Aim for 95% or more of outlines on edges.
inventory.computable_from: the plate's shot facts and the painting
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a calculation: the scale and shift that best fit the props' outlines to the painting's edges.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, align_painting.py (plugin kit). Run by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Run align_painting on every painting before projecting it; even 3 px shows as double edges.

inventory.name: Keeping painted shadows when the film switches to the behind painting
inventory.how_found: Log 32 motion check: 2 seconds in, the fire's long shadows from the pail and chair faded off the pavement. Fixed by keeping the main painting except inside the props' own outlines (keep_painted_shadows.py). A fresh helper then found a pale 10 to 15 px outline round the pail (the gap had no shadow); the shadows' darkening was carried into the gap. The pavement patch stayed at 70 to 71 levels, where before it rose to 89. Log 29: the barrel's painted scorch ring faded, so a soft 3D shadow was put under it.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Main painting everywhere except inside near props' outlines widened 10 px; shadow darkening carried inward; soft 3D contact shadows under props whose painted shadow goes.
inventory.computable_from: the plates, the paintings and the props' outlines
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a calculation. Add a check: pavement brightness just beside each prop, before and after the handover, changes by at most 2 levels.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, keep_painted_shadows.py (plugin kit). Run by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Measure the ground beside each near prop across the switch; a fading shadow shows only in motion.

inventory.name: Paint-out masks and stand-ins in AI paintings
inventory.how_found: Log 24: the canopy wouldn't fit as a rectangle because the painting's perspective isn't consistent, so it was fitted to its four painted corners. Ghosts of a post and the kiosk showed until the painted-out areas were widened. A grey block stood in front of the kiosk until the painted-out part was pushed further back. The canopy's underside drew dark until surfaces seen almost edge-on could wear the painting. Stand-ins drew brighter until both they and the background showed the painting with no lamp.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Match from the painting's view: mean about 4 levels off, 6.4% of pixels more than 12 off (the pass mark). Widen paint-out masks. Fit shapes to painted corners. No lamp on painted surfaces.
inventory.computable_from: the painting and the fitted boxes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Score automatically: render from the projector's view and compare with the painting; pass if mean difference ≤ 5 levels and share over 12 levels ≤ 7%. Widen masks by the painter's outline width + 4 px.
inventory.already_automatic: fit_station_proxies.py and station_plates.py are in the film kit only, not in the plugin kit. No general score.
inventory.llm_tip: AI paintings have inconsistent perspective: fit stand-ins to painted corners, not to true rectangles.

inventory.name: Keeping the painting's own light on 3D objects
inventory.how_found: Logs 22 and 24: one colour over each whole model turned chrome and headlights cyan; colour handling was wrong twice; models drew as black blocks (no surface directions in their files); models floated. The painting's own light is kept exactly; the 3D car and pumps take a small share of the lamp, and their shadows fall on a see-through ground that shows only shadows.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Painted surfaces unlit. 3D objects get a small lamp share. Car colour within a few levels of the painting; pumps about 10% darker.
inventory.computable_from: the painting, the model masks and a render from the painting's view
inventory.proposed_calculation: Use projected-set's calibrate (draw the set from the projector with and without the painting) and a per-object gain to match the painting inside each mask; two rounds.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: projected-set calibrate (film kit only). match_model_colours.py is superseded (its check was circular).
inventory.llm_tip: Work out surface directions when loading models that lack them, and never use one colour over a whole model.

inventory.name: What the painter garbles: lettering, thin parts, glows, holes
inventory.how_found: Log 29: the first repaint garbled the notice's small print, and the painter added snow-like blotches. Log 30: every program garbled the notice. Log 31: the pail's thin wire handle was removed (the painter would smear it). Log 32: an even orange disc in the drum's mouth would be painted as soup or a lid, so its glow fades up from the coals; a pure-black doorway made the shut gate read as open, so dim doors went behind it; the prompt forbade adding flames, smoke, glows or new shadows round near props, and the painter added nothing.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Signs keep their own surfaces (ownSurface). Remove parts only a few pixels thin. No even bright discs or pure-black holes near the story. The prompt says keep every shape and the light and dark, and never add flames, smoke, glows or new shadows.
inventory.computable_from: the plate render, the shot_facts id pictures and the text sizes
inventory.proposed_calculation: A painter-readiness scan of the plate: (a) for each prop part, the thinnest it shows on screen (a distance transform of its id mask); under 3 px means remove or thicken; (b) any lettering under about 24 px tall goes on its own surface; (c) any area over 0.3% of the frame that is very even (spread under 2 levels) and strongly coloured, or under 5 levels dark, inside the story box is flagged; (d) the prompt template adds the 'never add' sentence by itself.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Treat any painter as a smudger of detail: keep lettering and thin parts on your own surfaces.

inventory.name: Lettering big enough to read on a phone
inventory.how_found: Log 32, left for later: PITS WILL BE CLOSED is 11 px tall; about 18 px would read easily. Log 34: drums whose words couldn't be read, then PETROL and DIESEL made readable.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Key lines at least about 18 px tall on the 1080 × 1920 frame.
inventory.computable_from: the letters' height in metres, the camera and the lens
inventory.proposed_calculation: Height on screen = letter height (m) × (H/2) / tan(vfov/2) / depth. Choose letter height = 18 px × depth × 2 tan(vfov/2) / H at the shot's end frame, and flag anything smaller.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Size key lettering for the end frame of the move, where it has to be read.

inventory.name: Letters hidden by tacks, stains or props
inventory.how_found: Log 29: a rust stain from a tack hid the A of ABBOTSCLOUGH, another tack punched a hole in the E of NOTICE, and the colliery sign was cut to stray letters. Log 31: the checker first missed a post across the notice's words (fixed).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No decal or prop over key lettering; signs not cut by the frame.
inventory.computable_from: the glyph boxes from the lettering script and the id pictures
inventory.proposed_calculation: Export each key line's letter boxes. Check that no other group or decal overlaps them on screen, and that no sign is cut by the frame's edge.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: check_shot checks words of the subject hidden by a prop in front. Decals are not checked.
inventory.llm_tip: Place tacks and stains from the letters' boxes, never by eye.

inventory.name: Title size and contrast
inventory.how_found: Log 19: labels pale on pale walls. Log 20: a soft dark band behind words on the desk. Log 29: the opening title was too small and was made larger. Log 32: the amber 1926 was faint against the sky, so a soft dark band went behind it.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Titles go in dim sky away from the brightest lamp, with a soft dark band behind when needed, and big enough to read.
inventory.computable_from: the title's text, colour and position, and the frame behind it
inventory.proposed_calculation: Measure the contrast between the text colour and the background under it. If it is below 4.5 to 1, add a band with the smallest opacity that reaches 4.5 to 1. Flag titles whose letters are under about 3.5% of the frame's height (to confirm).
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Measure title contrast on the actual frame behind it, not on the design.

inventory.name: Fire, flames and glow
inventory.how_found: Log 29: the brazier's flames drew as white paper cones (lit by the fire's own lamp); a paper-crown flame; a see-through flame; flames like a neat row of cartoon teardrops; smoke rising as a stiff sheet. Fixed with three ragged flames of different sizes and leans and drifting smoke. Log 32: the glow's size pulse made its rim slide on the road, calmed to a 1.2% swing (from 2.8%); flames still look like flat cut-outs and sparks rise in tidy strings.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Three ragged flame shapes with different sizes and leans; flames not lit by their own light; glow size swing about 1.2%; drifting smoke.
inventory.computable_from: the effect's settings and the filmed frames
inventory.proposed_calculation: A flame maker that varies count (3 to 5), size (±30%) and lean (±15 degrees). Glow pulse at most 1.5% of its radius. Sparks start from jittered places. Measure the glow's swing on the film and keep it under 1.5%.
inventory.already_automatic: pit-village-effects.js is in the film kit only, not the plugin.
inventory.llm_tip: Even, regular effects read as cartoons: vary size, lean and timing.

inventory.name: Smoke and chimneys
inventory.how_found: Log 30: the liked picture's chimney pours smoke although the pit is closed. Log 32: two chimney smokes were dropped because both chimneys are out of frame. Log 34 round 4: the smoke looked like a fault (pale rings); round 5 blows it across the view.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Smoke only from emitters in frame and right for the story, blown across the view.
inventory.computable_from: the emitters' positions, the camera and the story state
inventory.proposed_calculation: Drop an emitter whose point is outside the frame for the whole shot. Set the wind across the screen, sideways to the view direction. Flag ring-like smoke by its round symmetry.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Ask whether each smoke source is in frame and makes sense in the story; a closed pit has no smoke.

inventory.name: Dust, snow and particles in the right places
inventory.how_found: Log 11: dust hidden behind the crowd. Log 13: dust lingered after its page. Log 27: dust billowed upward and snow fell inside the rooms. The filming tool starts each chunk a few frames early so dust and smoke are already in place.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Particles stay inside their space, fall downward, and end with their page. Each chunk has a pre-roll.
inventory.evidence: story L451 (log 11), L472 (log 13), L882-883 (log 27); render-paper-film.mjs line 137
inventory.computable_from: the room volumes and the page times
inventory.proposed_calculation: Keep emitters out of the room boxes. End particle lifetimes by the page's end. Set the pre-roll to the longest particle lifetime rather than a fixed few frames.
inventory.already_automatic: A fixed pre-roll in the filming tool. Nothing else.
inventory.llm_tip: Check effects in motion at the edges of rooms and pages.

inventory.name: Shadows on the paper stage
inventory.how_found: Log 11: no shadows at all until sheets cast from both faces; the smoothest soft shadows don't work in the hidden browser, so softened plain ones are used; shadows too small to see, then word shadows so big they read as a second word. Log 15: the trees came out almost black from shading themselves (fixed by changing how shadows are kept off a surface). Log 16: rings and criss-crossing shadows.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Sheets cast shadows from both faces; softened plain shadows; a small shadow offset for words; a shadow bias that stops self-shadowing.
inventory.computable_from: the lamp's position, piece sizes and shadow map size
