inventory.proposed_calculation: Bias = 1.5 × (shadow camera width / shadow map size). Word shadow offset at most 15% of the letter height.
inventory.already_automatic: The settings are fixed in the stage; check-shadows.mjs exists.
inventory.llm_tip: If a surface goes black, suspect it shading itself before changing the light.

inventory.name: Distance picture and lens blur
inventory.how_found: Log 16: a too-coarse distance picture and a blur that ate the detail. Log 19: the cinema look uses lens blur with focus falling off.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The distance picture at frame resolution; blur modest enough that detail survives; focus point given (finish_one_page_still --focus).
inventory.computable_from: the depth, the focus distance and the lens
inventory.proposed_calculation: Blur in pixels from the circle of confusion, proportional to |1/z - 1/z_focus|, capped at about 6 px. Distance picture at the same resolution as the frame.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly (the stage's lens blur).
inventory.llm_tip: Check close-ups of fine detail after adding lens blur.

inventory.name: Paper mouth from the voice's loudness
inventory.how_found: Log 11: the mouth looked like a black bar, so it became a narrower jaw that opens on louder syllables.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: 40 ms loudness slices; snaps open fast, closes a little slower.
inventory.computable_from: the levelled narration track
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, make_mouth_track.py (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Drive mouths from the voice track, never by hand.

inventory.name: Colourfulness of painted people and figures
inventory.how_found: Log 20: the politician's face was about 1.7 times as colourful as the other painted people; all three layers (face, jaw, mouth) were calmed to match. Log 34 round 2: the figures' coats were too red, with a toy-like look.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: tone_piece.py --saturation 0.62 --contrast 0.9 --lift 0.03, the same on every layer of one figure.
inventory.computable_from: all pieces and figure materials
inventory.proposed_calculation: Measure every piece with tone_piece --measure. For pieces above 1.2 × the median colour strength, saturation factor = median / piece. Apply it to all layers of that figure. For 3D figures, cap saturation at 1.2 × the scene's median.
inventory.already_automatic: Measuring yes; the factor is set by hand (tone_piece.py, plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Compare every figure's colour strength with the rest before filming.

inventory.name: A crowd as seen from the camera
inventory.how_found: Log 34 round 4: the men stood in single file, so from the camera they stacked into one dark column, and nobody was ever seen working. Round 5: a loose crowd across the gate and people working inside the lit doorways. Log 27: the strike crowd seemed to stand inside the factory until the pavement was widened and the crowd moved forward.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A loose crowd across the gate; workers visible in lit doorways; crowds clearly outside buildings.
inventory.computable_from: the figures' positions and the camera
inventory.proposed_calculation: Place figures on a jittered band sideways to the view (at least 0.6 m apart across, ±1 m in depth). Check on screen that each figure is at least 50% visible and that together they span at least 60% of the gate's width.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Arrange people as the camera sees them, not as seen from above.

inventory.name: Things that read as something else on a phone
inventory.how_found: Log 20 judge: stone blocks by the gutters looked like little cameras, figured wood like a contour map, dark lenses like sunglasses. Log 19: banknotes like white bricks. Log 26: bundles like soap. Log 34: striped brick (a one-line bug), doorways like bar charts, a gasholder read as a tank, a jacket as a headless man, heads that looked bald.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Judged at phone size.
inventory.computable_from: judgement only, except stripes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Give critics stills at phone size (about 390 × 693). Detect strong repeating stripes on large surfaces with a Fourier peak test.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Look at every new model in the real film frame at phone size before filming.

inventory.name: Telling two similar buildings apart
inventory.how_found: Log 34 round 2: No. 1 became dark red brick with one round chimney, No. 2 pale stone with two square chimneys and a tank, so they're told apart at a glance.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Different in brightness, colour and outline.
inventory.computable_from: the models
inventory.proposed_calculation: Render both outlines. Require a mean brightness difference of 20% or more and outline overlap (IoU) of 0.7 or less.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Things the viewer must tell apart need different outlines and values, not just colours.

inventory.name: Model detail against filming speed
inventory.how_found: Log 20: the works went from about 2,000 to 22,000 to 34,000 triangles; the town about 63,000; the props about 5,600; 232 parts joined into 19; bevels shade smoothly. Pages with detailed models drew at 12 to 16 s a picture, the others at about 3. Log 34: the FOUNDRY library was about 7 times slower (223 against 33 s for two views) and made the road icy; not used.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Join parts to cut draw calls; keep detail where it is seen.
inventory.computable_from: triangle counts, draw calls and profile_frame timings
inventory.proposed_calculation: Fit seconds per frame ≈ a + b × triangles + c × draw calls from profile_frame on a few pages. Join or simplify parts until the estimated filming time fits.
inventory.already_automatic: profile_frame.mjs (plugin kit), by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Profile one frame before adding detail, and join parts.

inventory.name: Parts sized to their parent model
inventory.how_found: Log 32: a critic asked for a sooty lining 0.365 m across inside a drum only 0.296 m in radius; it stuck out as a flat orange band (lesson 116). Log 31: putting the lantern back on its chair would have dropped it to the pavement. Log 29: the notice board's posts landed on top of it.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Measure the model before adding parts to it.
inventory.computable_from: the models' outline boxes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Build helpers read the parent's size and clamp a child to fit inside it. After building, assert no child's box exceeds its parent's by more than 1 mm unless allowed.
inventory.already_automatic: No (check_shot sees only what shows on screen).
inventory.llm_tip: Read real dimensions from the model; never trust a size from a critic's note.

inventory.name: What rests on what (floating and sunk objects)
inventory.how_found: Log 22: SAM models floated about half a unit, then 0.01 to 0.03. Log 20: price tags none within 15 units of the painting and none touching; the basket 0.05 clear on the belt. Log 29: the board floated. Log 31 tests: a pail lifted 5 m; a drum sunk 0.30 m got 'raise drum by 0.30 m'.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Contact within 0.01 to 0.03. Tags at least 15 units in front of the painted room. The checker states the fix in metres.
inventory.computable_from: the shot facts or the scene's outline boxes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Blender sets: already checked. Cinema-stage card models: cast a ray down (gap at most 0.03) and check tags stand at least 15 units in front of the painted room's depth.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes for Blender sets (check_shot) and ground_under_objects.py for SAM objects. Not for cinema-stage pages.
inventory.llm_tip: Check contact numerically; a few centimetres of float reads as fake.

inventory.name: Imported glass and lenses
inventory.how_found: Log 32: the gas lamps and the lantern looked like flat amber cards. The 'see-through' setting had been ignored because the imported glass takes that value from its picture; unhooked, the mantles and flame show. Log 20: dark lenses made reading glasses look like sunglasses.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Unhook the alpha picture on glass and set see-through explicitly; keep lenses pale.
inventory.computable_from: the imported materials
inventory.proposed_calculation: On import, if a material named glass or lens has its alpha fed by a picture, unhook it and set see-through explicitly; report it.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: After importing models, check every glass material's see-through setting.

inventory.name: Refreshing the Blender scene after moving the camera
inventory.how_found: Log 32: an extra lit window landed off the frame because moving the camera never refreshed the scene, so the window picker used the old camera.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Refresh the scene after any camera move before anything works from the camera.
inventory.computable_from: rule
inventory.proposed_calculation: Always call view_layer.update() after setting the camera. Assert the picked windows land inside the frame.
inventory.already_automatic: Fixed in the scene script only, not as a shared rule.
inventory.llm_tip: In Blender scripts, update the view layer after any move before working from it.

inventory.name: Filming time, worker count and stretch size
inventory.how_found: Measured in many logs. Log 11: 23 s took about 12 minutes. Log 13: chapter 1's 6,641 frames took about 80 minutes one page at a time (two at once was no faster). Log 19: two workers on 4 processors are 17% faster (1.44 against 1.68 s a frame). Log 20: detailed-model pages 12 to 16 s a frame, others about 3; about 7 hours in all. Log 26: Blender's fast drawing about 20 s a picture (fine for one background per shot). Log 27: 1.8 s a frame. Log 29: about 12 s a frame (40 minutes for 360 frames, two at once). Log 32: about 41 minutes per filming of 13 s. Log 34: held shots 1.1 to 1.3 s; round 4 at 1.4 s.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: 1 worker on 2 processors, 2 on 4; chunks of 240 frames; check the first finished stretch at once.
inventory.evidence: story L452, L474, L619, L674-676, L833-835, L903, L979-980, L987-988, L1235, L1254, L1359-1360, L1380; paper-film/tools/film-chapter-parallel.sh lines 2-5; plugin skills/film-and-finish/SKILL.md lines 20-35
inventory.computable_from: the page files' frame counts, profile_frame timings and the processor count
inventory.proposed_calculation: Before filming, time two frames per page (one held, one moving). Total time = sum over pages of frames × seconds a frame ÷ speed-up (1.17 for 2 workers on 4 processors, 1.0 on 2). Report the hours, and split into FILM_FROM/FILM_TO stretches of at most about 100 minutes each.
inventory.already_automatic: No estimator. profile_frame is run by hand, and the numbers are prose in the plugin skill.
inventory.llm_tip: Estimate filming time before you start and tell the user. Check the first finished stretch at once so a fault doesn't waste hours.

inventory.name: Surviving restarts and the 2-hour job limit
inventory.how_found: Log 19: the cloud machine restarted and silently stopped filming for about 90 minutes. Log 20: stopped by the 2-hour limit on background jobs, then a restart lost about 30 minutes of page 3; the tool now keeps every 60 frames as soon as they are drawn. Log 34: a restart overnight lost only the filming.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: PIECE_FRAMES 60. Run the same command again and it carries on. Watch for a job stopping, not only for it finishing.
inventory.computable_from: the measured seconds a frame
inventory.proposed_calculation: PIECE_FRAMES = round(300 s / seconds a frame), kept between 30 and 240, so a stop loses at most about 5 minutes. A check every 30 minutes that the newest piece file is younger than twice the time one piece takes; if not, restart.
inventory.already_automatic: PIECE_FRAMES=60 is fixed (plugin kit). No watchdog.
inventory.llm_tip: Watch for filming stopping, not only finishing; a cloud machine can restart without warning.

inventory.name: Running out of memory: lazy chapters
inventory.how_found: Log 34: 16 heavy pages ran the computer out of memory, so chapters now load only the pages a piece of film needs (about 2.8 GB a piece).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: lazy=true for long chapters of heavy sets.
inventory.computable_from: the page count, models per page and the machine's memory
inventory.proposed_calculation: Turn lazy on when the summed model file sizes × about 4 exceed half of free memory, or when there are more than 8 heavy pages.
inventory.already_automatic: In the film kit only. The plugin's cinema-chapter.js (69 lines against 100) has no lazy loading.
inventory.llm_tip: Use lazy chapters whenever pages carry Blender sets.

inventory.name: Held shots drawn once
inventory.how_found: Log 34: the still set is drawn once and reused, so a held frame takes 1.1 to 1.3 s, about 5 times faster.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Mark what moves; everything else is drawn once per held view.
inventory.computable_from: the page files (which objects animate)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Find animated objects automatically from the page's timeline (anything whose properties change during the held span) and cache the rest.
inventory.already_automatic: In the film kit only (the plugin's cinema-kit.js is older).
inventory.llm_tip: Mark moving things explicitly; anything not marked is frozen in held shots.

inventory.name: Changes on a held shot (state pictures)
inventory.how_found: Log 34: changes on a held shot (the men gone, the windows lit) are made by swapping only the area that changes. Measured on the people test's plates: two renders of the same set differ by under 1 level of grain.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: make_state_picture.py: a pixel counts as changed if, after a 2 px blur, its largest colour difference is over 6 levels, or over 3 levels after a 10 px blur. The mask is cleared of specks, widened, then softened.
inventory.computable_from: two plates (with and without the change) and the outlines
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a calculation.
inventory.already_automatic: In the film kit only. make_state_picture.py and make_behind_picture.py are NOT in the plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: Never cut to a whole second painting: every brushstroke would jump.

inventory.name: Sendable copy under 30 MB
inventory.how_found: Log 08: the first film file (37 MB) was too big to send, so the sent copy was squeezed to 25 MB. Later copies came out at 28.2, 27, 27.6 and 26.5 MB, each checked against the master.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A 28 MB default limit. Video kbps = 28 × 8000 × 0.97 / seconds - 128. Two-pass x264, preset slow, tune film; AAC sound at 128 kbps. The master copies the video untouched with AAC at 256 kbps.
inventory.evidence: story L403-406 (log 08), L477, L622-623, L680; narration-tools/finish_film.sh lines 16-27
inventory.computable_from: the film's duration
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a calculation.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, finish_film.sh (plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Compare busy frames of the sendable copy with the master.

inventory.name: File size limits: repository and kit parts
inventory.how_found: Log 14: the kit went in three zips under 30 MB (20.8, 17.5 and 24.8 MB). Log 21: masters of about 800 MB are over GitHub's 100 MB limit. Log 25: uploaded in four batches; the repository grew to 1.6 GB, more than GitHub's suggested 1 GB.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No file over 100 MB in git; parts of 28 MB or less for sending in chat; no video or audio in the repository (the user's rule).
inventory.computable_from: the list of file sizes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Pack files into parts of at most 28 MB (first-fit, largest first). A pre-commit check that refuses files over 100 MB and video or audio files.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check sizes before committing or zipping, not after a refusal.

inventory.name: Contact sheets and how often to look
inventory.how_found: Log 13: about 85 single moments checked at full size before filming, then contact sheets at one frame a second. Logs 19 and 20: one frame every 3 seconds of the finished film. Logs 29 to 32: sheets of two frames a second for motion. Log 27: motion checks found faults stills can't show.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Full-size stills before filming. After filming, one frame every 3 s for an overview, two a second for moving shots, plus find_jumps.
inventory.computable_from: the timeline (cue words) and the camera plans
inventory.proposed_calculation: Choose still times automatically: each cue word + 0.5 s; the start, middle and end of each move; the middle of each page turn. Make the sheets automatically.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: render-paper-film.mjs --stills and the contact sheet tools, but times are chosen by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Choose check moments from the timeline, not at random.

inventory.name: Fresh checkers after fixes, and a skeptic
inventory.how_found: Log 19: 4 must-fix and about 20 should-fix findings confirmed and 14 rejected; the fix check found 4 new problems the fixes had caused. Log 30: a skeptic rejected 11 of 35 claims. Log 32: a fresh helper found the pale outline the first fix had made.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Critics, then a skeptic, then fixes, then a fresh checker.
inventory.computable_from: judgement only
inventory.proposed_calculation: A workflow, not a number.
inventory.already_automatic: The critique-film and check-fixes workflows (plugin).
inventory.llm_tip: Always send a fresh checker after fixes: fixes make new faults.

inventory.name: Checking nothing changed after editing shared code
inventory.how_found: Log 14: the kit rebuilt pictures identical to the originals. Log 21: six moments identical pixel for pixel from a fresh copy. Log 34: the notice corner proven unchanged after its scripts were reused. Status: a largest difference of 4 to 5 of 255 on a few pixels is drawing noise.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Largest difference at most 5 of 255, on a few pixels only.
inventory.computable_from: stored reference stills
inventory.proposed_calculation: Keep reference stills for each scene. After a shared change, redraw them: pass if the largest difference is 5 or less and fewer than 0.1% of pixels differ by more than 2.
inventory.already_automatic: No automatic suite.
inventory.llm_tip: Redraw the reference stills before and after touching shared code.

inventory.name: Facts that go out of date
inventory.how_found: Traps list: New Zealand inflation may change on 22 October, the Reserve Bank's rate on 28 October, unemployment on 4 November.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Check dated figures before recording and before publishing.
inventory.computable_from: ledger entries with their next release dates
inventory.proposed_calculation: Give each ledger fact a valid_until date (its next scheduled release). Before recording and before publishing, list the facts past that date.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Write the next release date beside every 'latest' figure.

inventory.name: Checking names were said right, from the transcript
inventory.how_found: Log 05: Mattei said the Italian way. Log 09: Mattei in English sounds. Log 19: ElevenLabs' own transcript heard 'Ruhr' and 'Mattei' as those words.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Compare the transcript's words with the script's words.
inventory.computable_from: the script and the transcript
inventory.proposed_calculation: A normalised word comparison. Any name that doesn't match is flagged for a re-record.
inventory.already_automatic: No flag (extract_word_times only lines the words up).
inventory.llm_tip: Use the transcript as a free pronunciation check for names.

inventory.name: Re-recording one page moves everything after it
inventory.how_found: Traps and Status: the whole chapter's timing, mix and film must be made again, about 25 minutes of computer time.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Redo the timing, the mix and the filming of every page whose times change.
inventory.computable_from: the old and new timelines
inventory.proposed_calculation: Compare the two timelines and list the pages whose start or word times changed. Delete only those pages' chunks and film them again.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Record all pages before filming. A late retake costs a re-film of everything after it.

inventory.name: Period and story accuracy of pictures
inventory.how_found: Log 10: the samples drew Second World War tanks, a symbol like a hooked cross and a real movement's flag. Log 19: 1920s-dressed men in today's New Zealand street, a party-coloured tie, a top-hatted caricature. Log 29: too much coal for a lockout, snow on a May road. Log 32: the oil-drum brazier is more 1984 than 1926 (kept on purpose).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A history critic checks every picture.
inventory.computable_from: judgement only
inventory.proposed_calculation: None; a critic's job.
inventory.already_automatic: The critique-film workflow.
inventory.llm_tip: Ask a history critic about every painted object, not only the words.

inventory.name: Motion that matches the meaning of the words
inventory.how_found: Log 19: the rate dial slid down as if rates were cut; a needle fell on the word 'raising'; banknotes and a pay packet landed face-down; coins landed where the camera couldn't see them. Log 13: a worker's cap peeked over a slammed door (the door was made taller and page 6 filmed again).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Movement direction matches the spoken meaning; landings happen where the camera sees them.
inventory.computable_from: partly computable: landing positions, camera and occluders; the meaning is judgement
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each landing object, project its final position and check it is inside the frame and not hidden (frame_check plus the id pictures). Keep a table of words that mean up or down and check dial and needle directions against it.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Read each motion against its word: rising words need rising things.

inventory.name: Using an AI picture as a composition sketch only
inventory.how_found: Log 30 composition test: Nano Banana Pro choosing its own camera scored 7 to 8 of 10 and the user liked it; Flux keeping our camera scored lowest (3.5 to 5); every program garbled the notice and redrew the props. Flux takes at most ten pictures, Nano Banana Pro up to 14.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Copy the composition and the kind of move, never the pictures or their lettering.
inventory.computable_from: judgement only
inventory.proposed_calculation: None; then rebuild it and measure the rebuild with check_shot.
inventory.already_automatic: Documented in 07 Composing a shot.
inventory.llm_tip: Let a picture program choose its own camera for a sketch, then rebuild it in 3D and run the checker.

inventory.name: Paid steps need the user's own yes
inventory.how_found: Log 34: this session's automatic safety check refused the first ElevenLabs call despite the budget. Logs 21 and 25: the safety check also blocked saving files to the repository.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Ask the user; never work around a refusal.
inventory.computable_from: judgement only
inventory.proposed_calculation: None.
inventory.already_automatic: House rules in the plugin.
inventory.llm_tip: Do every free step first, then ask once, with the exact cost.

inventory.name: What the background remover drops from cut-outs
inventory.how_found: Log 13: laying every cut-out over magenta showed what the remover had dropped: the politician's lectern (put back), Sardinia on the map (the map went on a paper card) and part of a coal heap (kept with a lower threshold). Log 11: a small pale fin that could read as a flag was cut away.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A magenta contact sheet of every cut-out; a threshold per piece in the cut list.
inventory.computable_from: the painting and its mask
inventory.proposed_calculation: Flag pieces where more than 2% of the pixels that differ from the grey backdrop (by more than 12 levels) fall outside the mask, or where the mask has islands.
inventory.already_automatic: contact_sheet_masks.py, which is visual only.
inventory.llm_tip: Look at every cut-out over magenta, not over white or grey.

inventory.name: Dark masses where the eye enters (bottom left)
inventory.how_found: Log 32: the gutter was first a pale stripe, then joined the drum's shadow into one dark pool where the eye enters, then plain stone just under the road. The painted end frame's gutter covered 2.1% (limit 1%) but was kept as a narrow lead-in line.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Nothing in the bottom-left quarter covers more than 1%, except thin lead-in lines.
inventory.computable_from: the frame
inventory.proposed_calculation: Find connected dark areas (below half the frame's mean brightness) in the bottom-left quarter. Ignore those longer than 6 times their width (thin lines). Flag the rest above 1%.
inventory.already_automatic: check_shot has the 1% test, but it also flags thin lines.
inventory.llm_tip: A thin dark line leading in is fine; a dark lump is not.

inventory.name: Lens numbers every placement sum rests on
inventory.how_found: Re-derived by hand at least five times: the teaching critic's geometry_check.py (design round), round 1's film_distance_check.py (letter sizes), round 2's chimney ray casts, round 4's layout_calc.py and smoke_path.py, round 5's smoke_trace.py. Each helper rewrote the same pinhole sums in scratch.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Film frame 1080 x 1920, level camera, 60.4 degrees top to bottom: focal length = 960 / tan(30.2 deg) = 1649.4 px; half-angle across 18.1 deg. Plate 1536 x 2730 at 64.4 degrees: focal 2168 px. On-screen size px = size_m x 1649.4 / distance_m. Down = 0.5 + (eye_z - z) x 1649.4 / (d x 1920). Across = 0.5 + (x - cam_x) x 1649.4 / (d x 1080).
inventory.evidence: SCRATCH/redesign/design/critic-teaching-and-pictures/geometry_check.py lines 3-11; SCRATCH/redesign/round4-set/tools/layout_calc.py lines 4-15; KIT/paper-film/blender/inflation-chapter-2-newcomers/works/assemble_works.py line 169 (FILM_FOV, PLATE_FOV = 60.4, 64.4); PLAN line 1427 (T1)
inventory.computable_from: the 3D scene's camera file (works-camera-VIEW.json / shot facts) and any point in the scene
inventory.proposed_calculation: One shared module frame_geometry.py (Python and JS twin): focal(fov_v, H) = (H/2)/tan(fov_v/2); project(point, camera) -> (across, down, depth); px_tall(size_m, depth) = size_m x focal / depth; works for plate and film lens. Every calculator below calls it, with no Blender run needed.
inventory.already_automatic: No. shot_facts.py measures after a Blender run; no quick projector exists; helpers rewrote it in scratch each round. Not in the plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: Never guess where something lands on screen or how big it is: project it with the film lens (60.4 degrees vertical, focal 1649 px on a 1920-high frame) before building or moving anything.

inventory.name: Camera stands in line with the subject's edge, never turned
inventory.how_found: Design critics (T1, T2, T22) checked the first plan with the lens: W3 placed 3 to 3.6 m right of the lane's middle put the meeting point 0.15 to 0.18 of the frame's width off the pier, and turning could not close it; W1/W2 1 m off the wall saw the gate at 4.5 degrees (edge-on). Log 31 found the same.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Level camera, yaw 0: the lines meet at 0.5 across, 0.5 down. A sideways offset L at distance D moves the meeting point 0.5 x (L/D)/0.327 of the frame width. Stand with camera x on the subject's edge; a face seen at under about 20 degrees is edge-on and fails.
inventory.computable_from: subject outline in the 3D scene, camera lens
inventory.proposed_calculation: camera_x = x of the subject edge (or centre) that should hold the meeting point; yaw = pitch = 0; check |across(vanishing point) - across(subject edge)| <= 0.02; reject spots where atan(lateral/forward) to the subject's face < 20 deg.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py measures where the lines meet after a render (main rule). Nothing places the camera.
inventory.llm_tip: To move the meeting point, move the camera sideways; turning it moves everything together and never closes the gap.

inventory.name: Street camera sideways spot: clear of the near houses
inventory.how_found: Round 2: the plan's spot in line with the outer pier put the camera 0.2 m from the house fronts; near house and downpipe filled about 40% of the frame and a downpipe hid No. 2's chimney. Round 3 compared four placings with the shot checker (mid-pavement 12 and 4 problems; gates moved 0.5 or 0.9 m pushed the nearest man past the phone buttons; the pier spot stood inside the bank's bay). Round 4 moved 0.4 m toward the kerb.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: W1/W2 at x = +-3.7 m: pavement middle (4.1) minus 0.4 m, so 1.5 m from the house fronts. The near house then reaches only to about 0.2 across (was 0.28). Nearest downpipes removed; the two nearest cottages' windows dark, one dim curtained window at 0.6 share.
inventory.evidence: KIT/.../works/assemble_works.py lines 124-131 and 404-405; SCRATCH/redesign/round2-result.json checked.findings[0]; round3-result.json works.summary; round4-result.json set.summary 'Fuller W1 and W2'
inventory.computable_from: 3D scene (house-front line, kerb, subject), lens
inventory.proposed_calculation: Search camera x across the pavement in 0.1 m steps; for each, project the near facade's nearest visible corner and the subject; keep near facade <= 0.20 across (or >= 0.80 on the right), subject's far edge <= 0.88 across, meeting point on the subject; flag any vertical pipe or post within 0.3 m of the camera-to-subject ray.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Never stand a street camera against the house fronts; about 1.5 m out keeps the near wall in the frame's outer fifth.

inventory.name: Camera distance so the story fills the lower frame (feet near 0.72 down)
inventory.how_found: Round 4 critic against the notice-corner standard (drum, chair, pail fill 0.45 to 0.8 down): the Works story sat 0.53 to 0.65 down over 35 to 40% bare paving, because the 6 m rule plus a 6.6 m single file pushed the camera 12 m back. Worked out from the camera: 3 m nearer. Round 5 applied it and measured.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: W1/W2 plate 10.0 m and composed 8.8 m from the wall (were 13.0 and 11.8). Nearest man about 7 m away, feet about 0.72 down, gate about half the frame's width. Round 5 check: DIESEL drum reaches 0.72 down in W1 and W2 (target 0.70).
inventory.evidence: assemble_works.py lines 132-138; round4-result.json critique.findings[2]; SCRATCH/redesign/round5-set/checks/w1-quiet-d/light/report.md line 73; w2-quiet-c/light/report.md line 53
inventory.computable_from: eye height, ground height under the nearest story thing, lens
inventory.proposed_calculation: d_needed = 1649.4 x (eye - ground) / ((target - 0.5) x 1920). Target 0.72, eye 1.7 m: 6.6 m (7.2 m if the thing stands on a road 0.14 m lower). Put the composed spot so the nearest story thing's front foot is at d_needed, but no nearer than the figure minimum; plate spot = composed spot + slide length.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py's story_reaches_down reports it after a Blender run (film kit only); nothing places the camera.
inventory.llm_tip: Work out the camera distance from 'nearest story thing's feet at 0.70 to 0.72 down' before building; a bare floor in the lower third is the commonest failure.

inventory.name: Rule 7 check: some story thing reaches 0.70 down
inventory.how_found: Round 4 critic: 'the shot checker's main rule passes everywhere; it does not measure any of the above' (rule 7 never tested). Round 5 added it with a reach and a no-reach test file.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: check file key story_reaches_down = 0.70 in every Works check file; fails with a fix in metres.
inventory.computable_from: check file plus shot facts
inventory.proposed_calculation: Turn it on by default (0.70) in every new check file; add a pre-render version using frame_geometry on the 3D bounding boxes.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in the film kit's check_shot.py, opt-in only. The plugin kit's check_shot.py lacks it.
inventory.llm_tip: Always put story_reaches_down 0.70 into a new check file; passing the main rule alone does not mean the frame is full.

inventory.name: Raised eye height for the overview shot
inventory.how_found: Round 3 compared W3 eye heights 4.6, 5.5 and 6.5 m with the shot checker. Round 3's check wanted the queue's tail in the bottom third; with the eye 4.6 m up it reached only 0.66. Round 4 raised it.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: W3 eye 5.6 m above the lane (end terrace on a 1 m raised footway); last man's feet 0.71 down while still 6.07 m from W1's camera. Lines meet on the wall between the gates (about halfway down).
inventory.evidence: assemble_works.py lines 158-164; round4-result.json set.summary 'W3's queue'; round3-result.json works.summary
inventory.computable_from: camera spot, the furthest-forward story thing, lens
inventory.proposed_calculation: eye = ground + (target - 0.5) x 1920 x d / 1649.4 for the nearest story element at depth d (target 0.70 to 0.75). Check the meeting point stays on the subject.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: For a 'bigger picture' view, raise the eye until the nearest story thing reaches the bottom third, not by tilting.

inventory.name: Painted figures seen from behind: never nearer than 6 m
inventory.how_found: Plan from the lens (a 1.75 m man at 6 m is about a quarter of the frame height). People test (round 1): men at 6.62 to 8.80 m, 347 to 453 px tall, read 'at once as working men' at phone size. Round 3 set every man at least 6.2 m from any camera that sees him.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Backs to the camera, at least 6 m from every camera spot that sees them (plate, composed, every slide frame). 1.75 m x 1649.4 / 6 = 481 px = 0.25 of the frame.
inventory.evidence: PLAN line 124, 1468-1469; round1-result.json built[1].tested table; round3-result.json works.summary 'The men'
inventory.computable_from: figure positions, all camera spots and slide paths
inventory.proposed_calculation: d_min = 1649.4 x 1.75 / (0.25 x 1920) = 6.0 m; for every figure and every camera position along each slide, assert depth >= 6.0 m; report the nearest.
inventory.already_automatic: No; a figure distance table was printed by a scratch script per round.
inventory.llm_tip: Keep painted people backs-to-camera and at least 6 m away, measured from every camera position including the end of the slide.

inventory.name: Head size decides painted or silhouette (faces)
inventory.how_found: Teaching critic T8: at 6.5 m a facing man's head is about 58 px and the painter would paint faces. Round 4 critic: workers inside the doorways at 16 to 19 m have heads of 20 to 24 px, too small for faces. Glasgow walkers at 50 m are about 56 px tall.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A figure that faces the camera or shows a lit profile is painted only if its head is about 24 px or less (about 16 m or further); otherwise it is a near-black own-surface silhouette (page 14 men at 6.5 m), or turned away.
inventory.computable_from: figure positions and facing, camera spots
inventory.proposed_calculation: head_px = 0.23 x 1649.4 / d. facing = dot(figure forward, direction to camera) > -0.2 (face or profile visible). If facing and head_px > 24: mark 'own-surface silhouette' or rotate away. Distance at 24 px = 15.8 m.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Faces appear when a painter sees a head over about 24 px turned toward the camera: either push such figures past about 16 m or keep them as dark silhouettes.

inventory.name: Crowd stands across the line of sight, not along it
inventory.how_found: Round 3's fix put the queue in single file along the kerb (1.1 to 1.3 m gaps). Round 4 critic: both cameras look up the lane, so the file was seen end-on: 7 men one dark column in W3, a black mass in W1, No. 2's 8 men a black wedge (2.1% in the bottom-left quarter, limit 1%). Round 4's layout_search tried about 50,000 jittered layouts. Round 5 rebuilt as a crowd at the gate. W4 earlier: from the outer hinge post the 8 men stood behind one another and read as one man.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A loose crowd two deep across the gateway, backs to the lane, 0.3 to 0.5 m between shoulders, back row about 0.8 m behind the front row, each turned 4 to 16 deg, scaled 0.96 to 1.04 so heads differ; drums in front of the crowd's end so nobody stands in front of them from W1 or W3. Rule: never line figures up along a camera's ray.
inventory.evidence: SCRATCH/redesign/round5-set/tools/new_layout.txt; assemble_works.py lines 898-958; round4-result.json critique.findings[1]; round3-result.json works.summary 'W4'; SCRATCH/redesign/round4-set/tools/layout_search3.py
inventory.computable_from: figure positions and sizes, camera spots
inventory.proposed_calculation: (1) angle between each camera's view direction and the group's long axis >= 60 deg; (2) project each figure as a cylinder (r 0.28 m, h 1.74 m); for each pair whose vertical spans overlap, require a horizontal gap >= 15 px or an overlap >= 15 px (never 0 to 15 px 'just touching'); (3) every head's top clear of the shoulder line of the man in front by >= 0.5 head; search small jitters (0.1 m, +-15 deg) and keep the best.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py rule 4 reports edges just touching after a render; nothing proposes positions (layout search was scratch only).
inventory.llm_tip: A queue seen from its end reads as one man; spread waiting people sideways across the view, two deep, with gaps between heads.

inventory.name: Head-back darker than the coat (no bald heads)
inventory.how_found: Round 1 check: at plate size the men from behind had pale bald-looking heads (hand-on-bar head 80/54/35 vs coat 39/25/14); the figures helper had judged 'from behind: yes'. Round 2 cast rays and read pixels: hair present but shiny, reflecting sky and lamps (22 to 25 vs cap and coat 7 to 12).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Matt dark hair covering back and sides from under the cap into the collar; turned-up collars or high mufflers so no neck shows; caps 1.5 cm lower. Measured after: head band 12 vs coat 25, 15 vs 28 (head darker than coat).
inventory.evidence: round1-result.json checked.findings[0]; round2-result.json figures.summary and tested; KIT/paper-film/blender/figures/build_figures.py
inventory.computable_from: the plate and each figure's outline from shot facts
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each figure seen from behind: mean luminance of the band just below the cap vs mean of the coat inside its outline in the plate; flag if head >= coat. Also add a contact-sheet view lit from the camera's side (the light that showed the fault).
inventory.already_automatic: No (figure_sheet.py got the extra lamp-lit back view, but no measure).
inventory.llm_tip: Check the back of every head in the plate at full size: if it is paler than the coat, the painter will paint a face or a dummy.

inventory.name: Film grade turns dark cloth red: pick cloth colours after the grade
inventory.how_found: Round 2 check sampled the film: tan coats in the plate came out crimson (26/1/0, hue pure red). Round 3 found why: the film's grade turns anything darker than about 28/255 black, removing green and blue. Re-coloured, re-filmed a still and sampled again.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Use slate grey or grey cloth that reads dull grey-brown in the warm plate (about 46/39/32); on film it samples 27/16/3 and 30/16/3 (olive brown, hue about 30 deg), not red (was 19/1/1 and 23/2/1).
inventory.evidence: round2-result.json checked.findings[3]; round3-result.json fixes.summary 'The two right-hand men's coats'
inventory.computable_from: plate colours and the stage's tone curve (cinema-stage.js grade)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Run every figure's (and every large prop's) mean plate colour through the stage's grade function; flag if the graded hue moves more than 25 deg or lands in 345-15 deg (red) / party or chain hues with saturation > 0.5; suggest the plate colour whose graded result is the wanted hue.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Judge colours of dark things on a filmed still, not the plate: the grade crushes dark browns to red.

inventory.name: Profile faces turned away from the fire
inventory.how_found: Round 2: the stooped and arms-folded men faced the fire, so a lit cheek and ear showed. Round 3 turned them 18 deg (first try went the wrong way and showed more face). Round 4 bowed the stooped man's head 22 deg further and turned it 24 deg so his face is under the peak.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Turn heads 15 to 24 deg away from the strongest light so the camera sees mostly the back of the head; bow the head of a man leaning over a fire; stooped man stands 0.1 m off the drum (coat 0.14 m away), hands 13 to 15 cm above the rim.
inventory.evidence: round2-result.json checked.findings[4]; round3-result.json fixes.summary; round4-result.json set.summary 'The stooped man's head'; assemble_works.py lines 919-921
inventory.computable_from: figure head positions and facing, light positions, camera
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each head: lit_face = max(0, dot(face normal, direction to the nearest strong light)) x light strength / d^2; visible_face = dot(face normal, direction to camera). If both > 0.2, rotate the head away from the light in 5 deg steps until visible_face < 0.1.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: A fire-lit cheek in profile becomes a painted face: turn the head away from the fire, not just away from the camera.

inventory.name: Edge light so dark figures separate
inventory.how_found: Round 4 critic: the waiting men were pure black with no edge light, so neither viewer nor painter could separate them. Round 5 added rim lights reaching only the men. People test (painted, log 34): figure-to-surround contrast ratio about 2.2 painted, 2.98 as silhouettes.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Two rim lights per crowd, linked to the men only, no shadows: a cool yard light 220 W (colour 0.55/0.68/1.0) 1.2 m to the side and 1.6 m behind the gate, 2.4 m up; a warm lamp light 90 W (1.0/0.72/0.45) 1.9 m to the other side, 2.9 m up.
inventory.computable_from: plate, figure outlines
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each figure, measure the edge contrast (mean gradient across its outline) and the luminance ratio to a 20 px ring around it; require ratio >= 2 and a visible light edge on at least one side; if not, place a rim light behind the figure relative to the camera with light linking to the figures only.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Dark people against a dark street need a thin rim of light from behind, linked so it lights only them.

inventory.name: Show people at work where the story says 'flat out' or 'they go in'
inventory.how_found: Round 4 critic: both lit doorways showed an empty cream room; the men vanished at 'go' but never appeared inside; the flat-out factory read 'open late or deserted'. Round 5 added workers.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Two dark figures at the machines inside each lit doorway (No. 2 in every No. 2 plate, one in the slowed state; No. 1 only in the working and men-gone plates), from behind or side-on, cloth 0.025/0.024/0.026, 17 m or more from every camera (heads 20 to 24 px), spill lights linked to skip them so they stay dark against the lit back wall.
inventory.evidence: round5-set/tools/new_layout.txt WORKERS; assemble_works.py lines 959-973 and 1206-1212; round4-result.json critique.findings[0]
inventory.computable_from: script (which states need 'busy' or 'going in'), scene
inventory.proposed_calculation: From the script's state list, any state described as busy or working must contain at least one figure inside a lit area of the frame; check its projected head <= 24 px and its luminance below the lit wall behind it by a ratio of at least 3.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: If the words say people are working, show a dark figure at a machine; an empty lit room reads as deserted.

inventory.name: Keep figures out of live smoke and off props
inventory.how_found: Round 1 check: the brazier's live smoke drifted in front of the hand-on-bar man, making him a see-through grey ghost. Round 2 moved him off the kerb line; smoke drift 0.9 kept. The stooped man's hands rested on the hot rim; lifted.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No figure inside a live smoke column's screen path; hands at least 10 to 15 cm off a hot rim; stooped figure 0.1 m further than his pose's reach.
inventory.evidence: round1-result.json checked.findings[9]; round2-result.json figures.summary 'The hand-on-bar man'; assemble_works.py lines 919-921
inventory.computable_from: smoke emitter positions and wind, figure boxes, camera
inventory.proposed_calculation: Trace each smoke emitter's puff path on screen (see smoke calculator) and flag any figure box overlapped by puffs with opacity > 0.2.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Trace where the live smoke goes on screen before placing people; a man inside the smoke reads as a ghost.

inventory.name: Nothing round sits above a collar (things that read as people)
inventory.how_found: Round 1: a hung jacket with the cap above the collar read as a headless or hunched man; round 2 hung the cap on its own nail (reads as a disc from the side); round 3 collar and slumped shoulders, cap turned; round 4 critic still read a flat disc; set helper turned it 30 deg.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Cap on its own nail 0.4 m right and 0.2 m lower than the jacket's, its top 16 cm below the collar, turned 30 deg so crown and peak both show; jacket with collar and slumped shoulders; nothing round above a garment's collar.
inventory.evidence: round1-result.json checked.findings[3]; round2-result.json props_fixes.summary; round3-result.json fixes.summary; assemble_works.py line 1123 (CAP_TURN = -30.0)
inventory.computable_from: prop layout
inventory.proposed_calculation: Flag any roughly round object (aspect 0.7 to 1.3) whose bottom lies within 0.25 m above a hung garment's top; render a check from the shot's real camera at its real distance.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: A hung coat with anything round above it becomes a person to the painter; hang the hat beside it, turned so its peak shows.

inventory.name: Painted figures keep their outlines (people test result)
inventory.how_found: Paid people test (log 34, about 85 cents): plate painted by Flux 3 edit, then measured each figure's outline against the plate's (shape-match and outline distance per figure).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Near men: painted outline matched the plate's at IoU 0.88 to 0.92, median outline error 1 px, 91 to 99.9% of outline points within 3 px; small walkers 63 to 99% within 3 px. Silhouette version contrast ratio 2.98 against 2.2 painted.
inventory.computable_from: plate outlines (shot facts) and the painting
inventory.proposed_calculation: After every painting: per figure, chamfer distance from plate outline to painting edges; flag a figure if within-3-px share < 0.90 (near) or < 0.70 (far) or IoU < 0.85, meaning the painter moved, added or lost it.
inventory.already_automatic: No (scratch scripts).
inventory.llm_tip: After a painting comes back, measure every figure's outline against the plate; a figure that moved more than 3 px has been redrawn.

inventory.name: Letter height needed for a reading distance
inventory.how_found: Measured or worked out in every round: round 1 film-distance renders; round 2 measured props from the saved models (bank letters 0.2 m, not 0.29); round 3 resized the bank sign; T12 in the plan; round 4 critic's W4 target.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: px = letter_m x 1649.4 / d. Seen: 14 px (No. 1/No. 2 boards in W3) 'tiny on a phone'; 15 to 17 px (BANK 0.2 m at 20 to 22 m) marginal; 24 to 29 px (BANK 0.305 m) 'easy to read on a phone'; 26 px (4 cm headline at 2.5 m) too small for a headline; about 40 px the plan's test; about 60 px (0.1 m bill letters at about 2.75 m) readable on a phone; WAGES 1.8 cm = 5 px at 6 m, readable only within about 3 m; W4 target WAGES >= 25 px. Placard 0.12 m at 7 m = 28 px; No. 1 board 41 px in W1.
inventory.evidence: round1-result.json built[0].tested 'Film-distance check'; round2-result.json props_fixes.summary and checked.findings (bank, wages); round3-result.json fixes.summary (0.305 m); round4-result.json critique.findings[9]; PLAN lines 272-274, 281, 392, 549-554, 1438
inventory.computable_from: sign positions, letter heights from lettering-sizes.json, camera spots, script (which words must be read)
inventory.proposed_calculation: letter_m_needed = target_px x d / 1649.4 (target 25 px to be readable, 40 to 60 px for a headline the viewer must read). For every lettered prop and every view that shows it, print px and flag words below 16 px that the script needs read (then a typed label must carry them).
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: the prop builder writes lettering-sizes.json and index.json letter heights; no per-view pixel calculator.
inventory.llm_tip: Size every sign from its camera distance: letters need about 25 px on the 1920 frame to read on a phone; below about 16 px let a typed label carry the word.

inventory.name: Words meant to be read face the camera
inventory.how_found: T12: a headline at 4 cm letters unreadable; replaced by a newspaper bill in a wire stand. Kitchen letter: lying flat it shrinks to a third of its height, so propped against a mug facing us. Round 2: WAGES lying flat was 1 to 2 px tall foreshortened; round 3 stood it on edge leaning back 14 deg.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Lettering to be read stands upright facing the camera (lean at most about 15 deg); foreshortening factor = sin(angle between the sign's plane and the line of sight).
inventory.evidence: PLAN lines 391-393, 504-506, 1438; round2-result.json checked.findings[5]; round3-result.json fixes.summary 'New prop, tin-mug-and-wages-envelope'
inventory.computable_from: sign normal, camera spot
inventory.proposed_calculation: effective_px = letter px x |dot(sign normal, direction to camera)|; flag if < 0.85 for must-read words.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Prop up any paper the viewer must read so it faces the lens; flat on a table it all but vanishes.

inventory.name: Lettered props in must_read so no fragments show
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: house fronts hid most drums ('SEL', 'DIE'; PETROL never showed). Round 4 critic: crates popped up behind the drums ('THI', 'UP'), W4 crate showed 'AY UP', W3 DIESEL read 'DIESE'. Drums and crates added to must_read; round 4 measured 0 to 2% of drum words hidden.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every lettered prop in a view goes in that view's must_read; 0% of a word's letters hidden or cut by the frame, at the plate spot and the composed spot; else move or turn it, or take it out of frame.
inventory.evidence: round3-result.json checked.findings[8]; round4-result.json critique.findings[5] and [9]; round4-result.json film.summary item 6; KIT/examples/inflation-chapter-2-newcomers/works-w1-working-shot-check.json must_read
inventory.computable_from: shot facts (ids render per lettering material), check file
inventory.proposed_calculation: Auto-fill must_read from every material named *-lettering / *-stencil visible in the view; occlusion share = hidden letter pixels / all letter pixels from the ids picture; fail above 0%; also test the plate frame edges.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py measures must_read occlusion and the 0.90 limit, but must_read is filled by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Put every lettered thing in must_read; a half-hidden word ('DIESE', 'AY UP') is worse than no word.

inventory.name: Turn round lettered props to face the camera
inventory.how_found: Round 1: each drum stencil wraps about 86 deg round the drum, so from a side angle the first or last letter turns away. Round 5 set turns per drum.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Turn each drum so its stencil's middle faces the camera: No. 1's PETROL +12 deg, DIESEL +8 deg; No. 2's mirrored (-12, -8).
inventory.evidence: round1-result.json built[0].summary 'The drums need turning'; round5-set/tools/new_layout.txt DRUM_SPOTS; assemble_works.py line 912
inventory.computable_from: prop position, stencil's facing at turn 0, camera spot
inventory.proposed_calculation: turn = atan2(cam_x - x, -(cam_y - y)) in the stencil's frame (stencil faces -y at 0); for several views pick the turn that maximises the minimum |cos| over the views that must read it.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Turn each drum or curved sign toward the camera that must read it, by the angle from the prop to the lens.

inventory.name: A sign the page does not mention must not be the loudest word
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: BANK (29 px, lit by a gas lamp) was the clearest word in W3 on pages that never mention a bank; boards about 14 px. Round 4 dimmed it to 0.3 (118 to 52 levels; No. 1 board 120): still 'easy to read' per critic. Round 5: 0.15 until page 9, then brightened with the window.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: BANK_SIGN.dim = 0.15 (board and lettering, own copy of the board paint) until its page; measured in film 57 vs 128 levels at 0.3.
inventory.evidence: KIT/paper-film/scenes/inflation-chapter-2-newcomers/works-effects.js lines 132-138; round3-result.json checked.findings[7]; round4-result.json critique.findings[14], pageFixes.summary, film.summary
inventory.computable_from: script word times (when a word is first said), own-surface signs and their brightness in the plate
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each page and view: list legible signs (px >= 20); for signs whose word is not in that page's narration, set dim = (0.4 x brightness of the least bright sign that is named) / own brightness, at most 0.3; undim on the first spoken use.
inventory.already_automatic: No (the dim value was tuned by hand).
inventory.llm_tip: Dim or hide any readable sign until the narration names it; viewers read the clearest word first.

inventory.name: Plank joints and stripes kept off letters
inventory.how_found: Round 1: plank joints ran through 'No. 1' like a strike-through. Round 2: three planks, a wide middle plank carries the lettering, joints 3 to 4 cm clear; painter and builder stop if a joint would cross a letter.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Board joints at least 3 to 4 cm clear of any letter; the build refuses otherwise.
inventory.computable_from: lettering-sizes.json (where letters fall) and board build constants
inventory.proposed_calculation: Compute joint lines from plank widths; assert min distance to every letter's box >= 0.03 m; else re-split planks.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in build_chapter_2_props.py / paint_chapter_2_pictures.py (they stop); not in the plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: Keep every line on a sign (joints, borders) clear of the letters, or the word reads as crossed out.

inventory.name: Boards seen from behind carry their lettering too
inventory.how_found: Round 4 critic: from inside the yard (W4) the back of No. 2's board was a big blank plank in the top left.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Any board visible from both sides is lettered on both, or turned.
inventory.computable_from: views list, sign normals
inventory.proposed_calculation: For every sign and view: if dot(sign front normal, direction to camera) < 0 and the sign is visible, require a back lettering material or flag.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check each sign from every camera that sees it; a blank back is a blank plank sign on screen.

inventory.name: Only narrated figures on set; scan all lettering for digits
inventory.how_found: Plan's lettering rules and Traps; round 2 prop checker read every .glb directly ('only digits are No. 1 and No. 2'); round 4 film helper's words_check.py compared all 29 typed lines with the timeline (0 problems).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No numerals in the set except 'No. 1' and 'No. 2'; no prices, keypads, door, lane or close numbers, dates, phone numbers; typed words only short forms of what is said on that page.
inventory.evidence: PLAN lines 181-191 and 1454-1457; round2-result.json props_fixes.tested; round4-result.json film.tested 'Words'
inventory.computable_from: lettering strings in the prop index, page files' text, narration word times
inventory.proposed_calculation: Collect every lettering string (index.json, lettering-sizes.json) and every typed string in the page files; flag any digit sequence or number word not spoken on that page; flag any typed line whose content words are not in that page's narration.
inventory.already_automatic: No (scratch words_check.py and a scratch prop checker).
inventory.llm_tip: Before building, list every word and number that will be on screen and tick each against the narration.

inventory.name: Paint out baked labels in downloaded models
inventory.how_found: Round 1 check zoomed into the hand truck's texture: a modern maker's sticker baked in (pixels about 800-850 across, 985-1020 down). Round 2 added a paint-out step; also Poly Haven assets dropped for lettering (crate 01, generator, cash register, suitcase stickers).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: PAINT_OUT box per asset in the choices list, filled from nearby paint in colour, roughness and relief maps, saved lossless (0 pixels changed outside the patch).
inventory.evidence: round1-result.json checked.findings[4]; round2-result.json props_fixes.summary 'Hand truck'; PLAN lines 1417 (F11), 1177-1183
inventory.computable_from: downloaded texture maps
inventory.proposed_calculation: Run text detection (high-contrast small strokes, OCR) on every downloaded colour map; list candidate boxes for a paint-out; reject assets with lettering on large areas.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: convert_poly_haven.py paints out a box given by hand (film kit only).
inventory.llm_tip: Open every downloaded texture at full size and look for stickers, brands and digits before using the model.

inventory.name: Gate lamp off the pier's face
inventory.how_found: Round 3 flagged and round 4 critic measured: the gate lamp on the pier's front made the quiet side's pier the brightest thing (0.75 to 0.82 at 0.31 across, 0.52 down); gate held 0% of the brightest parts, 0.88 x average (rule 1.8); lit-from-below -0.02 (need 0.10). Round 5 moved and halved it.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Lamp bracket on the pier's inner face 0.1 m in from its front edge, foot 2.2 m (glass about 3.3 m), 7 W (half of 14 W); light 0.2 m toward the lane from the glass. Round 5 check: lit-from-below 0.25 (pass).
inventory.evidence: assemble_works.py lines 856-859 and 843-846; round4-result.json critique.findings[4]; round5-set/checks/w1-quiet-d/light/report.md line 79
inventory.computable_from: light positions, surface normals, camera
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each light: irradiance on camera-facing surfaces = P x cos(theta) / r^2; flag if any non-subject surface facing the camera receives more than the subject; propose moving the light behind the plane of the surface it over-lights (inner face) and scaling P by (subject target / current).
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py names the light that most lights an over-bright prop, after a render; nothing moves lights.
inventory.llm_tip: A lamp on the face of a wall lights the wall, not the subject; mount it on the inner face or above the subject.

inventory.name: Lights reach only what they are for (light linking)
inventory.how_found: Round 5: the brazier standing against the gate lit the inner pier's face into the brightest patch in W1; fire made to skip its own drum and the works wall. Round 4 had 110 W against the outer pier.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Brazier fire 80 W, linked to skip its drum and the works wall; rim lights reach only the men; doorway spill lights skip the workers inside.
inventory.computable_from: light list, story groups from the check file
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each light, list the 3 surfaces it lights most from the camera's view; if any is outside the check file's story and subject groups and brighter than the subject, add it to that light's skip list.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: dressing.light_reaches exists; choosing what to skip is by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Give every story light a list of what it may light; the commonest fault is a warm light turning a nearby wall into the brightest thing.

inventory.name: A dark subject stands against a pale background
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: the shut, chained gate hardly showed (dark bars on a dark doorway). Round 4 added a faint cool yard light; round 5 raised it from 260 to 900 W. Round 5 checks still found the gate 0.87 x average brightness and 8% of the brightest parts (need 1.8 and 40%): the 'subject is brightest' rule cannot hold for a dark iron gate.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No. 1's yard: a cool light 900 W (0.55/0.68/1.0), no shadows, at 3.6 m behind the wall, 5.2 m up, reaching only the yard's mill front, doors and setts; doorway dark until 'go'. Judge a dark subject by its silhouette contrast, not its brightness.
inventory.evidence: assemble_works.py lines 1148 and 1220-1221; round3-result.json checked.findings[9]; round5-set/checks/w1-quiet-d/light/report.md lines 21-23
inventory.computable_from: plate, subject outline
inventory.proposed_calculation: If the subject's own albedo is dark (iron, silhouettes), mark it 'subject_dark' in the check file and replace rule 5's brightness test with: mean luminance of a 30 px band behind the subject >= 2.5 x the subject's mean; place a backlight until it holds.
inventory.already_automatic: No; the checker still reports a failure that cannot be fixed by brightening.
inventory.llm_tip: Dark iron, dark coats and silhouettes are shown by lighting what is behind them, not by lighting them.

inventory.name: Only a few lights cast shadows
inventory.how_found: Round 3: with every light casting shadows a Works plate took about 25 minutes; men's long shadows made the state-picture mask 42%. Turning off shadows except the fire, the lit doorways and the sky light cut it to about 6 minutes and the mask to 5 to 9%.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Shadows only from the fire, the yards' lit doorways and the sky; lamps and lantern no shadows; figures cast no long shadows (visible_shadow False) and each has a small soft foot patch (two see-through ovals).
inventory.evidence: assemble_works.py lines 984-1047 and 1504; round3-result.json works.summary 'Speed' and 'State pictures'
inventory.computable_from: light list, figure list
inventory.proposed_calculation: Default every light to no shadows except those named as the shot's key light(s); set figures' visible_shadow off and add a foot patch sized 0.5 x 0.35 m under each.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Let only the key light cast shadows and give people foot shadows instead of long ones; plates draw four times faster and state changes stay small.

inventory.name: Exposure per view from how dark its plate is
inventory.how_found: Round 3 pages: W1 is the darkest view and the stage's tone curve halves a dark picture: 18 levels on screen against 37 to 43 for the other views; the waiting men were near-black on near-black. Raised exposure for the whole shot. Round 3 check warned the brick near the lamp turned bright orange at the cut from W3.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: W1 exposure 1.6 (others 1.0), constant across the shot; to be re-judged once the painting replaces the plate (the notice corner's painting came out brighter than its plate).

inventory.proposed_calculation: exposure = clamp(target_mean / graded_mean(plate), 1.0, 1.8) with target about 38 levels on screen (the other views' mean), computed per view from the actual picture in use; recompute when the painting arrives.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Measure each view's on-screen mean brightness after the grade; a view under about 25 levels needs more exposure, set for the whole shot.

inventory.name: Warm light share and where it falls
inventory.how_found: Round 4 critic W4: warm light covered 23.6% (guide 3%), top third 0.47 to 0.51 (limit 0.36). Round 4 set W2's new beam made 4.9%; round 5 W2 6.6%, W1 0.2%.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Warm light 1.5 to 3% of the frame, most of it round the story props; top third brightness at most 0.36; turn yard lights down to one pool.

inventory.llm_tip: Shorten a warm light's reach rather than its strength when it spreads; keep warm light to 1.5 to 3% of the frame.

inventory.name: Telling-apart features stay pale against the sky
inventory.how_found: Round 2 check: from street level No. 2's chimneys came out dark red-brown against the dusk (tops 15 levels vs sky 75) and seemed to rise out of No. 1's roof, so No. 1 looked like it had three chimneys. Round 3 made them pale buff with a little self-glow.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No. 2's chimneys tint 1.0/0.95/0.84 over white sandstone, sooted only near the cap, a small emissive glow on the lane-facing sides; measured 70 to 116 in W1 and 105 to 134 in W3 vs No. 1's about 10. Round 2 factories helper: at phone size the factories are told apart more by count (one vs two), tone (dark vs pale) and the tank than by round vs square.

inventory.proposed_calculation: For each identifying feature, measure its mean luminance vs the sky band behind it and vs the other factory's same feature in every view; require a difference of at least 40 levels and the planned order (No. 1 dark, No. 2 pale).
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Tell two places apart by count and light-vs-dark first; shape differences vanish at phone size.

inventory.name: Lit glass glows warm, not white
inventory.how_found: Round 2 factories helper: lit glass glowed white, dark glass caught lamps and looked lit; lowered glow and dulled the dark glass. Round 3 check: open doorway's inside read near white.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: LIT_GLOW = 1.4 for lit window glass (pit village's 4 used much darker pictures); dark glass dull, showing the dusk sky.
inventory.evidence: works_kit.py lines 59-60 and 194-213; round2-result.json factories.tested 'Earlier fixes'
inventory.computable_from: plate
inventory.proposed_calculation: Measure each lit window group's mean colour; flag if luminance > 230 or saturation < 0.25 (white); flag dark glass brighter than 1.5 x the wall around it.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Lit windows should read warm amber, never white; check the brightest pane in the plate.

inventory.name: Fal painting price on the day
inventory.how_found: Plan: fal's price list said 2.4 US cents a megapixel and log 32's 20 to 45 cents for two showed input pictures are charged too, so 25 cents a painting. People test ledger (log 34): 4.8 cents a megapixel on the day, about 85 cents for two.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: cost = rate x (megapixels returned + megapixels of every picture sent). 2k return 1504 x 2672 = 4.0 MP; plate 1536 x 2730 = 4.2 MP; style picture 768 x 1368 = 1.05 MP. At 4.8 c/MP: about 44 c with a style picture, about 39 c without. Sending the style picture at about 1 MP saved about 7 c at 2.4 c/MP.
inventory.computable_from: prices (fetched live), planned paintings list with their input pictures
inventory.proposed_calculation: Before each paid batch: read today's rate (fal get_pricing); sum per request rate x (W_out x H_out + sum W_in x H_in)/1e6; add repaint reserve; refuse if over the user's line.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check today's price per megapixel before every paid batch and count the pictures you send, not only the one returned.

inventory.name: Budget lines and reserves
inventory.how_found: Plan's money table after the feasibility critic.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Repaint reserve about one in two paintings (lesson 97: Flux's strength varies); up to 4 Nano Banana Pro sketches at 15 c only where the checker can't settle a view; narration about 6,300 characters about US$1.10; re-record reserve one page US$0.30; ask per batch; stay under the user's line (US$12 of US$20).
inventory.computable_from: plan's paintings list, narration character count, prices
inventory.proposed_calculation: total = paintings x per-painting cost x 1.5 + sketches x 0.15 + narration_chars x price_per_char + one page re-record; split into batches by place; print before asking.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Budget one repaint for every two paintings and ask for each paid batch separately.

inventory.name: Painting size and line-up
inventory.how_found: People test ledger: Flux returned 1504 x 2672 at '2k'; resized to the plate and lined up with align_painting.py against the props' outlines from shot_facts.py at the plate's own lens (64.4). Log 32 found 0.65% stretch and 3 px.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Resize to the plate (1536 x 2730), then align: stretch 1.0010 and shift +1.0, +0.5 px; outline agreement 0.874 before, 0.903 after. The behind painting aligned with --against the lined-up painting (0.999). Keep the painting lossless (PNG).
inventory.computable_from: plate, painting, shot facts outlines
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already automatic: align_painting.py; make it a required step that refuses to continue if agreement after < 0.85 or stretch > 1%.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes (align_painting.py in film kit and plugin kit); not enforced.
inventory.llm_tip: Line up every painting with its plate before any other step; Flux shifts and stretches slightly.

inventory.name: Painter prompt clauses for people and live effects
inventory.how_found: Plan's painter words; round 1 helper's predictions of painter faults (faces, uniforms, merged walkers, painted flames doubling the live ones, dropped shadows); people test prompt as sent.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Say: keep every figure exactly where and as it is, same number, size, pose, outline; no faces (only dark shadow under the cap); not photographs, statues, dummies or toys; never add flames, sparks, smoke, steam, glows, halos, puddles, new signs, new or longer shadows; thin parts stay thin; where two things meet keep each edge, never join them. For the behind painting: remove the people and their shadows, continue what is behind them, add nothing.
inventory.evidence: people-test-paintings.json paintings[0].prompt and paintings[1].prompt; PLAN lines 145-146; round1-result.json built[1].summary 'What the painter will likely get wrong'
inventory.computable_from: the plate's list of figures (count, poses), the page's live effects list
inventory.proposed_calculation: Generate the prompt from the shot facts: count figures by kind and pose ('five men: four seen from behind ...'), list thin props, list where live effects are drawn (so the prompt forbids painting them), list lights to keep.
inventory.already_automatic: No (prompts written by hand; paper-look 04 Painting prompts has general rules).
inventory.llm_tip: Count and describe every person in the prompt and forbid anything the film draws live (flames, smoke), or it will appear twice.

inventory.name: Second paintings differ everywhere: swap only inside a mask
inventory.how_found: Round 1 check: the free test swapped the whole picture; with two real paintings every brushstroke would change at the cut. People test paintings: the two paintings differ by 8.5 levels on average outside the mask.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Never cut to a whole second painting; a state picture = main painting outside the mask + second painting inside it. Paid test mask: 38.3% fully plus 8.2% partly.
inventory.computable_from: two paintings, two plates
inventory.proposed_calculation: make_state_picture.py (below); assert the cut swaps no pixel outside the mask.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in the film kit (make_state_picture.py); not in the plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: For a change on a word, swap only the area that changes; a whole new painting flickers every brushstroke.

inventory.name: State-picture mask thresholds
inventory.how_found: Round 2 compared thresholds 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14, alone and with a lower threshold for faint smooth changes, and mapped what each left behind; measured render noise (0.2 to 0.6) and JPEG noise (99th percentile 2 after blur).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Blur both plates 2 px; difference = largest colour channel; changed if > 6 levels, or if the 10 px-blurred difference > 3 (faint shadows). Clear specks, widen 12 px, soften 5 px, outline widen 6 px (for a 1536-wide plate; scales with width). 6 alone left 6.8% of the frame > 3 levels off; 10 alone left 0.48% > 8; chosen settings leave 0.04% > 4. Tool warns if a threshold is under 3 x measured noise.
inventory.computable_from: plate and helper plate, figure outlines
inventory.proposed_calculation: Keep as is; also print the swap area at 4/6/8 and faint 2/3/4 for the view so the choice is visible.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes (make_state_picture.py, film kit only).
inventory.llm_tip: Use threshold 6 and faint 3, then look at the mask picture before trusting it.

inventory.name: State pictures are lossless and read back exactly
inventory.how_found: Round 2 check: writing the state picture as JPEG 93 moved the whole frame 0.48 levels on average and up to 9 outside the mask.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Write PNG or lossless WebP only (JPEG refused); read back; largest difference from the main painting where the mask is zero must be 0 levels (stops otherwise).
inventory.evidence: make_state_picture.py docstring lines 41-46; round2-result.json checked.findings[8]; round3-result.json fixes.summary
inventory.computable_from: the files
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already automatic.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes (film kit only).
inventory.llm_tip: Never save a state picture or a painting used for one as JPEG.

inventory.name: Cut or blend, from the size of the change
inventory.how_found: Swap areas measured every round: people test 42% (long shadows); Works round 3 men gone 6.5 to 8%, slowed 5.2 to 6.5%, working 41 to 50%; round 4 men gone 9.3%, slowed 8.5%, behind 5.6%, working 75.7% once No. 1's beam lit the lane.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A time cut where the mask is small (about 10% or less: the men going); a blend (0.8 to 1.5 s) where it is large (windows lighting, 41 to 76%). States reached by a cut keep the spill lights of the state before, so plates differ only where the men stood.
inventory.evidence: round3-result.json works.summary and NOT DONE 'working state picture swaps 41%'; round4-result.json set.summary 'State pictures'; assemble_works.py lines 222-230 (STATES note on spill)
inventory.computable_from: plate pairs per change, script events
inventory.proposed_calculation: area = mask share; if area <= 0.12 -> time cut; else blend over 0.8 s + 0.7 s x (area/0.75); warn if a cut is asked for over 0.12. Check that lights not tied to the change have identical settings in both plates.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Cut when only a small part of the frame changes; blend when the light over much of it changes; keep every other light identical between the two plates.

inventory.name: One helper plate per separately timed change
inventory.how_found: Round 3 effects: 'go' needed W1 'men gone, windows still dark' or the mask couldn't keep the windows dark until 'start'. Round 3 pages: No. 1's doorway lit as soon as the slide started (behind picture had it lit) -> 'quiet, no men' plate. Round 4 pages: one slowed picture held both the dark windows and the men, so a window blend on 'slows' would fade the men in as ghosts -> needs a windows-only slowed picture.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every change that happens on its own word needs its own plate pair: men gone (windows dark), working (windows lit), quiet-no-men (behind picture), slowed-windows-only, slowed-with-men.
inventory.evidence: round3-result.json effects.summary 'One more helper plate'; round3-result.json pages.summary item 2; round4-result.json pageFixes.summary 'One thing page 12 will need'
inventory.computable_from: script events (state changes and their words) per view
inventory.proposed_calculation: From the page events, list per view the ordered state changes; each distinct (view, state after change k) needs a plate; derive the plate list and the state-picture commands automatically; flag a state change that bundles two changes timed on different words.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: List every change on its own word and give each its own plate; one plate holding two changes makes the earlier one ghost in.

inventory.name: Behind picture is the same state as the main picture
inventory.how_found: Round 3 pages: during page 3's slide No. 1's doorway lit up as soon as the camera moved, long before 'go', because the behind picture came from the working plate.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The behind picture (shown where near things stood once the camera moves) is made from a plate of the same state with only the near things left out ('quiet, no men'); swap area 5.6 to 5.7%.
