inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Make the behind picture from the same state as the main one, minus the near things, or hidden parts change early.

inventory.name: Time cut is the default; fade only as fallback
inventory.how_found: Plan T9; round 3 and 4 tested the go=swing fallback: men see-through for about a second while fading.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Default: a time cut on the spoken word to the state picture; fallback: gate swings in 0.8 s and men fade in 1.2 s inside the swing (two set draws). A state changes only while the camera holds; cards may change during a slide.
inventory.evidence: PLAN lines 132-143 and 1467; round4-result.json pageFixes.summary item 5
inventory.computable_from: script events, camera moves
inventory.proposed_calculation: Reject any state change scheduled inside a slide's time span; schedule cuts on the named word's start time.
inventory.already_automatic: No (camera_audit.py checks the camera, not state timing).
inventory.llm_tip: People vanish by a cut on the word, never by a fade, and only while the camera is still.

inventory.name: Wind blows across the view
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: smoke hidden under words. Round 4: wind (0.3, -0.05, -0.95) blew almost straight away from all three cameras; worked out with smoke_path.py: over a puff's life No. 2's plume moved only from 0.625 across, 0.237 down to 0.748, 0.309; puffs up to 13 m wide piled up and read as rings and a hook. Round 5 drew it with and without focus blur (rings the same) and traced the new path with smoke_trace.py.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: WIND = (-0.85, -0.12, -0.5) normalised (three.js axes), the same on every page: across the views, a little away, sinking. In W3 No. 2's plumes run left at 0.24 to 0.29 down, under the lower rule card (ends 0.236), fading by 0.45 across before No. 1's chimney (0.375 across); in W1/W2 they run along the top for about a quarter of the width.
inventory.computable_from: chimney-top markers (works-shot.json), camera spots, title card boxes, smoke settings
inventory.proposed_calculation: Wind horizontal direction = the unit vector most perpendicular to all views' look directions (sign toward the side with room); then trace puff centres p(age) = top + WIND x drift x k^1.25 + up x rise x k^0.75 (k = age/life) through the projector; require on-screen path length >= 0.15 of the frame width, path clear of title cards and >= 0.05 across short of any other factory's chimney; shorten drift or life until it holds.
inventory.already_automatic: No (scratch smoke_path.py and smoke_trace.py).
inventory.llm_tip: Never blow smoke along the camera's line of sight; trace the plume on screen in every view before filming.

inventory.name: Smoke look: colour, mouth, thickness
inventory.how_found: Round 3: smoke too pale (stills); round 4 critic: pale grey on dark sky read as glow, blob floating detached above No. 1's chimney; round 5 tuned.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: heavy: count 44, life 7 s, rise 0.6 m, drift 16 m, mouth 2 s at 1.9 m, size 3.4 to 9 m, opacity 0.95, fade 1.8, colour 100/92/84; working: 36 puffs, drift 15, mouth 1.7, colour 104/96/88; thin: 14 puffs, opacity 0.5. Brownish grey about 90 to 100 levels.
inventory.computable_from: chimney mouth size from the model, sky colour in the plate
inventory.proposed_calculation: mouth size = chimney top diameter x 1.0 to 1.1; colour = sky colour mixed toward warm grey so luminance difference to sky is 20 to 40 levels (dark against a light sky, light-brown against dusk); count = life x 6 for heavy.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Start puffs at the chimney's own width for the first 2 seconds so the plume is attached, and use a brownish grey, not white.

inventory.name: Chimney tops must not sit in the words band
inventory.how_found: Round 2: from gate views only the top 8 to 9 m of each chimney showed and tops fell at 0.07 to 0.14 down, inside the band kept for words. Round 3 check worked out the fix: 15 m further back or about 20 m tall puts them near 0.18 to 0.25 down in W2 and 0.28 to 0.34 in W3. Round 2: a full-height mill 8 m behind the wall hid most of a 25 m chimney 35 m back; mills kept to 2 storeys (eaves 7.8 m), measured by ray casts.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: down_top = 0.5 - (h_top - eye) x 1649.4 / (d x 1920); keep it below the title band (>= 0.24) or put words beside it, not over it; something tall in front (mill eaves) must not hide the identifying feature: visible chimney length W3 12 to 13 m.
inventory.evidence: round2-result.json factories.summary 'A conflict in the plan'; round3-result.json checked.findings[2]; round2-result.json checked.findings[0]
inventory.computable_from: model heights and positions, camera spots, title zone
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each view and marker: compute down_top; if < title_zone bottom + 0.02, solve for the height or distance that gives 0.24 (h = eye + (0.5 - 0.24) x 1920 x d / 1649.4) and report both; ray-cast from the camera to the marker to report visible length.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Project every tall landmark's top: anything above about 0.24 down collides with the typed words.

inventory.name: 'Busy' must change the windows by 15 levels or more
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check measured 'busy' (75.6 to 79.8 s): doorway 169.5 vs 169.4; No. 2's mill windows were not even in W2's frame. Round 4: windows 130 to 133 levels. Round 4 critic set the target; round 5 added a burst and measured with window_change.py.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Target: at least 15 levels change over the windows. BUSY = length 2.0 s, rise 0.25, fall 0.6, boost 3.0, dips 0.55, reach 2.75 m, band 1.1 m, shadow 0.75, doorway pulse 0.35, doorway dips 0.3; a dark band passes across the panes left to right.
inventory.evidence: works-effects.js lines 257-264; round3-result.json checked.findings[2]; round4-result.json critique.findings[8]; SCRATCH/redesign/round5-pages/tools/window_change.py
inventory.computable_from: two stills (before and during the event), window group outlines
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each 'brighter/busier' event, draw stills at the word and 0.6 s after; mean change over the window mask must be >= 15 levels; if not, raise boost by 15/measured.
inventory.already_automatic: No (scratch window_change.py).
inventory.llm_tip: Measure a visual event in two stills; under about 15 levels of change nobody sees it.

inventory.name: The window group that flickers must be in the frame
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: No. 2's mill windows were not in W2's frame at all (the gable had a loft door), so 'windows blazing' could not be seen. Round 4 replaced the loft door with three tall mill windows in the window groups.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each state's visible cue (lit windows, smoke, gate) must project inside the frame, below the title band, in every view that shows that state.
inventory.computable_from: window group bounding boxes, camera, script states per view
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each (view, state) list the cue objects; project their boxes; require at least 60% of each cue's area inside [0, 1] x [title bottom, 1] at the composed spot.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: For every word that changes a picture, check the thing that changes is actually inside that view's frame.

inventory.name: The picture must not contradict the card
inventory.how_found: Round 4 critic: the rule card says MOSTLY MORE THINGS MADE and draws a line to No. 1's chimney, but W3 still shows No. 1 cold with men waiting. Fixed by starting No. 1's working smoke on 'made'. Plan: Japan not shown as either factory; NOT THE ONLY REASON stays; 1915 window thins, not empties (T5, T19); lesson 83.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Whenever a card or line points at a thing, its state must match the claim at that moment (live effects can change without a redraw).
inventory.evidence: round4-result.json critique.findings[12]; works-effects.js lines 97-104; PLAN lines 1384, 1431, 1445
inventory.computable_from: page events (cards with targets), the states active at each time
inventory.proposed_calculation: For every pointer or label event, look up the target's state at that time and the claim's keyword (made, quiet, up); keep a small table of claims to required states; flag mismatches.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: For each card with a pointer, ask what the pointed-at thing is doing at that moment; if it contradicts the words, change the picture.

inventory.name: Words end exactly on a cut
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: words faded one frame before each cut (change 2.7 against a usual 0.5), so the cut took two steps. Round 4 added fadeOut 0; film measured the frame before each cut 0.39 to 0.41, the cut about 42 to 46.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: presence(..., fadeOut = 0) for every word, label, band and arrow that ends on a cut: whole until 'until', gone from it.
inventory.evidence: KIT/paper-film/scenes/graphics.js lines 21-28 and 112-113; round3-result.json checked.findings[16]; round4-result.json pageFixes.summary and film.tested
inventory.computable_from: page events and cut times
inventory.proposed_calculation: When an element's 'until' equals a cut or page-turn time (within one frame), set fadeOut 0 automatically.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes as an option in the film kit's graphics.js (must be set by hand); plugin kit's presence() lacks it.
inventory.llm_tip: Any word that lasts until a cut must not fade; set fadeOut 0 so the cut is one clean step.

inventory.name: Label reading time before a cut
inventory.how_found: Round 4 critic and film helper measured MACHINES: label words appear 0.3 to 0.55 s after the line starts; 'machines' at 54.17 s, words full at 54.70, cut at 55.10: readable about 0.4 to 0.45 s. Round 5 added wordsWithLine (words in at once, 0.12 s).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: readable = cut - (word time + delay); default delay 0.55 s, wordsWithLine 0.12 s; MACHINES then reads about 0.85 s. Aim for about 1 s or more.
inventory.evidence: graphics.js lines 105-118 and 156-158; page-3.js lines 110-116; round4-result.json critique.findings[7] and film.summary item 1
inventory.computable_from: narration word times, page cut times
inventory.proposed_calculation: For every label: readable = next_cut - (at + delay); if < 1.0 s use wordsWithLine; if still < 0.8 s move it to an earlier word in the clause or move the cut one word later.
inventory.already_automatic: No; option exists in the film kit only.
inventory.llm_tip: Count the seconds a label is fully readable before the next cut; under a second, bring its words in with the line or start it a word earlier.

inventory.name: A page's conclusion stays up at least 1.2 s
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: '-> PRICES UP' came on 'up' (106.48 s) and the cut was on 'Most' (107.15 s): 0.65 s, last frame already faded. Moved to 'prices' (105.96 s) with the arrow: about 1.2 s, full strength on the last frame.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Key conclusion visible at full strength for at least 1.2 s before a cut; start it on the first word of its clause.
inventory.evidence: round3-result.json checked.findings[4]; page-5.js lines 45 and 79; round4-result.json film.summary
inventory.computable_from: narration word times, cuts
inventory.proposed_calculation: For cards marked 'key', at = earliest word of its clause such that cut - at >= 1.2 s; else push the cut to the next word (if the next shot's cards start later).
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Start a conclusion on the first word of its phrase, not the last.

inventory.name: No two lines in the same place at once
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: for about 5 frames NO SPARE was drawn over the fading WHAT HAPPENS TO PRICES? ('NO SPAREPENS TO PRICES?') because presence() fades out before 'until'. Fixed: question until spare + 0.12 (0.3 s fade), NO SPARE at spare + 0.15; two empty frames between.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A new line in an occupied box starts only after the old one has fully gone: new.at >= old.until + 1 frame (with fadeOut counted inside 'until').
inventory.evidence: page-5.js lines 65-68; round3-result.json checked.findings[3]; round4-result.json critique.summary 'NO SPARE overlap gone'
inventory.computable_from: page draw calls with boxes and times
inventory.proposed_calculation: Collect every text element's box and [at, until]; for overlapping boxes with overlapping time spans, set old.until = new.at - 1/30 s.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: When a line replaces another in the same spot, end the old one a couple of frames before the new one starts.

inventory.name: Where typed words may go
inventory.how_found: Plan; round 3 check: MOST ECONOMISTS AGREE tops at 0.047 down, above the title area and under a phone app's top bar; moved to 0.061. Round 3 and 4 measured longest lines at 0.86.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Title zone 0.06 to 0.90 across, 0.05 to 0.22 down; left edge 65 px, right limit 972 px (TEXT_LEFT, TEXT_RIGHT); top of any letter at least 0.06 down; rule cards stacked at 0.07 to 0.15 and 0.16 to 0.24 (lower card ends 0.236); heading baseline 142 px. Name tags on a gable 0.21 to 0.23 down (TAG_HEIGHT 5.6 m); THE FLAT-OUT FACTORY SLOWS right edge 0.73.
inventory.evidence: graphics.js lines 341-346; page-5.js lines 36-40; round3-result.json checked.findings[17]; round4-result.json pageFixes.summary; works-effects.js lines 125-128
inventory.computable_from: page draw calls (text sizes and positions)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Measure every drawn string's box with the font metrics; flag top < 0.06 x 1920, right > 972 px, left < 65 px; flag tags whose box crosses the subject's box.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: TEXT_RIGHT clamps buildWords; no top-edge or overlap check.
inventory.llm_tip: Keep every letter at least 0.06 down from the top and left of 0.90 across; phones cover the very top and right.

inventory.name: A soft dark band behind words over sky or smoke
inventory.how_found: Plan T13; round 3 and 4 set helpers measured only 28 to 49% of the title band is sky in the gate views (roofs and chimneys fill it).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Words cross smoke or chimneys only over a soft dark band; title zone brightness at most 0.36.
inventory.evidence: PLAN lines 178-179 and 1439; round3-result.json works.NOT DONE 'The words band'; round4-result.json set.NOT DONE
inventory.computable_from: plate (title zone), smoke path, word boxes
inventory.proposed_calculation: If the title zone's sky share < 0.6 or its brightness > 0.36, or the traced smoke path crosses a word box, draw the band automatically under those words.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py measures the title zone; the band is added by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: If the area behind the words isn't plain dark sky, put a soft dark band behind them.

inventory.name: Page-turn shading comes in over 0.3 of the peel
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: the peel drew the whole old page about 11% darker on its first frame (change 5.8 at 74.27 s and 4.7 at 122.64 s against a usual 0.4). Round 4 brought the sheet's shading in gradually; proved on the notice corner (identical) and old chapter 2 (only the first 7 peel frames changed).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: PEEL_SHADING_IN = 0.3 of the 0.85 s peel (about 8 frames), shading = smoothstep(progress, 0, 0.3); first frames now change 0.5 to 1.5.
inventory.evidence: KIT/paper-film/stage/cinema-stage.js lines 357-364 and 458; round3-result.json checked.findings[14]; round4-result.json pageFixes.summary
inventory.computable_from: fixed (stage code)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Copy the stage change into the plugin kit; keep a regression test that the first peel frame changes less than 2 levels.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in the film kit's cinema-stage.js; the plugin kit's copy lacks it.
inventory.llm_tip: Any effect that starts at full strength on its first frame shows as a pop; ramp it in over a few frames.

inventory.name: Run-on join between pages without a dip
inventory.how_found: Round 3 effects: page 4 into 5 with the normal dissolve showed a 4-level dip (the dissolve darkens its middle), though both frames had the same average colour.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: 'run-on' join: plain blend with dip 0; largest change 0.60 to 0.95.
inventory.computable_from: page join kind from the plan (same frame continues)
inventory.proposed_calculation: When two pages share the same view and camera at the join, choose 'run-on' automatically.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in film kit; not in plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: When one page runs on in the same frame, use a plain blend, not a dissolve.

inventory.name: How many word groups
inventory.how_found: Teaching critic T6: about 130 cards (one every 3 s) against the user's 'minimal'; plan cut to about 65 groups.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: About one group of words every 6 s (65 in 407 s), 3 to 5 per page; more only where each is a figure or a placement the narrator says (page 7 carries 7). A card stays until the next replaces it or the page turns.
inventory.computable_from: page events, narration length
inventory.proposed_calculation: groups_per_page_max = round(page_seconds / 6) + count of spoken figures; flag pages over it.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Aim for one group of words about every 6 seconds; let pictures carry the rest.

inventory.name: Holds, peels and slide timing
inventory.how_found: Plan's page list and moves table; plan risk: holds cut short by the real recording.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Guess hold 4 s with a ring filling over 4 s; rule hold 2 s; final fade 4 s; page peel 0.3 s after the last word; holds written as pauses in the timeline, not seconds in the page. Slides 2.6 to 4.1 s, start and stop on words, one per page at most (user's limit three), never a turn.
inventory.computable_from: narration word times
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each slide pick (start word, stop word) pairs inside the phrase it serves with 2.5 <= gap <= 4.1 s; peel_at = last word end + 0.3 s; insert hold pauses into the timeline before word timing.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Tie every slide's start and stop to words 2.5 to 4 seconds apart, and write holds into the timeline as pauses.

inventory.name: Labels don't cover what they name, and point at something visible
inventory.how_found: Round 3: MACHINES pointed at a cottage window, QUIET sat on the gasholder. Round 4 critic: MACHINES pointed at No. 2's upper windows instead of the flywheel; WORKERS' line ran straight down over the men. Round 5: corner option and a flywheel screen point.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Label target = the screen point of a visible, named thing (marker in works-shot.json); line leaves the target sideways (corner dx 120, dy -8) and the words sit on empty ground, not on the target or other story things.
inventory.evidence: page-3.js line 116; graphics.js lines 114-118; round4-result.json critique.findings[7]; round3-result.json pages.summary item 4
inventory.computable_from: marker screen points and story boxes from shot facts
inventory.proposed_calculation: Place label words at the nearest empty spot (no story box, not the title zone of other cards) at 120 to 200 px from the target; route the line with a corner if the straight line crosses the target's box.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: A label's line must not run over the thing it names; send it out sideways to empty ground.

inventory.name: Seconds a frame and filming time
inventory.how_found: Plan used notice-corner measurements (F3); round 3 and round 4 filmed pages 3 to 5 and measured from logs.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Held, nothing live: 0.57 s (two helpers) to 0.8 s; held with smoke or flicker: 0.9 to 1.3 s alone (1.05 two helpers, 2.0 to 2.3 while another Blender runs); slides 2.9 to 6.6 s; loading 20 to 45 s a piece. Pages 3 to 5 (2,283 frames): 70 min (1.83 s/frame) in round 3, 53 min (1.4 s/frame) in round 4.
inventory.evidence: PLAN lines 616-618 and 1198-1208; round3-result.json pages.summary 'Seconds a frame'; round4-result.json film.summary
inventory.computable_from: shot list (held/effect/slide frames), timeline
inventory.proposed_calculation: hours = (held_plain x 0.8 + held_live x 1.3 + slide x 6 + pieces x 40 s) / 3600, with a 1.5 x margin if another heavy job runs; split into stretches under 2 hours.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Estimate filming from the shot list before starting, and never film while Blender is drawing.

inventory.name: Pieces, loading and memory
inventory.how_found: Feasibility critic F1 and F12: every 60-frame piece loaded all 16 pages; one painted set took 20 to 31 s and about 2.6 GB of browser memory; jump finder on the whole chapter about 19 GB. Round 4 pages helper ran out of memory when two Blender jobs used about 12 GB.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Load only the pages a piece covers (plus the next during a peel); pieces 240 to 300 frames (PIECE_FRAMES 240 used); stretches under 2 hours (FILM_FROM, FILM_TO); jump finder one piece or page at a time; no more than two views a page; two views of one place share one set; one heavy job at a time on 16 GB.
inventory.evidence: PLAN lines 1212-1221 and 1407, 1418; round4-result.json pageFixes.tested; KIT/paper-film/tools/film-chapter-parallel.sh lines 10-15
inventory.computable_from: page list, set sizes, machine memory
inventory.proposed_calculation: workers = floor((free_GB - 2) / (2.6 x views_per_page)); piece_frames = 270; refuse to start filming while a Blender process is running.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: film-chapter-parallel.sh takes FILM_FROM/FILM_TO and PIECE_FRAMES; lazy page loading is in the film kit's chapter scene, not the plugin kit's template.
inventory.llm_tip: Film in pieces of about 270 frames, one heavy job at a time, and load only the pages each piece needs.

inventory.name: Plate render time and its checks
inventory.how_found: Round 1/2 people test: 1536 x 2730 EEVEE at 48 samples about 11 minutes each. Round 3: 25 minutes with all lights shadowing, 6 with three shadowing lights. Plan: read render logs for shadow memory faults (lesson 110).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Plates 1536 x 2730, EEVEE, about 6 to 11 min; check each render log for 'Shadow buffer full' and 'Could not allocate shadow atlas'; previews 540 x 960 about 1 minute; checker runs at 1080 x 1920, 16 samples.
inventory.evidence: round1-result.json built[1].tested 'Plates'; round3-result.json works.summary 'Speed'; round4-result.json set.tested
inventory.computable_from: light list, plate list
inventory.proposed_calculation: Estimate plate minutes = 4 + 6 x shadow-casting lights / 3; after every render, grep the log for the two fault strings and refuse the plate if found.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: check_shot.py reads render logs (RENDER_FAULTS); plate estimate not.
inventory.llm_tip: Read the render log of every plate for shadow memory faults before judging its light.

inventory.name: Disk and repository size limits
inventory.how_found: Feasibility critic F2 and F15: film with grain is 3.5 MB a second even on held frames; notice corner's blend and export 83 and 62 MB.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: One full chapter copy 1.4 to 1.6 GB; peak about 6.5 to 7.5 GB; delete pieces after the silent film is checked; split exports (lane 15.6, factories 8.5, town 6.7, props 38.9 MB); keep pictures outside .blend; .blend1 backups off; every repository file under 90 MB (GitHub limit 100 MB).
inventory.computable_from: film length, set file sizes
inventory.proposed_calculation: film_GB = seconds x 3.5 / 1000 x 2 (pieces plus joined); check free space before each export and stretch; refuse a save over 90 MB.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check free disk before every export and filming stretch; a chapter needs about four times its final file size.

inventory.name: Stripe finder: squashed texture coordinates
inventory.how_found: Round 3 pages found the gate piers looked like orange curtains (works_kit bug); round 3 check wrote find_stripes.py and found 15, 27 and 33 striped parts still in the factories and far town (60 to 85% of No. 2's chimney brick). Round 4 rebuilt: 0, except 1.3 m2 on four roofs from the shared street builder.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every model passes the stripe finder with 0 striped parts before plates are drawn.
inventory.evidence: round3-result.json checked.findings[0]; round4-result.json critique.summary and set.summary; SCRATCH/redesign/check-round-3/tools/find_stripes.py
inventory.computable_from: the .glb files
inventory.proposed_calculation: For every textured face, area in UV space / area in 3D; flag faces with UV area near 0 (< 1e-6 of the median ratio) while 3D area is large; report square metres per part.
inventory.already_automatic: No (scratch tool only).
inventory.llm_tip: Run a stripe check on every built model; a squashed texture shows as streaks the painter will copy.

inventory.name: Shared-script safety: kept shot pixel-identical
inventory.how_found: Round 1: the rebuilt street differed by 7 levels on average (40 max) because colour settings (exposure 0.6, Medium High Contrast, 16 samples) were only set with --preview. Every round after redrew the notice corner and compared all 518,400 pixels.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: After any change to a shared script, redraw the kept shot's preview (540 x 960) and its film stills at 4.5 s and 10 s; 0 pixels may differ. Every build saves the same colour settings.
inventory.evidence: round1-result.json built[0].summary and tested; round2-result.json props_fixes.tested; round4-result.json pageFixes.tested
inventory.computable_from: kept shots list
inventory.proposed_calculation: A regression script: render each kept shot's stills before and after, compare; fail on any non-zero pixel.
inventory.already_automatic: No (done by hand each round).
inventory.llm_tip: Before and after changing any shared file, redraw a kept shot and compare every pixel.

inventory.name: Model facts measured from the saved file
inventory.how_found: Round 1 check: index.json sizes came from build constants and were wrong (jacket nail 0.846 vs 0.776 to 0.796 m; jacket 0.6 vs 0.516 m; bank letters 0.29 vs 0.2 m); eight props had a 'name.001' root; cloth pictures seeded with hash() differed each run.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Sizes, letter heights, nail and loop positions measured from the saved model before writing index.json (match within 1.5 mm); one root named after the file (builder stops if a part already has the name); seeds from zlib.crc32; cached pictures named with a colour fingerprint.
inventory.computable_from: saved .glb
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already partly automatic; add a glb reader check to every build script's end.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in the chapter 2 prop and figure builders (film kit); not in the plugin kit.
inventory.llm_tip: Measure a model after saving it; never trust a size written from build constants.

inventory.name: Checker false alarms on dark or thin things
inventory.how_found: Round 3: the checker's 'picture matches the scene' test called the picture out of date because the men are dark on dark, the gates thin bars and the boards' strongest edges their borders; ran a relaxed version (check_dark_picture.py). Round 4/5: 'man 2 rests on brazier' was a quarter-point ray starting 0.22 m inside the rim under his stooped reach.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Leave dark figures, thin bars and bordered boards out of the picture-match test; a figure leaning over a prop needs its ray test from its feet, not its box.
inventory.computable_from: check file groups
inventory.proposed_calculation: In check_shot.py: skip groups with mean luminance < 0.05 or width < 6 px from the picture-match test; cast 'on ground' rays from the lowest 10 cm of the figure's mesh only.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: If the checker says a dark or thin thing doesn't match, check by eye on the outlines picture before moving anything.

inventory.name: Jump finder with the planned cuts named
inventory.how_found: Every round ran find_jumps.py per piece and on a 2-second clip at each place pieces meet.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Ordinary frame change 0.39 to 0.51; a cut about 42 to 46; a time cut about 8.4 to 10.7; anything above about 1.5 that is not a planned event is a fault. Measure the frame before each cut too.
inventory.evidence: round2-result.json figures.summary; round3-result.json effects.tested; round4-result.json film.tested
inventory.computable_from: page events (cuts, time cuts, steps), filmed pieces
inventory.proposed_calculation: Generate the planned-change list from the page events automatically and pass it to find_jumps.py; also measure joins between pieces.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: find_jumps.py exists in both kits; planned list typed by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Hand the jump finder the list of planned cuts from the page events, and also check where filmed pieces join.

inventory.name: Phone-size newcomer test the checker cannot do
inventory.how_found: Round 3 pages and round 4 critic judged stills at phone size: main rule passed everywhere while men were specks, the far town's gasholder read as a second tank, BANK was read first, the flat-out factory looked empty, smoke looked like a fault.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: For each shot, list the 3 to 4 things a newcomer must see (two factories, men waiting, men going in, nobody waiting) and judge a 300 px wide still per event; a fresh helper not told what it shows watches in motion.
inventory.evidence: round3-result.json pages.summary 'Would a newcomer see the four things?'; round4-result.json critique.summary 'Judged against the standard'
inventory.computable_from: script's 'must teach' lines per page
inventory.proposed_calculation: Generate the question list from each page's must-teach line; build a contact sheet at 300 px wide per event; send to a critic agent with the list.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: film-critic agent exists in the plugin; no per-shot must-see list is generated.
inventory.llm_tip: Passing the composition checker doesn't mean a newcomer sees the idea; look at a 300 px wide still and name what must be seen.

inventory.name: Continuity sheet across views
inventory.how_found: Plan's 'how the two factories stay the same'; round 3 and 4 built one from the checker's measurements.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: One still per view side by side; counts per view (men 7, 7, 0, 0, 8, 8); No. 1 always left of No. 2; one round vs two square chimneys; boards consistent; same smoke and flicker seeds and wind on every page.
inventory.evidence: PLAN lines 1081-1107; round3-result.json works.summary 'Continuity sheet'; works-effects.js lines 111-117 (SEEDS)
inventory.computable_from: shot facts of every view
inventory.proposed_calculation: From each view's shot facts, count figures and identifying parts; compare against the state table; fail on any mismatch.
inventory.already_automatic: Partly: make_works_continuity_sheet.py (film kit, Works only).
inventory.llm_tip: Check every repeat view against one table of what must be the same.

inventory.name: Factory scale and identifying features
inventory.how_found: Round 2 factories built at true scale; chimney visibility measured by ray casting; plan required true scale (old 3.2 m shed).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Mills 22 x 22 m, front 8 m behind the wall, 2 storeys (eaves 7.8 m); No. 1: one round chimney 26 m (2.9 m to 1.84 m), 35 m behind the wall in line with its outer pier, sawtooth peaks 10.2 m; No. 2: two square chimneys 25 and 23 m (2 m to 1.36 m) at (5.3, 35) and (8.6, 38.5), water tank 3 x 3 x 2.8 m, top 14.8 m, lantern roofs to 10.9 m. Lane 22 m, carriageway 6, pavements 2.2; gates 3 m wide, 7 m apart; wall 4 m; dividing wall 5.5 m.
inventory.evidence: round2-result.json factories.summary; build_factories.py lines 122-123; assemble_works.py lines 122-157
inventory.computable_from: script (what must be told apart), camera spots
inventory.proposed_calculation: Size identifying features so each projects at least 60 px wide at phone scale... i.e. at least 200 px tall on the film frame in the overview, using the projector.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Build at true size and check by ray cast that the identifying feature shows over what stands in front of it.

inventory.name: Background landmarks must not borrow a factory's identity
inventory.how_found: Round 2: gasholder loomed beside No. 1's chimney; far chimneys rose over a factory roof. Round 3 put the gasholder and church on 38 m hills; round 3 check: now bigger than No. 1's chimney and read as a tank on No. 1's side. Round 4 moved the gasholder out of every view.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No background object of the same kind as an identifying feature (tank, chimney) within a factory's column in any view; nothing in a column bigger on screen than its factory's own identifying feature.
inventory.evidence: round2-result.json factories.tested 'Earlier fixes'; round3-result.json checked.findings[6]; round4-result.json set.summary 'The gasholder'
inventory.computable_from: far-town objects, identifying features, camera spots
inventory.proposed_calculation: Project every background object; for each factory column (screen x range of its identifying features +-0.05), flag background objects with screen height >= the feature's or tagged as the same kind.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Keep background tanks and chimneys out of each building's column, or they will be counted as its own.

inventory.name: Windows in step groups; no merged glow
inventory.how_found: Plan F4 (build_factory merged all windows); round 2 built separate panes in three named thirds per factory.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Every pane its own piece in groups <prefix>-windows-step-1 to 3 (No. 1: 25, 23, 26; No. 2: 26, 27, 27 plus the doorway); lit and dark glass materials kept; windows change in steps, the set redrawn once per step.
inventory.evidence: round2-result.json factories.summary and tested; works-effects.js header
inventory.computable_from: script states (fractions lit)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Split panes into N groups by x order where N = the number of distinct lit fractions in the script's states.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in build_factories.py (film kit).
inventory.llm_tip: Build windows as separate panes in groups so they can light in steps without a new painting.

inventory.name: Ground under raised areas
inventory.how_found: Round 2 check: odd dark patches across the yard setts (only 2 cm above ground 0) and a dark oval at No. 2's doorway: the lane's ground showing through. Round 3 lowered the ground under the yards.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Lower or cut the base ground under any surface laid less than about 5 cm above it.
inventory.evidence: round2-result.json checked.findings[9]; round3-result.json works.summary 'The factories and the far town'
inventory.computable_from: scene meshes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Ray-cast a grid downward over every floor surface; flag where another ground surface lies within 5 cm below it.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Don't lay a floor 2 cm over another ground; z-fighting and see-through patches follow.

inventory.name: Machines read as machines
inventory.how_found: Round 3 check: doorway 'machines' were stepped dark slabs that read as a bar chart. Round 4: lathe, press with a spoked flywheel facing the lane, pillar drill; No. 1's looms read as church benches; round 5 rebuilt looms chest-high with pulley wheel, belt, cloth roll and a broken-up back wall.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each machine has a recognisable outline (wheel, belt to a line shaft, different heights and shapes), chest-high or taller so it clears what is in front from the gate view; no rising rows of plain boxes.
inventory.computable_from: judgement only (outline at phone size)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Judgement only; a helper names the object from a 300 px wide crop without being told.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Plain boxes in steps read as a chart in an economics film; give machines wheels and belts.

inventory.name: Colour rules for real places
inventory.how_found: Plan's lettering and colour rules (election on 7 November); round 2 found two red coats were the eye's target.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No large flat areas of a party's, supermarket chain's or bank's colour; hi-vis orange, never yellow-and-black; no banknotes or coins (portraits).
inventory.computable_from: plate and filmed still
inventory.proposed_calculation: Convert to HSV; flag connected regions over 1.5% of the frame with saturation > 0.45 in listed party/chain hues; check yellow+black stripe patterns.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Scan every real-place view for big areas of one strong colour before painting.

inventory.name: Places and sizes of the bank and its sign across views
inventory.how_found: T2/T10: bank was a sliver; plan moved it to the lane's last third. Round 3: any further up, its hanging sign would hang across W1's view; put at the left terrace's third building (17 to 21.5 m from W3), sign at 3.75 m (above W1's frame).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: An own-surface sign meant for one view must project outside the frames of the other views (or sit above them).
inventory.evidence: assemble_works.py lines 165-167; round3-result.json works.NOT DONE 'Away from the plan, on purpose'
inventory.computable_from: sign positions, all camera spots
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each sign and each view that shouldn't show it, project; flag if it falls inside the frame.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check every sign placed for one view against all the other views that share the set.

inventory.name: Where the street's lines meet, worked out from the camera
inventory.how_found: Log 29-30: measured by hand and with measure_composition.py's line finder on finished pictures (47 lines found in the sharp liked picture, only 4 to 7 in clip 29's soft frames, so its figure for the clip was wrong, lesson 104). Log 31: the user said 'the lines don't converge the same way'; shot_facts.py then projected the street direction through the Blender camera, which is exact.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: For a level camera (tilt 0, lean 0), sensor fit vertical, frame W x H, lens V top to bottom, turn psi left of +y, street direction (0, 1, s): f = (H/2)/tan(V/2); across = 0.5 + f*tan(psi)/W; down = 0.5 - f*s/(H*cos(psi)). inventory.final_value_or_rule: Nelder-Mead over (x, height, turn, lens) at our distance up the street; steps (0.3 m, 0.3 m, 1.5 deg, 4 deg); pass if within 0.1 m height, 0.15 m sideways, 0.75 degrees turn, 2 degrees lens; the painting misses its own landmarks by up to 62 px, so smaller differences mean nothing; the fitted eye is clamped into the eye range. Reference lines-meet check allows 0.03 either way; a vertical difference with a level camera is the lens: V = 2*atan(s/(2*(0.5 - v_ref)*cos psi)).
inventory.evidence: check_shot.py check_camera_match lines 556-614, check_reference_lines 659-693; experiments/31 .../tools/match_camera.py; shot-check.json reference.camera_match
inventory.computable_from: landmark pixels in the sketch and the same points in Blender metres
inventory.proposed_calculation: Use the checker's fit before building (it needs only the check file and the camera); automate landmark reading with line detection on the sketch where possible, otherwise read them by hand.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes, inside check_shot.py (kit and plugin kit), but only after building and only with hand-read landmarks.
inventory.llm_tip: When copying a composition sketch, match the camera to its landmarks first; never move props to fix a camera difference.

inventory.name: Camera too near or too far against a reference (size ratio)
inventory.how_found: Log 31 helpers: the checker told users to move every prop when the camera stood too far back.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: At least 4 compared props, median height ratio against the reference; if |median - 1| > 0.15 and at least 75% of props agree within 0.15, move the camera median(d*(1 - ratio)) metres along its view.
inventory.computable_from: reference boxes and planned prop sizes/distances
inventory.proposed_calculation: Same formula before building, using projected heights.
inventory.already_automatic: After building, in check_shot.py.
inventory.llm_tip: If everything is uniformly too big or small, move the camera, not the props.

inventory.name: Props resting where they should (floating, sunk, landed on something high, on their support)
inventory.how_found: Log 29: rays cast down from the sky landed the board's posts on the board itself (lesson 88). Log 31: one ray slipped between seat planks (lesson 109), five rays now; the lantern-on-chair fix once dropped it to the pavement (lesson 108). Log 31 helper: a sunk prop read as floating; an upward ray was added. Round 4-5: the stooped man's box reached over the brazier rim, a false 'rests on brazier'.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Floating if more than 0.03 m of air; sunk if more than 0.05 m below; 'landed high' if more than 0.5 m above the street model; a prop on a support rests if its air <= 0.03 m and it hits that group; 'moved apart' over 0.1 m. Rays: 5 spots (centre and +-0.25 of the box) from 5 cm above the base; sunk test looks up half the prop's height; support top from 0.75 of its height at +-0.15 of its box, median. Placing: start the ray low (pavement + 2.0 m, under the eaves).
inventory.evidence: check_shot.py check_resting lines 697-775; shot_facts.py lines 221-287; set_dressing.place_prop lines 56-79; assemble_notice_corner.py line 111; works-w1-shot-check.json man_2_note
inventory.computable_from: the set and the props in Blender (ray casts)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Place every prop with place_prop from a start height just under its own top's clearance; for figures and anything with outstretched parts, take the footprint from the lowest 5 cm of vertices, not the bounding box's quarter points.
inventory.already_automatic: place_prop in set_dressing.py (not in the plugin kit); the checker after building.
inventory.llm_tip: Place props by ray cast from low down, update the view layer before reading positions, and judge 'stands on' from the feet, not the bounding box.

inventory.name: Story props together in 3D, in front of their backdrop
inventory.how_found: Log 31 helper planted a drum 1.5 m behind the board: it still looked grouped on screen and passed rule 3.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each ground story prop no more than 0.1 m further than the support (fix: bring it to support distance - 0.3 m); each within 0.3 m (footprint gap) of another story prop (fix: to 0.1 m); the support within 0.3 m of the nearest story prop. Board 0.75 m behind the fire so it wouldn't scorch.
inventory.computable_from: planned positions and footprints (no render)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Validate the layout table before building: footprint gaps by box distance, depths by projection on the view direction.
inventory.already_automatic: After building only.
inventory.llm_tip: Group the story props within 0.3 m of each other in the street, all in front of the backdrop.

inventory.name: Words hidden by a prop in front
inventory.how_found: Log 31 helper: a lamp post covering 16 to 21% of the notice was never reported; check added. Rule 3: the chair may cover only the signature.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Only the bottom fifth of a must_read group may be covered; at most 5% of the upper four-fifths hidden; a hider is named when it covers over 30% of the hidden part; sideways push = hidden columns' span + 25*W/1536 px; chair scale 1.05 so its back covers just the notice's bottom edge from standing height (3% hidden).
inventory.computable_from: projected silhouettes of must_read groups and nearer props
inventory.proposed_calculation: Pre-build occlusion test with the same masks (Workbench ids and solo pictures); move or scale the occluder until under 5%.
inventory.already_automatic: After building only.
inventory.llm_tip: Check words are clear from the composed spot; let a near prop overlap only the signature.

inventory.name: Story props cut by the frame or missing
inventory.how_found: Log 31 verifier: a pail pushed out of frame went unreported; a prop just past the edge was called 'hidden behind the set'.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Cut if the whole prop's picture touches the left, top or bottom 2 px (the support may be cut at the top); fix brings its box to 0.03/0.97. Missing: off-frame side from the unclipped box (0.99/0.01) or hidden behind the prop that covers most of it; bring just inside 0.05 to 0.95 across, 0.03 to 0.97 down.
inventory.computable_from: projected boxes
inventory.proposed_calculation: Pre-build projection of every story prop's mesh; reject layouts with any story prop under 100% inside.
inventory.already_automatic: After building only.
inventory.llm_tip: Every story prop must be wholly in frame and visible from the composed spot.

inventory.name: Which way a prop model faces, and turning props toward targets
inventory.how_found: Log 31 critic: at 140 degrees the chair's back faced the fire and hid the lantern; -40 degrees puts its back to the board and seat to the fire (lesson 114). The board is turned square to the composed camera.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Chair turn -40 degrees (model back on +y). Board facing = atan2(cam.x - board.x, -(cam.y - board.y)). Lantern turn 20, pail 30, drum 25, handcart -75.
inventory.computable_from: a 'front' direction recorded per model in props/index.json, and the target each prop should face (camera, fire, board)
inventory.proposed_calculation: turn = degrees(atan2(target - prop)) + model_front_offset, with model_front_offset measured once per model and stored in index.json.
inventory.already_automatic: Only the board's facing is computed; others are typed by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Record each model's front direction once; compute turns from what the prop should face.

inventory.name: Measure a model before using a size someone worked out from a picture
inventory.how_found: Log 32: the skeptic's sooty drum lining was 0.365 m radius; the drum is 0.296 m, so the lining stuck out as an orange band and brought the drum's edge 9 px from the notice (lesson 116). measure_drum.py found the wall's inner radius.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Lining radius 0.255 m inside a 0.26 to 0.28 m inner wall (0.296 m outside).
inventory.computable_from: the GLB's vertices
inventory.proposed_calculation: Read sizes (and inner radii at given heights) from the model automatically; never take sizes from a helper's picture estimate.
inventory.already_automatic: props/index.json has outer sizes; inner sizes are not recorded.
inventory.llm_tip: Measure the model in Blender before fitting anything inside or against it.

inventory.name: Letter height on screen for words that must or must not be read
inventory.how_found: Log 32: PITS WILL BE CLOSED only 11 px tall, 'about 18 would read easily'. Plan 34: W1 board about 41 px a letter, W3 boards 16 to 27 px; round 4: BANK 29 px still read, No. 1 and No. 2 about 14 px; WAGES should be at least about 25 px.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Words meant to be read: key lines at least about 18 px tall on the 1920-tall frame (25 px for a single word like WAGES); words not meant to be read on that page: dimmed (0.15) or about 14 px or less.
inventory.evidence: Project story log 32 'Left for later'; 34 Plan lines 260-275; round4-result.json findings 10 and 12
inventory.computable_from: letter heights in metres on the sign models and their depth
inventory.proposed_calculation: letter_px = f*letter_height_m/d; scale the sign or bring it nearer until key lines reach 18 px at the composed frame; flag readable signs not in the script.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Compute each sign's letter size at the composed spot; 18 px tall is about the least a phone viewer reads.

inventory.name: Subject is the biggest bright thing (rule 5)
inventory.how_found: Log 30 measurements: liked picture's notice 0.61 against an average of 0.32, about half to two thirds of the brightest 3% on it, about 80% in the group; clip 29 about a fifth. Notice corner final: 60 to 68% on the notice, 79 to 90% in the box, 3.07 to 3.13 times the average.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Brightest parts = the top 3% of the picture blurred by 1% of the width. At least 40% of them on the subject (its mask widened 9 x 9 px) and at least 75% in the story props' box; subject mean at least 1.8 times the frame's mean.
inventory.computable_from: needs a render; quick EEVEE at 540 x 960 with 16 samples is enough
inventory.proposed_calculation: Automatic light-tuning loop: render small, measure, raise the subject's linked key light (or dim the patch's owner light) by bisection until both shares and the 1.8 ratio pass; stop on burnt-out pixels.
inventory.already_automatic: Measured after rendering; tuned by hand over 29 lighting rounds.
inventory.llm_tip: Give the subject its own warm key light linked only to it, then tune by measurement, not by eye.

inventory.name: Dim sky and the frame's overall brightness
inventory.how_found: Log 30: liked top-centre sky 0.35, clip 29 0.49 (a cloud was the brightest thing). Log 32: cutting the fire's light left the frame a third darker than the liked picture (0.21 against 0.32), fixed with sky strength 1.4 to 1.96.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Each third of the top third <= 0.36 mean brightness; frame average near the reference's (about 0.30); notice corner SKY_STRENGTH 1.96 (street.blend 1.4); top row measured 0.24 to 0.26.
inventory.computable_from: needs a small render
inventory.proposed_calculation: Bisection on world strength between 1.0 and 2.5 to bring the frame average to the target while keeping every top-third cell <= 0.36.
inventory.already_automatic: Measured after rendering only.
inventory.llm_tip: Dim the sky rather than brightening everything else; tune its strength by measurement.

inventory.name: Warm light share and where it lies (rule 6)
inventory.how_found: Log 30: liked 2.2 to 2.3% warm, clip 29 0.5%. Log 31: fire light cut 900 W (white notice) to 300 (4.4%), deep orange 220 W (6.3%) and 140 W (4.5%), 160 W made the chair back as bright as the notice; settled at 70 W with light linking (lesson 112).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Warm = (red - blue)/255 times brightness > 0.18; share 1.5 to 3% of the frame; at least 50% of it within the story box widened by 6% of the width. FIRE_WATTS 70, light 0.55 m over the coals (0.4 m over the rim), ROAD_GLOW 450 W spot 40 degrees blend 0.8 aimed at (1.4, 25.0).
inventory.computable_from: render; lights' positions
inventory.proposed_calculation: Bisection on the fire's energy (and on each spot's custom distance) until the share is 2.0 to 2.5% and inside >= 70%; name lights for stray patches by energy/distance^2 within cone and reach (warm_lights_near).
inventory.already_automatic: Measured after rendering; lights named automatically; tuning by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Shorten a warm light's reach (custom distance) before cutting its strength, so the subject keeps its glow.

inventory.name: Subject lit from below: warm bottom, cool top
inventory.how_found: Log 30: liked notice warms steadily from top to bottom (+0.17 on the share measure). Log 31: red minus blue misjudged white parts; the share (r - b)/(r + b) told tests apart (lesson 111). 700 W in a 50-degree beam burnt 8% of the notice white (lesson 118); a 20-degree cone warmed only a patch behind the chair back; the beam went through the board onto the wall until a reach of 1.4 m was set.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Hue (r - b)/(r + b) in the subject's bottom 15% minus its top 15% >= 0.10 (reference 0.17). Notice glow: spot from 0.25 m over the coals, colour (1.0, 0.42, 0.12), 200 W, 50-degree cone, blend 0.9, no shadow, custom distance 1.4 m (notice 1.0 to 1.2 m away, wall 2.1 m), aimed 0.46 x scale below the notice centre (its bottom edge), linked to the notice and board only; corner lamp pale (1.0, 0.97, 0.94) 12 W.
inventory.computable_from: the subject's position and size, the fire's position, the wall behind
inventory.proposed_calculation: aim = subject bottom edge centre; cutoff = midpoint between the subject's farthest point and the first surface behind it along the beam (ray cast); cone = 2*atan(subject half-diagonal / distance) + 10 degrees; link it to subject + support; energy by bisection on lift >= 0.12 with no clipped pixels.
inventory.already_automatic: Measured after rendering; set by hand. The film page gets a copy of the light from notice-corner-shot.json automatically.
inventory.llm_tip: Light the subject from below with a narrow deep-orange spot that reaches only the subject; keep the light above it pale.

inventory.name: No story prop as bright as the subject; lamps' glass and flames
inventory.how_found: Log 31-32: the chair's seat and top rail, the lantern's brass and glass, the drum's rim and inside wall each came out as bright as the notice. Lantern watts 60, 15, 5, 3, 2 then 1. Chair paint 0.18 made its legs darker than the pavement; 0.25 kept. Light linking added (lesson 120).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: A story prop's 95th-percentile brightness must stay under the subject's median - 0.05 (props of at least 400 px). A prop that is a light (lights_in_story) may outshine it only over 10% of itself (a small flame lights about 6%, a glowing glass 18 to 22%). Chair tint 0.25; lantern 1 W, glass emission 0.3, see-through 0.45; the lantern's light skips the lantern; the fire's light skips the drum and the chair; lamp mantle emission 8, glass 0.3 see-through 0.5.
inventory.computable_from: which lights sit inside or next to which props (Blender positions)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Automatic default links: every light skips the object it sits in; a container's own light skips the container and props within 0.6 m; a subject key light reaches only subject + support. Then bisection on tint (0.18 to 0.35) and lamp energies against the rule.
inventory.already_automatic: Light linking helper exists (set_dressing.light_reaches, not in plugin kit); choices made by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Link lights so they never light their own housing; a lamp's flame may be the brightest point but its glass may not.

inventory.name: No burnt-out colour
inventory.how_found: Log 31-32: notice, board, chair seat and drum top near white under the first 900 W fire.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Pixels with any channel >= 254 must cover no more than 0.02% of the frame and 3% of any prop, and no more than 0.1% of the frame on the set.
inventory.computable_from: render
inventory.proposed_calculation: Stop condition for every light-tuning loop.
inventory.already_automatic: Measured after rendering.
inventory.llm_tip: White has no warmth: cap lights before the subject clips.

inventory.name: Stray warm patches named by light
inventory.how_found: Log 31-32: an orange oval on the house wall from the notice glow's beam passing the board; fire glow on the road.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Warm patches with hue > 0.25 and brightness > 0.25 outside all props, opened 9 x 9, over 0.2% of the frame (top 3) are listed with the lights reaching them most (energy / distance^2, respecting spot cone, custom reach and light linking).
inventory.computable_from: render plus lights in facts.json
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already a calculation; make it feed the tuning loop (shorten that light's reach).
inventory.already_automatic: Yes after rendering, as a note.
inventory.llm_tip: Give every spot a custom distance just past its target so it can't paint the wall behind.

inventory.name: Quiet side weight (rule 10)
inventory.how_found: Log 30: liked 43/57, clip 29 46/54 (needed by both, not decisive). Notice corner 34% (log 31), 36%, 38% (log 32), 46% on the film page. A left fill of 500 W moved it only 36 to 37%; detail and small lights work better.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: The half away from the subject holds 40 to 48% of the weight (Laplacian of the blurred picture, blurred 25 px, plus distance from mean grey, each normalised); ranked at 0.8 of other faults; no light there as bright as the subject; no non-story prop there over 2%. Fixes used: a second gas lamp on the left kerb (10 W, pale), a cool area fill 350 W (3 x 18 m, colour 0.62, 0.72, 1.0, houses at about 0.6 of the sky's brightness), two dim lit windows.
inventory.computable_from: render; window and lamp positions
inventory.proposed_calculation: Automatic: if under 40%, light 1 to 3 more windows in the quiet half (picked as light_left_windows does) and re-measure; do not raise fill light energy beyond the houses at 0.6 of the sky.
inventory.already_automatic: light_left_windows() picks windows automatically (0.05 to 0.42 across, 0.25 to 0.48 down, every other one, emission 1.2) in the notice corner script only.
inventory.llm_tip: Balance the quiet side with small details and dim lights, not a big fill light; it is the weakest rule.

inventory.name: Lamps and lights that land on the subject or the meeting point
inventory.how_found: Log 31: the far street lamp touched the board's post right where the lines meet; the street's own lamp behind the camera flooded the near road. Lamps at y 39 and 64.5 removed; lamp at y 11 dimmed to 70 W.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: No lamp head or post within a clear gap (18 px) of the subject's outline or the meeting point; lights behind the camera that reach the near-left ground are dimmed.
inventory.computable_from: set lamp positions and the camera
inventory.proposed_calculation: Project every set lamp; remove or move those within 18 px of the subject's silhouette or within 0.03 of the frame of the meeting point; dim lights within 15 m behind the camera.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Check the set's own lamps from the composed spot; the street builder put them there, not you.

inventory.name: Render shadow memory and reading the render log
inventory.how_found: Log 31: a hard black wedge across the road, blamed on the lighting by three critics, was 'Shadow buffer full'; '2048' could not be set up ('Could not allocate shadow atlas') (lesson 110).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: EEVEE shadow_pool_size '1024' and shadow_resolution_scale = min(1, 1080/width); the checker refuses the light rules when the log has either message.
inventory.evidence: set_dressing.py render lines 232-246; check_shot.py RENDER_FAULTS line 1811 and main 1924-1931
inventory.computable_from: picture width; the render log
inventory.proposed_calculation: Always write the log beside every plate and still, and pass it to check_shot automatically (check-shot.sh only does it if RENDER_LOG is set).
inventory.already_automatic: The render setting is automatic in set_dressing.render (not in the plugin kit); the log check runs only when given.
inventory.llm_tip: Before judging light, grep the render log for 'Shadow buffer full' and 'Could not allocate shadow atlas'.

inventory.name: Glowing things and see-through glass in the plate
inventory.how_found: Log 29: flames lit by their own lamp rendered as white paper cones (lesson 89). Log 32: setting glass alpha was ignored because the glTF glass reads it from its picture.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Glow materials have a black base (glow_material); see_through() unhooks the alpha link first; drum soot glows 0.6 at the coals fading to 0 under the rim.
inventory.evidence: set_dressing.py glow_material and see_through; assemble_notice_corner.py lines 136-148
inventory.computable_from: material names (glass, bulb, flame)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Automatic pass over imported props: any material named *glass* or *_bulb* gets make_glow/see_through with the place's lamp colours.
inventory.already_automatic: Helpers exist (not in plugin kit); applied by hand per prop.
inventory.llm_tip: Give glowing parts a black base colour and leave flames out of the plate entirely.

inventory.name: Out-of-date or shifted picture detection
inventory.how_found: Log 31: a picture made before the scene changed was judged as current. Log 32: brightness-only edges missed a rusty drum on a blue-grey road (lesson 117); colour edges added; the test then found Flux's 3-pixel shift.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Edges: LAB blurred 1.5, Canny 20/60 on lightness and 10/30 on both colour channels, widened 7 x 7. Each story prop (and others over 0.5% of the frame, at least 400 px) is slid up to 1/30 of the width in steps of max(2, W/270) px. Out of date if the best agreement gains at least 0.08 or stays under 0.45 (up-to-date pictures gained 0; moved props gained 0.09 to 0.23).
inventory.computable_from: the picture and the facts
inventory.proposed_calculation: Already computed; run it on every painting as it arrives and route a failure to align_painting.py.
inventory.already_automatic: Yes in check_shot.py (kit and plugin kit).
inventory.llm_tip: If the checker says the picture doesn't match the scene, re-render or align the painting before reading any light rule.

inventory.name: Lining a painting up with its plate (align_painting.py)
inventory.how_found: Log 32: every prop lined up better slid about 4 px; Flux had stretched the notice corner 0.65% and shifted it 3 px (lesson 123).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Coarse search: stretch 0.985 to 1.015 in 0.0025 steps, shift -12 to +12 px in 2 px steps (frame basis 1080 wide); fine: +-0.002 in 0.0005 and +-2 px in 0.5. Edges as above, widened 5 x 5. Results: notice corner 1.0065, +3, +3 (outlines on edges 0.70 to 0.96); people test 1.0010, +1.0, +0.5 (0.874 to 0.903).
inventory.computable_from: the painting, the plate camera's facts (shot_facts.py with the plate's lens)
inventory.proposed_calculation: Run automatically on every returned painting; accept if agreement >= 0.85 and stretch within 1%; else re-ask the painter.
inventory.already_automatic: Tool exists in the kit and plugin kit; run by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Always line a painting up with its plate before shining it onto the set; measure the facts with the plate's own lens (64.4).

inventory.name: Lining up the behind painting against the main one
inventory.how_found: Log 32 and people test.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: --against: edges of the lined-up painting (Canny 40/100 on lightness) except round the removed props (their outlines widened 25 x 25 px). Notice corner 0.990 to 0.991 (shift -0.5, -1.0); people test 0.999.
inventory.computable_from: both paintings and the near groups
inventory.proposed_calculation: Run automatically after every behind painting, naming the same groups that were painted out.
inventory.already_automatic: Tool exists; run by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Line up the behind painting against the lined-up main painting, not against the plate.

inventory.name: Keeping painted shadows round the near props (keep_painted_shadows.py)
inventory.how_found: Log 32: the fire's shadows of the pail and chair faded off the pavement 2 s into the slide (lesson 122); the first fix left a pale 10 to 15 px strip round the pail (lesson 125); pavement held at 70 to 71 (was rising to 89).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Main painting everywhere except inside the near props' outlines widened 10 px (painting pixels), soft join sigma widen/3; inside, the behind painting darkened by the ratio painting/behind (plus 8, clipped 0.25 to 1, blurred 3) measured outside and spread inward (quarter size, Telea radius 12, blurred 4). Default groups: subject, support, story props and 'lamp post'.
inventory.computable_from: check file core groups and the plate facts; which props are near enough to need it
inventory.proposed_calculation: Default groups = every group whose parallax over the slide exceeds 1 px (see the behind-painting item) instead of the hard-coded 'lamp post'; widen = the painter's outline width (measure the dark rim width round props, about 10 px).
inventory.already_automatic: Tool exists in kit and plugin kit; groups partly hard-coded.
inventory.llm_tip: After a behind painting, always keep the main painting's shadows outside the near props, then check the film frame by frame for a pale rim.

inventory.name: Which near things need a behind painting, and when the handover starts
inventory.how_found: Log 29: moving the camera uncovered pale jagged outlines behind the sacks and cart (lesson 91); the handover waited for 1.4 degrees, too late; half a degree works (lesson 96); every near prop then needs a soft 3D shadow (the barrel seemed to float).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: projected-set behind: { painting, hide } with reach 0.05 of the frame height round the props and quickMove 0.00003 (1 - cos of about half a degree); frontStretch [1.3, 1.9]; each hidden prop gets a soft contact shadow.
inventory.computable_from: the slide vector and each group's depth and the depth of what is behind it
inventory.proposed_calculation: parallax_px = f*L_lateral_component*|1/d_prop - 1/d_behind|/... (screen shift of the prop against the background over the slide); every group with over 1 px goes into 'hide', keep_painted_shadows and the behind prompt; every group in 'hide' gets a soft shadow automatically.
inventory.already_automatic: No; lists are typed by hand.
inventory.llm_tip: Anything the camera moves past at a different depth from its background needs the behind painting and its own soft shadow.

inventory.name: Plate preparation: thin parts and things the painter misreads
inventory.how_found: Log 31: the pail's wire handle removed (the painter would smear it); log 29: standing sacks read as clay jars once painted; log 32: chimney smokes dropped (both chimneys out of frame).
inventory.final_value_or_rule: Parts thinner than about 6 px at 1080 (the checker's without_wires opening) are removed, thickened, or named in the prompt as 'stay thin or left out'.
inventory.computable_from: solo masks from shot_facts.py
inventory.proposed_calculation: For each group: thin = solo mask minus its morphological opening (size max(3, round(6*W/1080)) odd); if thin pixels > 5% of the group, list it for removal or for the prompt's thin-parts sentence.
inventory.already_automatic: No.
inventory.llm_tip: Before painting, find every wire, rung and bar under 6 px wide; remove what doesn't matter and protect the rest in the prompt.

inventory.name: Prompt part: style header and fixed instructions
inventory.how_found: Log 29 lesson 97: Flux gave a near-photograph once; asking for the reference's thick strokes and ink outlines and 'nothing should look like a 3D render' got a painting. Log 32 and the people test used the same opening.
inventory.final_value_or_rule: 'Repaint image 1 completely as a hand-painted illustration in the exact painting style of image 2: the same visible brush strokes, dark ink outlines, simplified painterly textures on brick, stone, slate and wood, and matte painted finish. Nothing should look like a 3D render or a photograph any more.' then 'Keep image 1's camera, framing, perspective and every shape, outline, size and position exactly as they are, and keep its pattern of light and dark; change only the brushwork and the colour handling.' Style picture: the place's master painting (style-glasgow.jpg) sent at 768 x 1368. Flux 3 edit, 2k, aspect auto, png, safety 2; returns 1504 x 2672, resized to the plate.

inventory.name: Story reaches the lower part of the frame (rule 7, story_reaches_down 0.70)
inventory.how_found: Log 34 round 4: a fresh critic found every Works view passed the main rule while the story sat 0.53-0.65 down over bare paving; round 5 added a checker rule and brought W1/W2 3 m nearer (plate 13.0 -> 10.0 m, composed 11.8 -> 8.8 m from the wall). Lesson 133.

calculators.name: Frame geometry core and shared film settings
calculators.file: kit/calculators/frame_geometry.py (Python) + kit/paper-film/scenes/frame-geometry.js (same sums for pages) + kit/film-settings.json (one table of house numbers read by every tool)
calculators.what_it_computes: Where any 3D point lands on the 1080 x 1920 film frame (or the 1536 x 2730 plate) without rendering anything: across and down, depth, size in pixels, metres per pixel, where the street's lines meet, how far a camera may stand to reach a given 'down', the eye height needed, how much a turn or a sideways slide moves things, how much a near thing slides against what is behind it. Every other calculator calls it. The settings file holds every fixed number once, so the tools can't drift apart (today the default page pause is 1.4 s in assemble_chapter_narration.py and 1.5 s in estimate_timeline.py; frame_check.py uses 140/380 px margins while rule 12 uses 0.90/0.95).
calculators.inputs: A camera (Blender position plus target, or yaw/pitch, vertical lens angle; or a works-camera-*.json / notice-corner-camera.json); points, directions and sizes in Blender metres; film-settings.json.
calculators.outputs: Python and JS functions plus a CLI: frame_geometry.py project|vp|size|reach|eye|turn|slide|parallax --camera FILE ... printing plain lines and --json. frame_check.py becomes a thin wrapper that takes 8 box corners per thing instead of one point.
calculators.method: Settings (film-settings.json): frame [1080,1920], fps 30, film_fov 60.4, plate_fov 64.4, plate [1536,2730]; safe area: words right edge <= 0.90 across, story props <= 0.95 in the button strip 0.45-0.95 down, left >= 65 px (0.06), letter tops >= 0.06 down, title band 0.05-0.22 down, nothing to read below 0.80 (380 px); first_word_at 1.08, tail 4.0, default_pause 1.4 (both timeline tools), turn_after_last_word 0.3, peel 0.85; voice -16 LUFS, mix -15, music-only -14, true peak -1.0 dBTP, music_level -11 dB and the duck constants; every check_shot.py threshold (moved out of the code into one named table); frame-cost classes; a dated fallback price table. Sums: f = (H/2)/tan(V/2); horizontal lens = 2*atan(tan(V/2)*W/H). Blender (x,y,z) -> three.js (x,z,-y). Camera axes: fwd = norm(target - cam), right = norm(fwd x (0,0,1)), up = right x fwd. A point p: d = p - cam, depth = d.fwd, across = 0.5 + f*(d.right)/(depth*W), down = 0.5 - f*(d.up)/(depth*H). Where a direction D's lines meet: same with d = D (D.fwd > 0). Level camera turned psi left, street (0,1,s): across = 0.5 + f*tan(psi)/W, down = 0.5 - f*s/(H*cos(psi)); turn for a wanted across u: psi = atan((u - 0.5)*W/f). Size: px = size_m*f/depth; metres per pixel = depth/f; share of frame = area_m2*(f/d)^2/(W*H). Ground point at depth d: down = v_meet + f*eye/(d*H); deepest a story thing may stand to reach r down: d_max = f*eye/((r - v_meet)*H); eye needed for depth d to reach r: eye = z_ground + (r - v_meet)*H*d/f. One degree of turn moves things f*(pi/180)/W of the width. Sideways slide for a screen shift du at depth z: s = du*W*z/f. Parallax of a near thing at depth d against the surface behind at d_b: sideways slide s gives f*s*|1/d - 1/d_b| px; forward slide L gives p*L*(d_b - d)/((d - L)*(d_b - L)) px, p = its px from the frame centre.
replaces_items: Lens numbers every placement sum rests on
Turn-to-meeting-point conversion: 1 degree of turn = about 0.027 of frame width
Where the street's lines meet, worked out from the camera
Frame with numbers before rendering (edge margins)
Words clear of phone buttons (safe area)

calculators.name: Check file generator

calculators.what_it_computes: The shot check file that check_shot.py, shot_facts.py, the painter's prompt builder and the state planner all read, made from the Blender scene instead of by hand: groups, roles, must_read, pairs_also, on_ground, lights_in_story, lines, eye height range, title zone, story_reaches_down, match_excludes and one group per figure.
calculators.inputs: The assembled .blend, the view's camera, a short shot entry (subject, support, optional story list, which lights belong to the story), the street builder's settings (slope), lettering-sizes.json, optionally shot_facts' ids.png for the title zone.

calculators.method: Groups: one per root empty of each imported .glb (second copies first renamed '<instance>-<part>'), every figure its own group, at most 20 groups a view (shot_facts palette limit; merge far background groups of one kind if over). Story = subject + support + props whose footprint is within 1.5 m (box gap) of the support and no deeper than the support + 0.1 m; work = all other props; pairs_also = every named group not in the story (background near-touches included). on_ground = groups whose lowest vertex is within 0.05 m of the ground found by a ray cast from below the object after view_layer.update(). must_read = groups holding a material named *-lettering, *-stencil, *-printing or *paper, or listed in lettering-sizes.json; the same materials are written into the page's ownSurface list. lights_in_story = lights inside a story group's box grown 0.2 m. lines = {street: [0, 1, tan(slope)], level: [0, 1, 0]}. eye_height = [floor_offset + 1.5, floor_offset + 1.9], floor_offset = height of the floor the viewer stands on above the surface shot_facts hits under the camera (0 on a pavement, the sill for a window view). title_zone = largest rectangle inside 0.05-0.90 across and 0.02-0.22 down of ids.png that is >= 85% sky, holds no light and no story prop over 1% (fallback [0.06, 0.05, 0.90, 0.22]). story_reaches_down 0.70 by default. match_excludes = groups with mean plate brightness < 0.08 or median mask width < 6 px (dark waiting men, iron gates, thin bars), read by an updated check_shot.py instead of the scratch wrapper check_dark_picture.py.

calculators.what_it_computes: From the shot list and the props' measured sizes it places the camera (x, height, turn), the composed and plate spots, the slide and its longest safe length, the plate's lens and size, the people (spacing, rows, turns, distances) and the props' turns, then predicts the composition numbers the checker would measure (rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 12, the main-rule spot box, subject share, faces) and refuses a plan that breaks them. Blender then confirms with fast Workbench facts instead of trial renders.
calculators.inputs: Shot entry (place, view, subject and support position and size, story props, work props, figures with count and pose, street direction and slope, where the viewer stands: pavement, window, yard), ground heights (street builder settings or an exported height grid), props/index.json (true sizes and front axis per model), film-settings.json, optional landmarks read from a liked picture.
calculators.outputs: <view>-plan.json: composed and plate camera (x, y, z, yaw), eye height, slide start/end, L and L_max, plate lens and pixels, eye_height range for the check file, predicted numbers per rule with pass/fail, figure positions and turns with head px and nearest distance from every camera position along the slide, prop turns; a printed table in plain words.
calculators.method: 1 Rule 1 (sideways place): camera x on the support's near edge along the street (subject's edge when there is no support); predicted gap = 2D distance from the meeting point to the support's projected outline (as check_shot check_lines), limit 0.03 of width = 0.03*W*d/f metres (0.096 m at 4.9 m). 2 Rule 2: z = ground(x, y) + 1.7 (1.5-1.9; 1.81 when matching a reference), rotation (90, 0, psi); lift the subject so its key corner sits at eye height above its own ground (the lines meet at eye height on a street that rises with its lines). 3 Turn: wanted meeting point u* = 0.895 - subject's screen width - 0.01 (mirror when the subject is left of it); psi = atan((u* - 0.5)*W/f). 4 Distance: nearest story thing's front foot at d <= d_max = f*eye/((0.70 - v_meet)*H); figures seen from behind >= 6 m (a 1.75 m man is a quarter of the height at f*1.75/(0.25*H) = 6.0 m); a figure whose face could show needs head_px = 0.23*f/d <= 24 (d >= 15.8 m) or becomes an own-surface silhouette or is turned away; subject share about 3% (2.9-3.3%): d = f*sqrt(A/(0.03*W*H)), or scale the subject. 5 Overview views: raise the eye to z_ground + (0.70 - v_meet)*H*d/f for the nearest story element, never tilt. 6 Pavement spot: search x across the walkable strip in 0.1 m steps; keep the near facade within 0.20 of the frame side, the subject's far edge <= 0.88, and no upright pipe or post within 0.3 m of the camera-to-subject line. 7 Rule 3: story spread across the view <= 0.40*W*d/f (0.262*d m at 60.4 deg), height <= 0.50*H*d/f (0.582*d m) or the reference's box + 0.02; every story prop within 0.3 m (footprint gap) of another, none deeper than support + 0.1 m. 8 Rule 4 and edge runs: project mesh silhouettes (convex hull of vertices; figures as cylinders r 0.28 m, h 1.74 m); signed distance must be <= -ceil(20*W/1536) px (15 at 1080) or >= ceil(25*W/1536) (18); upright edges at different depths at least 18 px apart over their shared rows; fix = move the back thing (need + 4 px - distance)*d/f metres. 9 Rule 8: work prop of height h stands between f*(eye - h/2)/((0.62 - v_meet)*H) and f*(eye - h/2)/((0.47 - v_meet)*H), covers <= 0.02*W*H*(d/f)^2 m2, unlit; silhouettes in the bottom-left quarter <= 1%. 10 Rule 12: every must_read right edge <= 0.895 across, story props <= 0.945 in 0.45-0.95 down; fix by sliding sideways (u - limit)*W*z/f m, never turning, then recheck the rule 1 gap. 11 Slide and plate: end = composed spot; start = end - L*unit(horizontal end-to-subject-centre), same height and turn; L_max = d_end*(ratio - 1), ratio = (plate_H/H)*tan(film_V/2)/tan(plate_V/2) = 1.314; plate drawn from the start; plate lens = 2*atan(largest corner tan needed while the film camera's corner rays, cast to the set every 10% of the slide, are projected into the start camera) + the 0.03 frame-edge fade; default film + 4 deg; turn allowance (Hfov(plate) - Hfov(film))/2; sideways allowance z_near*(tan_plate_x - tan_film_x). 12 People: a group's long axis must make >= 60 deg with every view that sees it; place a loose crowd two deep across the view (0.3-0.5 m between shoulders, back row 0.8 m behind, turns 4-16 deg, scale 0.96-1.04), jitter 0.1 m / 15 deg and keep the layout where every pair of heads has a gap >= 15 px or an overlap >= 15 px (never 0-15 px) in every view; every figure >= 6 m from every camera position along every slide; turn a head 5 deg at a time away from the strongest light while both lit_face = max(0, n.l)*P/r^2 and visible_face = n.c exceed 0.2. 13 Prop turns: turn = atan2(target - prop) + the model's front offset from index.json. 14 Predicted spots (meeting point, subject centre, story centroid) inside 0.30 x 0.40 to leave room for the render's spread. Blender companion: shot_facts in Workbench (about 15 s) then check_shot's layout tiers (set-up, camera, resting, missing, lines, story, edges) in ranking order; apply its metre fixes, re-measure, at most 5 rounds; EEVEE only once no layout problem is left. Landmark mode: Nelder-Mead over (x, height, turn, lens), steps 0.3 m, 0.3 m, 1.5 deg, 4 deg; pass within 0.1 m height, 0.15 m sideways, 0.75 deg, 2 deg (match_camera.py from experiments/31 promoted).
