calculators.name: Camera path audit for moving shots
calculators.file: kit/paper-film/tools/camera_audit.py (extend the existing tool with --built-set, --relief and --plate modes)
calculators.what_it_computes: From the camera samples of a built page: the number of named moves per shot, creeps, still share, and for built-and-painted sets: any turn during a slide, how far the street's meeting point drifts, the slide's magnification, whether the frame ever leaves the painted plate; in painted relief rooms the parallax of each move and any rise during a pan. It takes the page window from the timeline itself.
calculators.inputs: render-paper-film.mjs SCENE --camera FILE.json 3 samples (position, target, fov, focus, shot name), timeline.json, page kind (paper, relief, projected set), the projector camera.json, the street direction from the check file, the relief's depth picture statistics.
calculators.outputs: Per shot OK/PROBLEM lines with numbers, the move-end times for weights-view stills, JSON for the preflight.
calculators.method: Keep the tuned thresholds: moving when the aim turns > 0.6 deg/s, or travel > 1.2% of the focus distance per s, or lens change > 1.2%/s; moves under 0.35 s apart are one; a cut is a jump > 0.25 of the distance or a turn > 8 deg or a new stillShot name; PROBLEM above 3 moves or still < 25% of the shot. New: window = [firstWordAt(page) - 0.8, lastWordEnd(page) + 1.3] from the timeline; creep = one move longer than the sentence it serves. Built-set mode: PROBLEM if heading or pitch changes > 0.1 deg inside a move, or the meeting point's across (frame_geometry vp of the street direction) varies > 0.02 between the move's samples; magnification d_start/d_end <= 1.314. Plate mode: every 0.1 s cast the 4 frame corners and 4 edge midpoints to the set (depth from the plate's depth picture) and project into the projector camera; all must fall inside [0.03, 0.97] (projected-set frameEdge). Relief mode: parallax = f*t*(1/z_near - 1/z_far), z_near = 5th percentile depth inside the frame; cap = the largest value among chapter 2's accepted 1-2 unit moves; a camera rise during a pan is a PROBLEM (tears). Stand-ins: a sideways step > 1% of the subject distance needs a repainted background, not a free fill.

calculators.name: Lettering, figure and landmark audit per view
calculators.what_it_computes: For every view of a place: letter height in pixels of every sign (with foreshortening), whether must-read words face the camera, the turn that makes a curved stencil face its cameras, signs louder than the subject that the page never names (and the dim value), backs of signs that show, head sizes of figures, tall landmarks that hit the typed-words band, background things that borrow an identifying feature, signs meant for one view showing in another, and figure and feature counts per view for continuity. Given a still, the contrast behind every typed title and the soft dark band needed.
calculators.inputs: The place's shot json (cameras per view, sign positions and normals, chimney tops, figures), lettering-sizes.json and props index letter heights, check files, the timeline's words per page and the page-to-view map, optional stills and the typed titles' boxes.
calculators.outputs: Per view table (sign, letter px, facing factor, verdict; head px; landmark top 'down'), required letter heights, dim values, band opacities, continuity table; JSON for the preflight.
calculators.method: letter_px = h*f/d*|n.(-v)| (n sign normal, v unit view ray). Must-read: key lines >= 18 px, a single word >= 25 px, a headline the viewer must read 40-60 px; below 16 px the word must be carried by a typed label. Needed letter height = target_px*d/f at the shot's end frame. Facing: |n.(-v)| >= 0.85 for must-read words; a sign whose back shows (n.(cam - p) < 0) needs back lettering. Curved stencil turn = atan2(cam_x - x, -(cam_y - y)) in the stencil's own frame (faces -y at 0); for several views choose the turn maximising the smallest |cos|. Loud unnamed sign: legible (>= 20 px), not spoken on that page, px >= 1.2 x the subject's letters -> dim = min(0.3, 0.4*B_least_named/B_own) until the word is first said. Landmark top: down = 0.5 - (h_top - eye)*f/(d*H); flag above the band bottom + 0.02 (0.24) and print the height giving 0.24, h = eye + 0.26*H*d/f, or say 'put words beside it'; ray-cast each identifying feature's visible length (>= 200 px tall in the overview). Identity: background objects of the same kind inside a feature's screen column (+-0.05) and as tall -> flag; two places' identifying features must differ by >= 40 levels in the plate. Heads: head_px = 0.23*f/d; a face that can show (facing within 100 deg of the camera) above 24 px -> silhouette or turn. Signs for one view: project into every other view; inside the frame -> flag. Continuity: counts of figures and identifying parts per view against the state table. With a still: contrast = (L1 + 0.05)/(L2 + 0.05) over the word box grown 20 px; below 4.5 add a band of opacity a = 1 - ((L_text + 0.05)/4.5 - 0.05)/L_bg (light text); title zone brightness <= 0.36 or sky share < 0.6 -> band. Mixed fonts: OCR each rendered title (tesseract --psm 7) letter by letter.

calculators.name: Light planner and tuner
calculators.file: kit/calculators/plan_lights.py (before any render) + kit/paper-film/blender/tune_lights.py (bpy loop on small EEVEE renders measured by check_shot.py's light rules)
calculators.what_it_computes: Starting watts, reach, cone, aim, colour and links of every light from distances; which lights may cast shadows; EEVEE shadow memory settings; lamps that land on the subject or light a wall brighter than the subject; glow and glass material faults; exposure per view and look settings by page type; then a tuning loop that moves watts and reach until the light rules pass, instead of 26 hand rounds.
calculators.inputs: The scene's lights (or a lights JSON), the check file (subject, support, story, lights_in_story, subject_dark), ray casts into the set, plates or stills for exposure, page type.
calculators.outputs: A light plan JSON and a bpy script applying it, a tuning log (each try and its numbers), exposure per view, look settings, warnings.
calculators.method: Blender spot watts light the subject like a point light of the same watts (the cone only masks; confirm once): irradiance E = P/(4*pi*d^2). A lamp near a prop starts at P = P_key*(d_lamp/d_key)^2. Reach (custom distance) = farthest target point + 0.2 m and must stop short of the first non-target surface along the beam (ray cast), else move the light. Cone = 2*atan(subject half-diagonal/d) + 10 deg, blend 0.9; aim at the subject's bottom-edge centre for 'lit from below'; fire key colour (1.0, 0.42, 0.12), lamps above pale (1.0, 0.97, 0.94). Default links: a light skips the object it sits in and anything whose box is within 0.2 m; a key light reaches only subject + support; a container's light skips the container and props within 0.6 m; rim lights reach figures only; doorway spills skip the workers inside. Shadows only from the key/fire, the lit doorways and the sky; figures visible_shadow off with a soft 0.5 x 0.35 m foot patch; plate minutes about 4 + 6*shadow_lights/3. EEVEE shadow_pool_size '1024', shadow_resolution_scale = min(1, 1080/width); after every render search the log for 'Shadow buffer full' and 'Could not allocate shadow atlas' and refuse the picture. Materials: emission > 0 with base brightness > 0.05 -> black base; glass alpha fed by a picture -> unhook. Lamp faults: project every set lamp; within 18 px of the subject's outline or 0.03 of the meeting point -> move or remove; a light whose brightest camera-facing non-subject surface (P*cos(theta)/r^2) beats the subject -> move to the inner face and scale by subject target/current. Dark subject (subject_dark in the check file): instead of 'subject brightest', the band behind it >= 2.5 x its mean, add a backlight. Three.js stages: one shadow-casting light; bias = 1.5*(shadow camera width/mapSize); paper words 0.55 units out, pieces d_min = (margin + 0.1h)/tan(a); folded props with > 10% inward faces get normalBias 0; reflections inside paintings = clamp(painting brightness near the models/0.5, 0.1, 1); room light level scales emissive and base colour (0.15 + 0.85*level). Exposure per view: one still at 1.0, exposure = clamp(target/measured, 0.8, 1.8), target 45-55 levels after the grade, one more pass. Look by page type: projected set {exposure 1.0, aperture 4.0, maxBlur 2, glowThreshold 0.9, glowStrength 0.6, contrast 1.04, vignette 0.3, reflections 0.2}; relief room {reflections 0.3, keyShare 0.6-0.8}. Tuning loop (EEVEE 540 x 960, 16 samples, about 1 min each, at most 8 rounds): bisection on each warm light's watts, and reach first when warm light spreads (reach x sqrt(3%/share)), until: subject >= 1.8 x frame mean, >= 40% of the brightest 3% on it and >= 75% in the story box, warm share 1.5-3% with >= 50% inside the story box grown 6%, lift (r-b)/(r+b) bottom 15% minus top 15% >= 0.10 (aim 0.17), each top-third cell <= 0.36, no story prop's 95th percentile >= subject median - 0.05 (light props: <= 10% of themselves), burnt <= 0.02% of frame and 3% of any group; quiet side 40-48% by lighting 1-3 windows (0.05-0.42 across, 0.25-0.48 down, every other one, emission 1.2), never by a big fill; sky strength by bisection 1.0-2.5 for the reference's frame mean (about 0.30). Exposure: frame share above 0.95 brightness > 2% -> lower by log2(p99/0.92).

calculators.name: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
calculators.what_it_computes: Before paying: whether the plate is ready to paint, the main and behind prompts written from the check file and shot facts, the list of near things for the behind painting, the pictures to send and their sizes, and the price, written to the paintings ledger.
calculators.inputs: Plate PNG and its render log, shot facts measured with the plate lens (facts.json, ids.png, solo masks), check file, place entry (place, era, time of day), the page's live effects, the place's prop library, the style or master painting, the research ledger's real names, today's fal rate, the spend ledger.
calculators.outputs: request JSON (model blackforestlabs/flux-3/edit-image, resolution 2k, aspect auto, png, safety 2; image 1 the plate 1536 x 2730, image 2 the style picture at about 1 MP, 768 x 1368), the prompt texts, the near list for after_painting, a preflight report whose failures stop the request, and the cost line.
calculators.method: Preflight: (a) no RENDER_FAULTS in the log; (b) check_shot's light rules pass; (c) thin parts: thin = mask - opening(mask, k = max(3, round(6*W/1080)), odd); > 5% of a group -> remove or thicken, else named in the prompt; (d) lettering under 24 px on screen must be an own surface, not in the plate; (e) even bright discs (spread < 2 levels, strongly coloured, > 0.3% of frame) or near-black holes (< 5 levels) inside the story box -> flag; (f) model lint stripe count 0; (g) figures from behind: mean of the band under the cap darker than the coat; (h) every figure's and large prop's mean colour pushed through the stage's grade: hue inside 345-15 deg (red) or a party/chain hue with saturation > 0.5 -> flag, propose the plate colour that grades to the wanted hue; (i) round objects (aspect 0.7-1.3) within 0.25 m above a hung garment's collar; (j) no real person's name from the ledger in any prompt or piece name; every figure's and prop's era matches the page's. Prompt sections: 1 fixed header word for word ('Repaint image 1 completely as a hand-painted illustration in the exact painting style of image 2 ... Nothing should look like a 3D render or a photograph any more.' + 'Keep image 1's camera, framing, perspective and every shape ...'); 2 place, era, light in one sentence; 3 'Keep:' every group showing over 0.1% of the frame, in order subject, support, story, pairs_also, work, landmarks, each with its paint_as text from the check file (default: props index 'what'), 'darker than <subject>' for story props, 'small, far up the street' beyond 10 m, its state ('shut'); 4 lights: lamps with warm glass and a small mantle, 'Warm light stays only where it already is: <groups owning > 10% of the plate's warm mask>', 'Nothing is brighter than <subject>'; 5 thin parts; 6 edges that meet or nearly meet: pairs whose signed distance lies between -2 x overlap and 2 x gap, plus intended overlaps; 7 people: count near (< 15 m) and far, facing from turn against the camera, 'No faces anywhere' if any head > 25 px, 'Add no people and remove none'; 8 lettering: '<group> with plain marks, no readable letters'; 9 never-add core (flames, sparks, smoke, steam, glows, halos, light rays, people, animals, extra props, puddles, reflections, moon, stars, bright clouds, new signs or lettering, new or longer shadows) + removed parts + absent library props of the place + the page's live effects. Behind prompt: near list = groups whose parallax over the slide exceeds 1 px (sideways f*s*|1/d - 1/d_b|; forward p*L*(d_b - d)/((d - L)(d_b - L))), what lies behind them = material names hit by rays through their pixels with them hidden, mapped to plain words; 'Remove ... (and their shadows, for figures). Where each one was, continue exactly what lies behind it: ... Keep everything else exactly as it is: ... Add nothing new.' Cost = rate_per_MP*(MP_out + sum MP_in), rate read live (fal get_pricing or estimate_cost), fallback the dated table; refuse when it would pass what is left of the allowance (budget planner).

calculators.name: Painting arrival checks
calculators.what_it_computes: The fixed chain for every returned painting, with pass marks: resize to the plate, line it up, line the behind painting up against it, keep the painted shadows round the near props (groups and width computed), check every figure's outline, colour continuity with the place's master painting, a painted-not-photo score, party colours, lossless saving; for the painted-room look, cut-out and depth-picture checks and colour calming of cut-outs.
calculators.inputs: Returned painting(s), the plate, plate shot facts, check file, near list from paint_request, the place's master painting, style picture; for cut-outs the painting and mask; for reliefs the depth picture.
calculators.outputs: Aligned and combined PNGs, a report with pass/fail and what to re-ask (a paid re-ask still needs the user's yes), tone factors for cut-outs.
calculators.method: Resize to 1536 x 2730 (area filter). align_painting.py: accept agreement >= 0.85 after and |stretch - 1| <= 0.01, else re-ask; behind painting with --against: >= 0.95. keep_painted_shadows.py with groups = the near list and widen = the measured width of the painter's dark rim round props (default 10 px); then the ground band 10-30 px beside each near prop may change <= 2 levels between the main and combined pictures. Figures: chamfer distance from each plate outline to the painting's edges; within-3-px share >= 0.90 (near) or >= 0.70 (far) and IoU >= 0.85, else the painter moved, added or lost a figure; figure-sized edge blobs outside every outline -> added person. Colour continuity: mean CIELAB per group against the master painting, delta E > 8 -> repaint (tune on the first pair). Painted score: edge density and colour flatness (k-means 16) against the style picture; < 70% of it -> photo-like, re-ask once. Party/chain colours: regions > 1.5% of frame with saturation > 0.45 in listed hues; yellow-and-black stripes. Save PNG only; refuse JPEG for any painting used as a base. Cut-outs: missing paint = pixels > 30 levels from the grey backdrop with alpha < 0.5 (flag > 1% of the object); see-through = alpha 0.1-0.9 over > 3% inside the hull (lower the threshold); > 3 islands -> print on a card; sheet = alpha box + 4% margin, fail if alpha touches the edge; contact sheet captioned with prompt and ledger id after each batch; tone: a piece > 1.2 x the page's median saturation gets factor median/own on all its layers. Reliefs: equalise depth; warn if 90% of pixels sit in < 20 grey levels; blur 3. Stand-ins: projector-view render against the painting, mean difference <= 5 levels and share over 12 levels <= 7%.

calculators.name: State picture planner
calculators.what_it_computes: From the pages' events: every plate a place needs (one per change timed on its own word), which groups change, how big each swap will be, whether each change is a time cut or a blend and how long, whether the cue that changes is in frame, and the exact make_state_picture.py and make_behind_picture.py commands with thresholds from measured noise.
calculators.inputs: Page events from page_events.mjs (state changes with their words and views, slides), the place's state table (windows, lights, figures per state), check files per state, rendered plate pairs.
calculators.outputs: Plate list (view, state, groups hidden or shown, shadow settings), predicted and measured mask shares, cut or blend with duration, commands, warnings.
calculators.method: Plates: one per distinct (view, state after change k) in event order; a change that bundles two sub-changes timed on different words is split into two plates; every sliding view gets a behind plate = its main state with the near things hidden; window panes are split into N step groups, N = the number of distinct lit fractions in the states. Outline groups = the symmetric difference of the two states' groups plus groups whose facts (position, visible area) differ by > 1%, measured with the plate lens. Lights not tied to the change must be identical in both plates (compare their settings). Things that come and go: cast no shadows, get foot patches; predicted mask = their outlines grown 12*W/1536 px; flag mask/outline area > 3 (long shadows or blocked light) and any cut over 15%. Cut or blend: share <= 0.12 -> time cut on the word's start; otherwise blend 0.8 + 0.7*(share/0.75) s, at most 1.5 s, in 3 steps (steppedBlend); refuse any change inside a slide; a cut where only people change -> warn 'change something else in the same frame'. Cue in frame: >= 60% of the changing cue's box inside the frame and below the title band in every view showing that state; a 'busy' or 'working' state needs a figure inside a lit area (head <= 24 px, darker than the wall behind by >= 3x). Thresholds = max(6, 3*noise99), faint = max(3, 3*noise_smooth); PNG only; 0 levels different outside the mask.

calculators.name: Effects planner (smoke, wind, fire, dust, contact shadows)
calculators.what_it_computes: Wind for each place chosen against its cameras, every chimney plume traced on each view's frame before filming, emitters to drop, plume colour and mouth, flame variety and glow pulse, contact shadows for props the behind painting removes, dust emitter places, particle pre-roll, and the measured change of each teaching event.
calculators.inputs: The place's shot json (chimney tops, emitters, cameras per view), title and card boxes per page, effect settings (the kinds in works-effects.js), near props and footprints, page times, stills for change measurements.
calculators.outputs: Wind vector, a per-view trace table, pass/fail per view and kind, emitters to drop, contact shadow sizes and fade times, boost factors.
calculators.method: Wind: the horizontal unit vector that maximises the smallest |sin(angle to each view's direction)| (views along +-y give +-x), sign toward the side with room (away from other identifying chimneys and cards); add 0.5 away from the main camera and 0.12 downward, normalise. Trace (same sums as ChimneySmoke): k = age/life, climb = rise*k^0.75, blown = drift*k^1.25, size from the mouth size (first 2 s) to [a, b] by rest^0.8, strength = opacity*min(1, age/0.2)*(1 - k)^fade, projected with frame_geometry. Pass: travel on screen while strength >= 0.1 is >= 0.15 of the width; puff centres below the lowest card's bottom (or a band is drawn); strength < 0.1 at least 0.05 across before another identifying chimney; no puff with strength > 0.2 over a figure's box; an emitter outside the frame for the whole shot is dropped; mouth >= the chimney top's diameter; plume brightness 20-40 levels from the sky behind it. Fire: 3-5 ragged flames, size +-30%, lean +-15 deg, glow radius swing <= 1.5%. Pre-roll = the longest particle life for emitters that keep state (0 for seeded functions of time). Contact shadow for every prop in behind.hide: size about 1.2 x footprint diagonal, 0.012 m above ground, opacity 0.55, fading in over 0.8 s from the slide's start. Dust: if a nearer piece covers the landing point, put the emitter just in front of the landing piece, starting at the cover's top + 0.1; for words z - 0.1; particles stay in their room box and end with their page. Teaching events: stills at the word and 0.6 s after; mean change over the cue mask >= 15 levels, else boost x 15/measured. Lint: every emitter made through kit.effect.

calculators.name: Script and narration gate
calculators.file: kit/narration-tools/lint_script.py (and sync estimate_timeline.py into the plugin)
calculators.what_it_computes: Before paying for the voice: script lint (cue, capitals, names, sentence length, figures per minute, the rule said twice, unfamiliar words, stakes early, terms with several meanings, who 'they' are, out-of-date facts), guess holds, the estimated timeline with words a minute per page, and the credits and dollars. After recording: cues read aloud, names said wrongly, late first words after pauses, and the pages to re-record.
calculators.inputs: Narration script JSON (pages, phonetic_names, key-page marks), research ledger (claims, sources, valid_until), a 5,000 common-words list, an earlier word-times file of the same voice, transcripts after recording.
calculators.outputs: Lint report (errors stop the paid step), timeline-estimated.json with --pause-after filled, per-page table (words, seconds, wpm), credits and US$, re-record list.
calculators.method: Cues: exactly one [..] at the start of every page, identical on every page, no other brackets. No all-capital token of 2 or more letters except a whitelist (NZ, GDP). Names only in their phonetic_names respellings. Sentences: mean <= 12 words (aim about 9), none over 20; spoken figures per estimated minute <= 4; years in order (at most 1 reversal); words outside the common list with no explanation within 2 sentences; the main rule sentence present exactly twice, word for word; a stake in the first 30 estimated seconds; term table of every repeated key noun with its sentences (one word, one meaning, read by a person); 'X says' lines whose ledger source is not X; facts past valid_until. Guess pages (last sentence a question to the viewer or containing 'guess') get pause_after 4.0; a '...' must leave >= 1.0 s in the recording. Timeline: estimate_timeline.py (word = base + per-letter x letters + extra for its ending, median gaps, scaled so the measured recording reproduces its real length); flag pages above 1.1 x the chapter median or 170 wpm, and a key page above the median. Cost: credits = sum of page text lengths including the cue; US$ = credits x 0.000175. After recording: transcript against script minus brackets; any cue word or extra word -> re-record; a name not matching -> re-record; the voice-onset correction (already in extract_word_times.py) also for the first word after any silence over 0.5 s; a record_page wrapper downloads at once and saves pageN.mp3 and pageN-words.json.

calculators.method: Lookups: each at/end without n where key(w) occurs more than once on the page -> fail listing every time with 3 words either side (or make wordClock throw). Pause after a page = clamp(0.3 + 0.85 + 0.2 x pieces folding away first, 1.1, 1.7); guess pages 4.0. Joins: same view and camera across the boundary -> 'run-on'; a hold >= 3 s at the boundary -> cut; else peel at last word + 0.3 s for 0.85 s; a join must end >= 0.1 s before the next page's first word. Rests: gaps between visual events that overlap speech > 1.7 s (2.5 s on the end card) -> fail. Readable time = min(until, next cut) - (at + delay), delay 0.55 s for callouts (0.12 with wordsWithLine), 0.14 s for buildWords; fail < 1.0 s; a key conclusion needs cut - at >= 1.2 s (one frame tolerance), else start on an earlier word of its clause. Anything whose until is within one frame of a cut -> fadeOut 0. Same-box lines: new.at >= old.until (fade counted inside until), else set old.until = new.at - 1/30. Margins: letter tops >= 0.06 x H, right edge <= 972 px, left >= 65 px, words in the band 0.05-0.22 down unless placed as labels, nothing to read below 0.80. Word groups per page <= round(seconds/6) + spoken figures. Typed words: every content word and number must be spoken within +-3 s of the line's start (exact, stem, or number words: '8 MILLION' = 'eight million'); unmatched words listed for a person to accept or cut. A card or pointer's target state must match its claim (small table: made -> working, quiet -> quiet). Numbers: shown value within half its last digit of the ledger value, qualifiers kept ('up to', 'about'); counts end <= at(number word) + 0.1 and hold >= max(1.0, 0.5 + 0.15 x characters) s. Slides: start and stop words 2.5-4.1 s apart, at most one per shot in built sets; state changes only while the camera holds. Stills: every event + 0.25 s, each move's start, middle and end, each page's last word + 0.3, 0.7 and 1.2 s (whole chapter in one run), projector view at each shot's start, weights view at each move's end; contact sheets 1 frame a second for an overview and 2 a second for moving shots; 390 px phone copies. Planned cuts: stillShot name changes, still-key steps, joins. camera_audit window [first word - 0.8, last word end + 1.3]. Re-record: compare page start times old and new; chunks whose frame range moved are deleted and re-filmed (from the first changed page unless its pause absorbs the change). Skeleton: from shots.json write the T table with kit.at(word, n), one stillShot per shot with its slide from start word to stop word, and draw2D stubs.

calculators.name: Page pose sampler (layout, clearance, fades and held shots)
calculators.what_it_computes: What single stills miss: standing pieces leaving the frame at their own distance, rows too wide for the tall frame, words overlapping things, pieces in the header band or too small, clearance and poking through, stage models floating, knocked-down pieces showing blank backs, thin props seen from too high, one-frame pops, fades that snap off half way, effects outliving their page, still keys that change during moves or are missing on holds.
calculators.inputs: Page files, timeline, the kit (room.clearance, boxesOverlap, toScreen), film-settings.json.
calculators.outputs: Per-page problem list with times and numbers to fix (largest allowed x per piece, worst clearance per pair).
calculators.method: Sample every event time and every 0.1 s during moves. Standing piece: visible half-width at its depth w(z) = (D - z)*tan(Hfov/2); require |x| + half-width <= w(z)*(1 - 2*140/1080) and print the largest allowed |x|. Row: sum of widths + gaps <= 2*w(z)*(1 - 2*140/1080), else stagger in depth with 10-30% overlap. Text boxes against every other box; header band intrusions; pieces < 60 px tall. clearance >= 0 (>= 0.05 standing, >= 0.15 in the air) sampled across faces, boxesOverlap for every visible pair; stage card models: downward ray gap <= 0.03, price tags >= 15 units in front of the painted room's depth. Knocked-down pieces: fold > 60 deg toward the camera with the centre in the lower 40% for > 0.3 s -> warn. Camera tilt > 35 deg onto a thin horizontal prop whose silhouette shrinks below 40% of side-on -> warn. Any opacity, light or position change completed in < 3 frames that is not a planned cut -> flag; opacity < 1 on a cut-out without the see-through switch (alphaTest 0.5) -> flag until CutOut.set is fixed. Still key changing inside a move -> flag; a hold without a still key -> warn (5 x slower). Objects of a page visible after it hides -> fail; emitters not made through kit.effect -> fail.

calculators.name: Sound calculator and gates
calculators.file: kit/narration-tools/sound_gates.py (called by mix_narration_over_music.sh, add_music_bed.sh and finish_film.sh)
calculators.what_it_computes: The music level for any soundtrack by measuring the gap under the voice, the length after every audio step, the finished copy's loudness, true peak and alignment, the voice steadiness verdict per page, each page's levelling gain, the soundtrack stretch for music-only clips, and the paper mouth's thresholds from the voice.
calculators.inputs: Levelled narration, soundtrack, timeline word spans, the mix and the finished files.
calculators.outputs: music_level_db and the speech and pause gaps, pass/fail lines added to the finish report, a re-record list, the chosen soundtrack start and fades, mouth thresholds.
calculators.method: Ducking: render voice-only and ducked music-only stems through the same chain; gap_speech = median over word spans of (voice - music) short-term loudness, gap_pause the same over gaps >= 0.5 s; music_level_db += gap_speech - 18; repeat until within 1 dB (2-3 passes); flag gap_pause outside 10-14; 'slightly louder' moves the target 3 dB. Length: after every step |measured - requested| <= 0.05 s (ffprobe) or stop naming the step; aresample=48000 after any loudnorm. Page gain to -16 LUFS by volume only; flag a page needing more than 4 dB either way. Final: ebur128 peak=true on the AAC sendable copy: -15 +-0.5 LUFS and true peak <= -1.0 dBTP, else lower the limiter by (peak + 1.2) dB and re-encode the sound; music-only clips -14 LUFS. Alignment: check_sound_alignment.py inside finish_film.sh; fail if any page is off by more than 3 ms or correlation < 0.8. Voice: page typical pitch more than 1.5 semitones from the chapter median, a word 5 or more semitones up or more than 6 dB louder -> re-record that page; chapter spread target <= 2.2 semitones. Soundtrack stretch: 3 s short-term loudness; the window of the clip's length within 2 LU of the mood's target with least variance, snapped to the nearest onset; fade in 0.8 s on an onset, else 2 s; fade out 1.5 s. Mouth: QUIET = 40th percentile and LOUD = 90th percentile of voiced 40 ms slices (dB).

calculators.name: Budget, filming time, memory and disk planner
calculators.what_it_computes: The price of every paid step from today's rate, the running total against the user's allowance, the filming hours from the page plan and measured frame costs, the number of workers, the piece size, the two-hour stretches with their FILM_FROM/FILM_TO commands, lazy loading on or off, memory, disk, plate render minutes and a push check.
calculators.inputs: Painting list with sizes sent and returned, script character counts, spend ledger (00-requests.json and paintings ledgers) with the allowance and its start date, live prices, render-paper-film --info frame ranges, page events (held, moving, live, peel frames), profile_frame timings, nproc, free memory and disk, export sizes, git file list.
calculators.outputs: Cost table and running total (refuses over the allowance), filming plan with commands, hours, piece size, workers, lazy setting, memory and disk checks, push check.
calculators.method: Paintings: sum of rate x (MP_out + sum MP_in) x 1.5 (one repaint per two paintings), sketches 0.15 each, narration chars x 0.000175 + one page re-record 0.30; unique things to paint = props across pages merged, text things removed. Ledger: spent = sum of costs since the allowance's start date; print what is left before any paid call; refuse if the call is larger; a vague reply is not approval. Frame classes from page events: held with nothing live 0.8 s (0.57 with two workers), held with smoke or flicker 1.5 (1.05), moving 6.0 (no gain from two), peel x 2, paper look 0.85, model pages from profile_frame; loading 40 s a piece; x 1.5 while Blender renders. Workers = 1 if nproc <= 2 else 2 (two for held stretches, one for moving ones; speed-up 1.17 on 4 CPUs). PIECE_FRAMES = max(60, min(ceil(load_s/(0.10 x spf)), floor(900/spf))). Stretches: add pages until frames x spf / speed-up reaches 6,600 s (2 h minus 10 min); print the commands; a status/stop helper with a pid file and a heartbeat (stalled if no new piece for twice a piece's time; stop by saved pid, never pkill -f). Lazy = true when model MB x 4 > half the free memory or more than 8 heavy pages; workers <= floor((free_GB - 2)/(2.6 x views per page)); refuse to film while Blender renders. Disk: seconds x 3.5 MB x copies + exports + stills, checked before every export and stretch. Plate minutes about 4 + 6 x shadow lights/3. Push: refuse audio and video files, files over 95 MB, secrets by regex; batches under 400 MB; chat parts <= 28 MB.

calculators.name: Model lint (Blender and .glb)
calculators.what_it_computes: Model faults before plates: squashed textures that paint as stripes, surfaces on the same plane, floors laid just over ground, duplicate '.001' names and wrong roots, sizes copied from build constants instead of measured, parts bigger than their host, glass with linked alpha, glowing materials with light bases, inward faces, bevels without hardened normals, objects per material, triangle and frame-time budgets, baked labels in downloaded textures, and each model's front direction.
calculators.outputs: Per-file report, measured sizes and front axis written into index.json, suggested fixes.
calculators.method: Stripes: per textured face UV area / 3D area against the part's median; < 1e-3 -> striped, report m2 per part. Same plane: face pairs from different objects with parallel normals, < 0.1 mm apart and overlapping -> offset max(1 mm, 1e-4 x camera distance). Floors: downward ray grid; another ground within 5 cm below -> flag. Names: one root per file named as the file, no '.001', second copies renamed '<instance>-<part>'. Sizes: index sizes and letter heights measured from the saved file (within 1.5 mm); a fitted child's box <= its host's + 1 mm (or 2%). Glass and lenses: alpha fed by a picture -> unhook and set explicitly; emission > 0 with base brightness > 0.05 -> black base. Shading: > 10% faces pointing to the mesh centre -> normalBias 0 note; bevels without harden_normals; more than one object per material -> join; unbaked parts sharing a material with baked ones; bake texture = next power of 2 above 2 x on-screen size (cap 1024). Budget: a prop over 10% of the frame with < 5,000 triangles or one material -> warn; held frame > 2 s or moving > 8 s in profile_frame -> warn. Labels: OCR or small high-contrast strokes on downloaded colour maps -> candidate PAINT_OUT boxes. Front: store 'front' per model in index.json. Export names end in .glb.

calculators.name: Preflight runner, report and kit sync
calculators.what_it_computes: One command per stage (script, record, shots, plates, paint, pages, film, finish, release) that runs every calculator that applies, hashes the inputs, writes one report with pass/warn/fail plus cost and time, blocks paid and long steps on failures, requires a critique newer than every page file before filming, runs the regression stills and planted-fault tests after shared-code changes, and checks the plugin's kit against the film kit.
calculators.inputs: The project folder, the stage name, film-settings.json, every calculator's JSON output, both kit trees.
calculators.outputs: preflight-<stage>-<date>.json and a page in plain words (Markdown or an artifact), exit code 0 pass / 1 fail / 2 bad input, kit-sync list.
calculators.method: Stage graph: script -> lint_script + plan_budget cost; record -> lint_script after recording + sound_gates voice; shots -> make_check_file, plan_shot (+ solve_shot), view_audit, plan_effects, plan_states; plates -> plan_lights/tune_lights, model_lint, paint_request preflight; paint -> paint_request cost and approval, after_painting; pages -> plan_page_timing, check_page_layout, camera_audit; film -> plan_budget filming + a critique report newer than every page file with every finding fixed or accepted; finish -> sound_gates final + find_jumps with the planned cuts; release -> kit sync. Every line carries the tool's version (sha1, 8 characters); inputs hashed at start and end, report marked stale if any changed. Regression after shared-code changes: redraw kept shots (notice corner preview 540 x 960, film stills at 4.5 s and 10 s); pass if the largest difference <= 5/255 and < 0.1% of pixels differ by more than 2; after changes to check_shot.py or shot_facts.py run run-checker-tests.sh (11 planted faults, each report's first fix must name its fault). Kit sync: hash both trees, list missing and different files, every backticked path in skills and docs must exist in the kit; BLENDER, DISPLAY and the browser path read from one config written by setup. Names: log-number prefix, no 'final' or 'v2', generated files stamped with a hash and never edited by hand.
