design.tips_guide_outline:
LLM tips and tricks for making an explainer film (kit/docs/LLM tips and tricks.md; linked from make-explainer-film/SKILL.md; every tip names the calculator that checks it)

0. How to work
- Run the stage's preflight first and read its report before doing anything by hand.
- Compute before you render: project a point with frame_geometry instead of drawing a still to see where it lands.
- Make one change, then measure again. A camera fix moves everything, so fix in this order: camera, then props, then light.
- Quote measured numbers in every report, never 'looks fine'.
- Test a tool's advice by following it once (lesson 108).
- Don't edit files while helpers are checking them. Every report names its tool version.
- Read the render log before judging any light.
- For our own shots trust the 3D facts (shot_facts) over a line finder run on a picture.

1. Numbers to know
- Frame 1080 x 1920 at 30 fps. Film lens 60.4 deg (focal 1649 px); plate 64.4 deg at 1536 x 2730.
- Pixels = metres x 1649 / distance. One degree of turn moves things 0.027 of the width.
- Words left of 0.90 across, story props left of 0.95 in the button strip, letter tops at least 0.06 down, typed words in the band 0.05-0.22 down, nothing to read below 0.80.
- Story reaches 0.70 down. Men seen from behind at least 6 m away. A face that shows: head 24 px or less.
- Letters at least 18 px (25 px for a single word).
- Warm light 1.5-3% of the frame. Subject at least 1.8 x the frame's mean.
- Music 18 dB under the voice. Mix -15 LUFS, true peak -1 dBTP.

2. Script and voice
- Plan at the narrator's measured speed (about 160 wpm), never a generic 140.
- One identical cue per page. No capitals. Names respelled in English sounds.
- Sentences of about 9 words; at most 4 figures a minute; say the main rule twice, word for word.
- Give the key idea a slower page.
- A guess needs a 4 s hold; a '...' is not thinking time.
- Estimate the timeline before paying, and build the pages on it.
- Download recordings at once (the links expire after 2 hours).
- Judge the voice by numbers and re-record only flagged pages.
- Record every page before filming: a late retake means re-filming every page after it.

3. Words on screen and timing
- On-screen words are short forms of what is said; never show a year or price she doesn't say.
- Give the occurrence number for any word said twice on a page.
- Every word group must be readable for at least 1 s; start a conclusion on the first word of its phrase.
- fadeOut 0 for anything that ends on a cut.
- One line per box at a time.
- Counts finish on the spoken number and hold at least 1 s.
- A label's line leaves its target sideways and the words sit on empty ground.
- A dark band goes behind words over busy or bright backgrounds.
- About one word group every 6 s.
- Check page turns in one run of the whole chapter. Separate still times with spaces.

4. Camera
Built-and-painted sets:
- Stand where a person would (1.5-1.9 m up), in line with the subject's edge.
- Turn once to place the meeting point, then only slide; never close a gap by turning.
- Get the distance from the 0.70 reach.
- Draw the plate 4 deg wider, from the slide's start.
- Push at most 1.3x; sideways moves of a few centimetres only.
- At most 3 named moves a shot; cut instead of adding a fourth.
- Read the weights view for blue edges.
- Match a liked picture's camera by landmarks before moving any prop.
Painted relief rooms:
- Push with the lens; travel 1-2 units; never rise during a pan.
Paper pages:
- Check each piece at its own distance from the camera.
- Stack things in depth, not side by side.

5. Composition
- Every strong thing points at the subject: the meeting point, the brightest parts, the warm light, the story props.
- Props either clearly touch or clearly don't. List background props too (pairs_also).
- Work props small, far and dim. Nothing dark or big at bottom left.
- Fill the lower third with the story itself, not filler.
- A rule-of-thirds reason was tested and dropped (log 30).

6. People
- Backs to the camera at 6 m or more. Faces become silhouettes. Never paint a real person.
- Crowds stand across the view, two deep, with gaps between heads.
- Turn heads away from the fire.
- Dark matt hair, collars up. Judge coat colours after the film's grade.
- A thin rim light separates dark figures.
- No long shadows from people. When the words say people are working, show them working.
- Nothing round above a hung coat's collar.

7. Lettering
- All lettering is ours, on its own surface; ask painters for plain marks.
- Size letters from the distance. Words to be read face the camera; turn drums toward their cameras.
- Every lettered prop goes in must_read, so no fragments like 'DIESE' show.
- Dim a readable sign until the narration names it.
- Keep joints and tacks off letters. Letter the back of a board that shows from behind.
- No numbers the narrator doesn't say.

8. Light
- Give the subject its own narrow key light, from below, linked to it alone.
- Work out practical lights' watts from distances (a lamp 15 cm from a seat needs a few watts).
- Cut a light's reach before its strength. Only a few lights cast shadows.
- Glowing things get a black base colour. Lamps go on inner faces, not the faces of walls.
- Show a dark subject against a lit background.
- Tune by the checker's numbers on small renders.
- Check the painting's own warm spots too.
- Set exposure per view from its measured brightness.

9. Painting
- Fix the light in 3D first. Pass the preflight before paying.
- Build the prompt from the template; count and describe every person; forbid what the film draws live.
- Send the style picture at about 1 MP and count every picture sent in the cost.
- Line up every painting with its plate.
- Make the behind painting from the same state, then keep the painted shadows.
- Check figure outlines. Save PNG only.
- Paint the place's master view first; use it as the style picture for the rest.
- Re-ask once if the result looks like a photograph, and ask the user before paying.

10. State changes
- Swap only what changes, inside a mask.
- One plate per change on its own word.
- Cut when under about 12% of the frame changes; blend when more does.
- Never change state during a slide. Change something else along with the people.
- Use thresholds 6 and 3, and look at the mask picture.

11. Effects
- Blow smoke across the view, and trace it on every view before filming.
- Only smoke sources that are in frame and make sense in the story.
- Vary flames.
- Give a contact shadow to every prop the behind painting removes.
- Make effects through kit.effect.
- A teaching change must move the picture by at least 15 levels.

12. Models and Blender
- Measure a model before fitting anything to it.
- Cast placement rays from below, after view_layer.update().
- Rename second copies. Record each model's front direction.
- Never put two surfaces on one plane. Run the stripe check.
- Unhook the alpha on glass.
- Run EEVEE under Xvfb with shadow pool '1024'.
- One heavy job at a time. Turn .blend1 backups off.

13. Filming
- Estimate the time and tell the user before starting.
- Give held shots still keys and mark moving things with kit.moving.
- Use lazy chapters with pieces of 240 frames or more, and stretches under 2 h.
- Workers by CPU count. Stop jobs by the saved PID, never with pkill -f.
- Watch for a job stopping, not only for it finishing. Check the first stretch at once.
- Run find_jumps with the planned cuts, and check in motion.

14. Sound and finishing
- Measure lengths after each audio step. Resample after loudnorm.
- Level pages by gain only. Use the limiter with latency=1.
- Measure the encoded AAC copy, and the alignment in milliseconds.
- Deliver captions as separate files. Sendable copy 28 MB.
- Music-only clips at -14 LUFS.
- Choose the music stretch by measurement and say so.

15. Money and approval
- Get the live price. Keep a running total from the allowance's start date.
- Do the free steps first, then ask once with the exact cost.
- A vague reply is not a yes. Never work around a refusal.

16. What the calculators can't judge
- Use the judgement list below.
- Have a fresh critic compare the work with the best frame made so far, followed by a skeptic.
- Check the fixes again with a fresh checker.
- Look at stills at phone size.
- A history critic checks every painted object.
- Newcomer testers see only what a viewer sees.

17. Plugin hygiene
- Sync the kit after fixing a tool.
- Check that every named file exists.
- For built-and-painted sets, the log 30-34 rules beat the log 20 rules.
- Change numbers only in film-settings.json.

18. Top traps (one line each)
- The 192 kHz loudnorm trap.
- A word said twice.
- One-frame pops.
- A fade that snaps off half way.
- Turning during a slide.
- Smoke blowing away from the camera.
- A single-file crowd.
- Bald-looking heads.
- The grade turning coats red.
- Shadow-buffer wedges.
- The painter's 3 px shift.
- A JPEG state picture.
- pkill -f.
- The 2-hour job limit.
- A '.001' copy taken for the original.
- A size taken from a helper's picture.
- Prices that change from one day to the next.
judgement_only: Using a picture program's free-camera composition only as a sketch, and choosing which arrangement to copy (Program composition as a sketch only; Using an AI picture as a composition sketch only)
Scrapbook engraving hatch rules (that look is not in use)

Whether a detail reads as something else on a phone (little cameras, sunglasses, contour-map wood, bar-chart doorways, soap bundles, a gasholder as a tank); the tools only supply phone-size sheets and a stripe test
Period and story accuracy of pictures (wrong-era tanks, coal heaps in a lockout, snow in May, the 1984-looking brazier kept on purpose); a history critic decides
Whether motion matches the meaning of the words (a needle falling on 'raising'), beyond a small up/down word table
Whether machines read as machines and props as what they are (looms as church benches); a helper names the thing from a 300 px crop
Whether a hero prop has enough detail, beyond the triangle and material warning
Research honesty: scoping a rule exactly to its evidence, one word one meaning (the term table only lists uses), whose words stand behind 'they say'
Newcomer understanding and the 3-4 things a newcomer must see per shot (test-script-with-newcomers workflow; testers get only spoken and on-screen words)
Fresh-critic rounds against the best frame made so far, the skeptic, and the fresh check of every fix
Whether a time cut where people vanish reads as time passing or as a glitch (the planner only warns when nothing else changes)
Whether a picture contradicts a card beyond the small claims-to-states table
Whether a colour or symbol carries political or commercial meaning in context (the scan only flags hues)
Accepting or cutting an on-screen short form that the words check could not match to the narration
Paid steps: the user's own clear yes is needed; a vague reply is not approval; refusals are never worked around
The story choices: place, era, mood, which thing is the subject, which props tell the story, what each prop must not turn into in the painting (paint_as text)
Whether a returned painting looks painted enough and how strict the colour-continuity limit is (the score flags, a person decides; tune on the first pair)
The mood of a soundtrack stretch (quiet or tense): picked by measurement because nobody can listen here, and said so

Which rule wins when rules conflict (a dark iron gate can't be the brightest thing; chimney tops in the words band vs words placed beside them; the notice corner's 1.34x slide made before the 1.3x rule)
The overall feel of the light (cool against warm, dusk mood) beyond the rule numbers
Hand-reading landmarks off a liked picture for the camera match (automatic line detection only helps)
Whether a flagged near-touch, thin part or small sign is worth fixing or acceptable for the story
design.summary:
I grouped the 423 hand-found values into 17 tools, plus one shared settings file the plugin would run itself. Each one works out from a new film's own inputs what was found by trial over 35 logs: the script, the word times, the 3D scene and its camera, the check file and prices. Every tool lists its formulas and the cases from this project it must reproduce. A tester can prove each one against the saved files.

**The core.** A small geometry module does the camera sums every helper kept rewriting in scratch files. The film lens has a focal length of 1649 px, so on-screen size is metres × 1649 ÷ distance. One degree of turn moves things 0.027 of the frame width. The same module gives where the street's lines meet and how far a camera may stand. It already reproduces the shot checker's notice corner numbers (meeting point 0.684, 0.4395). It also reproduces all seven letter sizes in works-shot.json exactly (29.0, 14.7, 13.8, 50.0, 47.0, 22.1 and 22.1 px). One shared settings file ends the drift between tools: today the default page pause is 1.4 s in one tool and 1.5 s in the other, and the edge margins disagree too.

**Before anything is drawn.**
- **Check file generator:** writes the shot's check file from the Blender scene instead of by hand.
- **Shot planner:** places the camera, the slide, the plate and the people from the rules. Planned this way, round 4's camera spot shows its bare bottom third (0.65 down) and round 5's spot passes (0.72), before any render.
- **Lettering and figure audit:** sizes signs, heads and landmarks per view.
- **Effects planner:** picks the wind against the cameras and traces each smoke plume on the frame. The round 4 wind moves the plume only 0.044 of the width, a fail; the round 5 wind moves it 0.188, a pass.
- **State picture planner:** lists every plate a change needs and chooses a cut or a blend from how much of the frame changes.
- **Light planner:** sets starting watts and reach from distances, then a small-render loop tunes them against the light rules instead of 26 hand rounds.
- **Painter's request builder:** writes the prompt from the check file, checks the plate first and prices it. The people test comes to 83.9 cents against the ledger's 'about 85'.

**After painting and while building pages.**
- **Painting arrival checks:** line-up, kept shadows, figure outlines and colour continuity, with pass marks.
- **Page timing and words planner:** reproduces round 4's MACHINES label being readable for only 0.38 s, and the PRICES UP fix (0.67 s up to 1.19 s).
- **Page pose sampler:** catches pops, snapping fades, poking-through and still keys that change during a move.
- **Camera path audit:** adds 'no turn during a slide' and plate coverage to the existing camera_audit.py.
- **Script and narration gate** and **sound gates:** the script lint, the estimated timeline and cost, and music level and loudness measured rather than guessed.
- **Model lint:** stripes, same-plane faces, '.001' names, glass.
- **Budget, filming time and memory planner:** reproduces 53 minutes for pages 3-5 and about 94 minutes for chapter 1's 6,641 frames, and sets piece size and two-hour stretches.
- **Preflight runner:** runs whatever applies at each stage and writes one report. On the round 4 Works state it should raise 8 of the critic's 15 findings without a critic.

**First to build:** the geometry and settings, check file generator, shot planner, camera audit, lettering audit, painter's request builder, script gate, timing planner, budget planner and preflight. The light tuner, painting checks, state and effects planners, page sampler, sound gates and model lint come second.

**Plugin kit first.** The plugin's copy of the kit has to catch up with the film kit before any of this. It lacks projected-set.js, make_state_picture.py, make_behind_picture.py, estimate_timeline.py and the pit-village and figure builders. It also has older copies of check_shot.py, graphics.js, the stage, the chapter code and the renderer. Its docs name an example check file it doesn't ship.

**One formula I changed.** In Blender, widening a spotlight's cone does not weaken the light on the subject, so the light planner uses distances only. This should be checked once in Blender.

The tips guide is outlined in 19 sections (sections 0-18). Some things must stay with people: history accuracy, what reads as what on a phone, newcomer understanding, story choices and the user's yes before spending. Those are listed separately.

All the test numbers are recomputed by /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Music/02fc5154-76f5-5aac-a505-860164e7e921/scratchpad/plugin-calculators/verify_test_cases.py, with its output in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Music/02fc5154-76f5-5aac-a505-860164e7e921/scratchpad/plugin-calculators/verify_test_cases-output.txt. The list of plugin files that are missing or out of date is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Music/02fc5154-76f5-5aac-a505-860164e7e921/scratchpad/plugin-calculators/plugin-gap-files.txt. I changed no project file and spent nothing.

verdicts.calculator: Frame geometry core and shared film settings
verdicts.problems: The sums are right. I re-derived the forward-slide parallax, the slide limit L_max = d_end*(ratio-1), the turn for a wanted meeting point and the reach formula. Most of its test cases only check one formula against another copy of the same formula. shot_facts uses the same projection, and assemble_works.py computed works-shot.json letter_pixels with the same pinhole sum, so getting 29.0/14.7/50.0/22.1 back proves consistency, not truth. Two defaults are slightly off. (1) The slide-magnification limit uses the plate's 2730 px height. The painting comes back at 2672 px and is resized up, so the real ratio is (2672/1920)*tan(30.2)/tan(32.2) = 1.29, not 1.314. At 1.29 the checkout's 3.1 -> 2.4 m slide (1.29x) sits right on the limit. (2) A settings file only stops drift if every tool loses its own literal numbers. Today check_shot.py, frame_check.py, assemble_chapter_narration.py (1.4) and estimate_timeline.py (1.5) each keep their own.
verdicts.changes: Build it first, as designed. Compute the plate ratio from the painting's returned height, read from the painting ledger. Remove the literal numbers from every tool in the same change. Add a JS/Python parity test. In film-settings.json, mark each number as measured, judged or invented, so later agents know which ones they may change.

verdicts.problems:
The story role can't be inferred.
- **W1:** the hand file puts DIESEL, the lantern and the men in the story and PETROL in pairs_also. W1 has no support, and by the 1.5 m rule (gap to the gate plane at y 22.3) PETROL (about 1.25 m) would go in and DIESEL (about 1.7 m) and the lantern on its lid would go out, the opposite of the hand file.
- **lights_in_story by distance is wrong:** at the notice corner the notice-glow spot sits 0.25 m over the coals (about 0.95 m up). That is inside the drum's box grown 0.2 m, so the drum would be marked a light prop. That would excuse the drum rim being as bright as the notice, a real fault critics caught in log 31.
- **The title zone can't be found in the Works:** only 27% (W1), 32% (W2) and 28-49% (round 3/4) of the band is sky. The fallback zone then fails rule 12 every time.
- **Missed false alarms:** match_excludes by darkness and thinness misses bordered boards and signs. The checkout sign scored 2-25% outline agreement, and the round 5 wrapper excluded 'board' and 'sign' too.
- **Street-only:** on the checkout counter, check1 reported four props 'landed on something high', 0.9 m up. The checkout file needed on_ground [] and "sky": "ceiling*".
verdicts.changes: Take subject, support, story and work from the shot list, since they are story choices. Generate only the rest: groups (one per import root, one per figure), must_read from lettering materials, pairs_also, lines, the eye range, the sky pattern, and on_ground measured against declared support surfaces (counter, floor, pavement). Mark a group as a light prop only when its own materials emit light (glass, flame). When no sky zone exists, write "band": true and teach check_shot to judge a dark band instead. Replace the match_excludes rule with: leave a group out when its best slide lands on a neighbour of the same kind, or it is thin, dark or a bordered sign. Add an "accepted" list (rule, reason, who accepted it, date) that the checker reports as known rather than as a failure.

verdicts.calculator: Shot planner (camera, slide, plate and people before anything is drawn)
verdicts.problems:
The closed forms are right and better than the hand numbers.
- **W1 reach:** on the level lane d_max for 0.70 is 7.30 m. The nearest man (man-6 at 7.42 m) lands at 0.696 (box bottom 0.704) and the DIESEL drum front at 0.723. The round 4 critic's 'nearest man 7.6 m, feet about 0.72' and assemble_works.py's comment were both wrong: 7.6 m gives 0.692. Head size at 6 m is 63 px, a quarter-height man stands at 6.01 m, and round 4's spot at y 10.2 gives 0.653.
- **It encodes the notice-corner still life as hard limits, but the accepted round 5 Works views break them.** The final round 5 reports (scratchpad redesign/round5-set/checks/final-*/report.md) show W1's crowd story box 0.64 wide against 0.40, many near-touches between men (W3: 1-11 px), drums 1.4-1.6% in the bottom-left quarter, and 27% sky in the title band. W2 misses rule 1 by 0.108 of the frame width (no-2 gateway 117 px below the meeting point). W3's crowd at 29-30 m reaches only 0.67 down, so the planner would demand an eye of about 6.9 m, where the project instead filled the bottom with a non-story handcart. The planner would refuse or endlessly rework the current accepted shots.
- **Silhouettes:** the 'becomes an own-surface silhouette' fallback, and the W4 test case built on it, contradict lesson 137. The people test dropped silhouettes because they read as shadow puppets.
- **The 24 px face limit is untested.** In the people test, far walkers with heads of about 10 px still got pale face or hand dots. The facing man at about 7 m (head about 53 px) got no features, only an orange-lit cheek, judged minor. The prompt did the work, not the distance.
- **Pure-geometry predictions mispredict.** Hulls and 0.28 m cylinders for rules 3/4/8/12 duplicate check_shot and misjudge real silhouettes: raised arms, and the stooped man whose reach caused round 4's false 'rests on brazier'.
- **Auto-applying the checker's metre fixes for 5 rounds** would thrash: round 5 still has 13 layout problems, and lesson 108 found advice that dropped the lantern to the pavement.
- **Slide limit at the wrong distance:** it is judged at the subject, but nearer painted props magnify more (notice corner pail 4.8/3.3 = 1.45x against the notice's 1.34x).

verdicts.calculator: Camera path audit for moving shots
verdicts.problems:
Sound, and it extends a tool that already works. I checked that stillShot slides move the target with the position (cameraAt and notice-corner.js set target = position + ahead*10). The heading is therefore constant, and the 0.02 meeting-point drift test is really a turn test, which is fine. Weaknesses:
- It inherits the magnification-at-subject issue: the notice corner's pail magnifies 1.45x, not the notice's 1.34x.
- The plate-coverage test needs the plate's depth for each pixel (from shot_facts at the plate lens), which must be listed as an input.
- The relief-mode parallax cap is for the older painted-room look and has no value computed yet.
verdicts.changes: Build the built-set mode and the timeline window now. Measure magnification at the nearest painted surface in the end frame, using the painting's returned height. Make relief mode second priority, and compute its cap once from chapter 2's accepted 1-2 unit moves before using it.

verdicts.calculator: Lettering, figure and landmark audit per view
verdicts.problems:
Foreshortening:
- letter_px = h*f/d*|n.v| is wrong for boards turned about a vertical axis: turning shrinks letter width, not height.
- Only tilt toward or away from the camera, as with WAGES lying flat, shrinks height.

Thresholds:
- 'A single word needs at least 25 px' would flag PETROL and DIESEL at 22.1 px. Round 4 recorded them as 'fully readable in W1 and W2'.
- The 25 px figure was a critic's suggestion for WAGES.
- The evidence is: 11 px 'only just', 14 px 'tiny', 22 px readable, 29 px easy.

The dimming formula:
- dim = min(0.3, 0.4*B_named/B_own) gives exactly 0.3 for BANK (118 levels against the boards' 120).
- Round 4 tried 0.3 (52-57 levels against 120-128) and the critic still read BANK, because it is twice the size.
- The accepted 0.15 is a judgement the formula does not reproduce.

Other gaps:
- The 'at least 200 px identifying feature' and '+-0.05 identity column' rules have no data behind them.
- It needs inputs a new film won't have unless defined: sign normals, letter heights, chimney tops, figure facing. Today these come from works-shot.json's one-off keys.
verdicts.changes: Use the vertical part of the view ray for letter height and the horizontal part for width. Fail must-read words under about 20 px and warn at 20-25. For unnamed signs, compare legibility as letter px x contrast against the named signs (calibrate the limit on BANK: about 0.5 of the boards'), or take the sign out of frame. Drop the 200 px and column rules until there is data. Define a standard place-facts JSON that every assemble script writes. Keep chimney-top 'down', back-of-sign, cross-view sign leaks, drum turns (maximin across views, within 1 deg of the hand values) and the continuity counts.

verdicts.calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
verdicts.problems:
Worth building, but several of its tests prove less than they claim.
- **The header test only echoes the template.** The descriptive keep-list text ('a dark sooty hollow with only a faint orange glow low inside') is written by a person; the check file's paint_as field has to hold it.
- **The price test is circular.** The ledger's 'about 85 c' was itself worked out as 4.8 c/MP x (out + in), and fal showed no exact charge (story log 34).
- **Preflight (e) would miss lesson 138's fault.** It flags even bright discs, but the drum's faint inner glow was lifted into a band.
- **The people test showed two more prompt needs:** far walkers got pale face and hand dots, and the facing man got a lit cheek.
- **The grade check needs work first:** it needs the stage's grade curve ported to Python.
verdicts.changes:
Keep it in the first group:
- Add to the preflight: light inside the top 30% of a hollow prop's mask means darken it before painting.
- Add prompt clauses: 'far walkers are flat dark shapes with no pale spots'; a facing figure's face is 'lost in deep shadow under the cap, no lit cheek'.
- Read the real charges from fal's request history once and fit the price formula to them before trusting it.
- Port the grade curve from cinema-stage.js once and test it on round 2's crimson coats (26/1/0).

verdicts.problems:
The pass marks don't fit the evidence.
- **Alignment:** a floor of 0.85 can't detect misalignment on a busy painting. The people test scored 0.874 before alignment; the notice corner was 0.70 before.
- **Figure overlap (IoU >= 0.85):** this would fail 2 of the 5 near men in the people test, the hand-on-bar man (0.587) and the leaning man (0.497). Four helpers judged the painting to have 'the same number, places and poses'.
- **Figure outline (within 3 px >= 0.90):** the stooped man passes only at 0.909. The plate's own outline scores just 0.838 for the hand-on-bar man (outline-chamfer.json), so this measure is noisy at that limit. Walker 4 at 0.634 (his bag lost) is a true catch.
- **Untested scores:** the painted-not-photo score and colour continuity (delta E 8) have no project data.
- **What it misses:** the people test's real must-fix faults. The men went from about 15% to about 50% of their surroundings' brightness. The warm pool on the ground fell from 19.7% to 11.6% against the notice corner. Skin-coloured pixels in the hand-on-bar man's head went from 0 to 183.
verdicts.changes:
Always run alignment. Fail only if the result is no better than before, if the best shift sits at the edge of the search (12 px, 0.985/1.015), or if it ends under 0.85.

Figures: drop IoU. Pass when within-3-px is no more than 0.05 below that figure's plate baseline. Count figure-sized blobs to catch added or lost people.

Add these measures:
- figure-to-surround brightness, plate against painting;
- skin-hue pixels per head;
- a style match against the standard painting (brightness 77.4, spread 26.1, colour strength about 50, ink lines 6.7%, line width about 2.9 px, warm ground share).

The painted score and delta E stay warnings only. Move the cut-out (paper look) checks to second priority.

verdicts.problems: The plate list, splitting changes that fall on different words, the outline groups and the cut threshold are all sound. A share of 0.12 separates round 4's 9.3% men-gone cuts from the 41-76% window blends. The blend length 0.8 + 0.7*(share/0.75) s is invented: the project's blends are works-effects.js steppedBlend, 0.8 s in 3 steps, whatever the area. 'Mask/outline > 3' has one data point: the people test, at about 7.7x.
verdicts.changes: Use the project's steppedBlend default (0.8 s, 3 steps) and drop the area formula. Keep the rest. Add 'two sub-changes on one plate' as an error, because the round 4 slowed plate held both the windows and the men.

verdicts.calculator: Effects planner (smoke, wind, fire, dust, contact shadows)
verdicts.problems:
The wind trace is verified. With the round 5 settings the round 4 wind travels 0.044 of the width and the round 5 wind 0.188, and it reproduces the critic's 0.625 -> 0.748 across. Contact-shadow sizes come within 0.15 m of the hand values.

Two faults:
- **It tests puff centres, not puff edges.** smoke-final-trace.txt shows the puff tops at 0.209-0.228 down, above the lower card's 0.236 bottom.
- **'Sign toward the side with room' has no single answer for two factories:** one wind blows one plume toward the other chimney whichever sign is chosen.

Over-built: dust emitter auto-placement and the paper-look dust rules don't apply to the built-and-painted look.
verdicts.changes: Test puff top edges (centre - width/2) where opacity is 0.2 or more. Trace both wind signs and keep the one that passes. Move the dust rules to second priority. Keep the window-change check (15 levels) and the glow-swing limit.

verdicts.problems: 'At most 4 spoken figures per estimated minute' would fail the accepted newcomer script. It has 28 figures in the estimator's 407 s, which is 4.1 a minute; the old script had 37 in 252 s, 8.8 a minute. 'Unfamiliar word with no explanation within 2 sentences' and 'a stake in the first 30 s' need judgement. The key page at 175 wpm against a 164 median is under the 1.1x median flag; only the 170 wpm absolute limit or a key-page mark catches it. The cost formula rests on one billed point (4,300 credits about US$0.75) and is an upper bound, since re-records showed 0 credits.
verdicts.changes: Set the figures limit at 5-6 a minute, or calibrate it on the two scripts. Turn unfamiliar words and stakes into lists for a person. Require a "key": true mark on the page carrying the main idea. Otherwise build it first, as designed: cue, capitals, names, the rule said twice word for word, guess holds, estimate_timeline sync, and the transcript checks after recording.

verdicts.problems:
Highest value, but the pause formula is wrong for this chapter. clamp(0.3 + 0.85 + 0.2*pieces, 1.1, 1.7) ignores each page's own join. Page 4 has a run-on after 3.5 s and page 5 a peel after 2.0 s, and timeline-estimated.json has gaps of 3.5 and 4.0 s. The clamp would cut those holds to 1.7.

The test numbers for PRICES UP ignore the method's own 0.14 s buildWords delay: 0.67/1.19 s become 0.53/1.05.

Chapter 1's pauses come from the paper look (turn 0.8 s plus folding pieces), so they can't test the cinema formula.

page_events.mjs needs graphics.js instrumented to record every drawn box and its opacity, which is the hardest piece and isn't costed.
verdicts.changes: Set the pause after a page to join.after + join.length + about 0.15 s settle, plus any hold. Clamp to 1.1-1.7 only for plain peels. Read each element type's appear delay from graphics.js. Budget the graphics.js instrumentation as its own task. Keep everything else in the first group: word-lookup lint, readable times, fadeOut at cuts, same-box lines, margins, numbers against the ledger, still lists, planned cuts for find_jumps, and the chunks to re-film.

verdicts.calculator: Page pose sampler (layout, clearance, fades and held shots)
verdicts.problems: Over-built for the current look. About half of it covers paper-look faults: standing pieces at their own distance, rows too wide, knocked-down pieces, the crane seen from too high, and pieces under 60 px. The fading-cut-out check only reports a kit bug; fixing CutOut.set (in the sync list) removes it.
verdicts.changes: Build a slim version, second priority: one-frame pops outside planned cuts, effects visible after their page, still keys changing during a move, holds with no still key, clearance and overlap at events and during moves. Fix the fades in the kit itself. Keep the paper-look checks as an optional mode.

verdicts.problems: Correct in substance, and the ducking loop is linear in dB because the voice drives the gain reduction. One technical slip: 'short-term loudness' is a 3 s window, longer than a word (0.2-0.6 s), so the speech gap measured over word spans would be smeared by the pauses. The mouth-percentile thresholds are untested.
verdicts.changes: Measure the voice and music stems with momentary (400 ms) loudness, or RMS over each word span and each pause of 0.5 s or more. Keep the length, true-peak, alignment and voice gates as they are, called from finish_film.sh.

verdicts.calculator: Budget, filming time, memory and disk planner
verdicts.problems:
The frame-cost table is out of date. Round 4's own measurements (scratchpad redesign/round4-film/film/frame-times.txt, one worker) give:
- held shots with live effects: 0.88-0.99 s a frame;
- sliding: 4.31 s a frame;
- page loading: about 23-58 s a piece.

The design's 1.5 s (held, live) and 6.0 s (moving) applied to pages 3-5 (about 2,080 held-live frames, about 200 sliding, about 10 loads) predict about 79 min against the 53 measured.

Its tests prove nothing:
- '2,283 x 1.4 s = 53 min' only re-multiplies the measured average.
- The 83.9 c and US$1.10 checks reuse the same rates that produced the expected numbers.
- Plate minutes miss the round 3 measurement (10 against 6).
verdicts.changes: Profile one held and one moving frame in every view before filming (each a few seconds after loading) and plan from those numbers. Keep the table only as a fallback, updated to 0.9 / 4.3 s and about 35 s loading a piece. Fit the price formula to real fal charges, read from request history for free. Keep the spend ledger, stretches, piece size, workers, lazy loading and the push checks.

verdicts.problems: The stripe threshold isn't the one that found the faults. find_stripes.py (scratchpad check-round-3/tools) flags faces with UV area / 3D area < 0.02 x the median and reports parts over 0.5 m2; that gave round 3's 15, 27 and 33 parts. The design's 1e-3 x median would find fewer. The rest (same-plane faces, floors just over ground, '.001' names, measured sizes, glass alpha, glowing bases, front axis) is sound, cheap and covered by recorded faults.
verdicts.changes: Use the stripe tool's real thresholds and test them against the round 3 and round 4 counts. Write the measured sizes and front axis into props/index.json. Second priority.

verdicts.calculator: Preflight runner, report and kit sync
verdicts.problems:
The claim that on round 5 everything passes or is listed as known is false. The final round 5 reports list:
- W1: 13 layout and 21 light problems;
- W2: 15;
- W3: 29.

With no accepted-exceptions mechanism, the preflight would block the work the project has accepted.

The '8 of 15 round 4 findings' claim is plausible (2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 12). Finding 5 (gate lamp) was already flagged by check_shot in rounds 3 and 4 and carried over, so the gain is in blocking, not in detecting.

Its test cases are all on data used to derive the rules.
verdicts.changes: Read the check files' "accepted" list: rule, reason, who accepted it, date. Show accepted items as known and block only on new failures. Test the whole chain on checkout C1 (check1-check5 in scratchpad redesign/round5-checkout) as a hold-out place. Keep the kit sync, the regression stills, the planted-fault tests and the critique-before-filming gate.

missing: Shot-kind rule profiles: the design applies the notice-corner still-life rules as hard limits, but the accepted round 5 Works views fail them. W1 crowd box is 0.64 wide (limit 0.40) with near-touches between men and drums 1.4-1.6% bottom-left. W2 rule 1 misses by 0.108 because the subject is an opening. W3's crowd at 29-30 m reaches only 0.67 down and the bottom is filled by a non-story handcart. Profiles are needed for still life, crowd, overview, interior and dark subject, with a priority order when rules conflict (reach 0.70 against the bottom-left limit, crowd width against the rule 3 box).

An 'accepted' list in each check file (rule, reason, who, date) that check_shot and the preflight both read. Today the man_2_note is free text and the final round 5 reports list 13-29 problems that nobody marked as accepted or fixed.

Interiors: 3 of the plan's 6 places (checkout, corner shop, kitchen). Checkout check1 falsely reported four props 'landed on something high' (0.9 m, on the counter). The checkout check file needed on_ground [] and "sky": "ceiling*". The reach and eye formulas need the support surface's height, and the generator's on_ground needs declared support surfaces.

A standard place-facts JSON that every assemble script must write: views with plate, composed and subject; signs with normal and letter height; emitters; figures with facing and height; lights with targets; landmark tops. view_audit, plan_effects and plan_states currently read works-shot.json's one-off keys (men_at_no_1, no-2-tank-top), which a new film won't have.

People test measurements missing from after_painting: figures went from about 15% to about 50% of their surroundings' brightness (a must-fix); skin pixels in a head rose from 0 to 183; the style match against the standard painting (brightness 77.4/77.4, spread 26.1/26.1, colour 45/50, ink lines 6.4%/6.7%, line width 3.7/2.9 px, warm ground 11.6%/19.7%).

Lesson 137 against the plan: own-surface silhouettes were rejected (they read as shadow puppets), yet assemble_works.py still makes W4's men silhouettes, and the shot planner offers silhouettes as a fallback. Resolve this in the code and the planner.

Lesson 138 (darken a faint glow inside a hollow before painting) and the people test's prompt fix for far walkers ('flat dark shapes with no pale spots') are not in the preflight or the prompt template.
The inventory's 'Check pictures against the history' calculation (a contact sheet at each event time, captioned with the spoken sentence and ledger ids, for verify-facts) is in no calculator.

Already automatic but in no calculator's list and needing sync or protection: no lamp on projected surfaces; edges by colour (check_shot); painted sky on a far card (skyCard); full-frame passes ignore depth; peel shading ramp (PEEL_SHADING_IN 0.3); projected-set handover defaults; newcomer graphics (dotPanel, ruleCard, guessRing and others); street and set builder settings (place_prop rays start at pavement + 2 m).

Real fal charges: the US$0.85 people-test figure is itself an estimate (fal shows no exact charge). Read the actual charges from fal's request history or billing to confirm rate x (output + input megapixels) before the budget planner relies on it.

Hold-out validation: the test cases use the notice corner and the Works, which the rules were derived from, and several are circular (letter_pixels came from the same sum; 53 min = 2,283 x the measured 1.4 s; 85 c came from the same rate). Validate every calculator on checkout C1, which is in progress and wasn't used to derive the rules.
Updated frame costs from scratchpad redesign/round4-film/film/frame-times.txt (one worker): held with live effects 0.88-0.99 s a frame, sliding 4.31 s, loading about 23-58 s a piece.

Judgements to add to the judgement list: whether a dark subject (iron gate, opening) uses a 'dark subject' rule set, since round 5 tried to make the gate brightest and failed (0.85x); the exposure target per view (W1 accepted at 28 levels with exposure 1.6); how much to dim an unnamed sign (BANK 0.15 was chosen by eye after 0.3 failed).

Slide magnification must be measured at the nearest painted surface (notice corner pail 1.45x against the notice's 1.34x) and from the painting's returned height (2672 px gives a limit of 1.29, not 1.314).

Correct the hand numbers the formulas disprove: assemble_works.py's comment and the round 4 critic said the nearest man's feet reach about 0.72 down at about 7-7.6 m. The formula gives 0.69-0.70 (measured box bottom 0.704). The 0.72 comes from the DIESEL drum.
skeptic.summary:
I'd keep all 17 calculators, but several need their rules or pass marks changed before they would reproduce what the rounds found by hand. I checked the formulas against the project's own records and changed no files.

**What holds up.** The camera sums are right and beat the hand estimates. At W1 the formula puts the nearest man's feet at 0.696 down (measured 0.704) and the DIESEL drum at 0.723, which is the drum's real 0.72. The round 4 critic's 'about 0.72' for the nearest man was wrong. A head is 63 px at 6 m and 58 px at 6.5 m, and the smoke traces reproduce round 4's failing wind and round 5's passing one.

**Where the design is wrong:**
- **The shot planner and preflight would block the shots the project has accepted.** They treat the notice-corner rules as hard limits, but the final round 5 Works reports show 13 to 29 problems per view. The crowd's box is 0.64 wide against a 0.40 limit, men nearly touch each other, and drums sit in the bottom-left quarter. W2 misses rule 1, and W3's crowd reaches only 0.67 down. The design says round 5 passes; it doesn't. The fix is a rule set per kind of shot (still life, crowd, overview, interior, dark subject) and an 'accepted' list in each check file.
- **The planner's silhouette fallback was already rejected.** The people test dropped dark silhouettes because they read as shadow puppets (lesson 137). The 24 px face limit is also untested: tiny far walkers still got face dots, while the facing man at about 7 m got none.
- **Several pass marks would fail the people test the helpers approved.**
  - Two of the five near men fail the figure-overlap test (0.587 and 0.497).
  - The 0.85 alignment floor was already met before alignment (0.874), so it can't detect a misaligned painting.
- **Lettering limits disagree with what was judged.**
  - The 25 px single-word rule would flag PETROL and DIESEL at 22 px, which round 4 called fully readable.
  - The dimming formula gives exactly the 0.3 for BANK that the critic rejected.
  - Height foreshortening is wrong for boards turned sideways.
- **Some timing and script rules contradict the project's own files.**
  - The page-pause formula ignores each page's own exit, so it would cut the 3.5 and 4.0 s holds after pages 4 and 5 down to 1.7.
  - The script gate's limit of 4 spoken figures a minute fails the accepted newcomer script (4.1 a minute).
  - The blend-length formula is invented; the project uses 0.8 s in 3 steps.
- **Filming-time and price numbers are out of date or circular.** Round 4 measured 0.9 s a frame for held shots and 4.3 s for slides. The design's 1.5 s and 6.0 s would predict about 79 minutes for pages 3 to 5 against the 53 measured. The 85-cent painting cost and the 53-minute check only repeat the numbers they were derived from.
- **Two thresholds don't match the tools that set them.** The stripe check uses a different limit from the scratch tool that found the striped parts. The light tuner's goals fight each other when the subject is dark.

**What's missing:**
- Indoor places: 3 of the 6 planned places are interiors. Counter props falsely came up as 'landed on something high' in the checkout's first check.
- A standard file of place facts that every build script writes, so a new film has the inputs these calculators need.
- The people test's tone and style checks: the men painted paler, skin pixels added, the warm pool on the road halved.
- Lesson 138's glow-in-a-hollow check before painting.
- A captioned still sheet for the history checker.
- Reading real fal charges to confirm the price formula.

**Biggest test gap:** nothing has been checked on a place the rules weren't built from. The checkout scene now in progress is the obvious place to do that.

**Over-built parts to trim:** the planner's geometric predictions, which the checker already measures in about 15 seconds; the page-pose checks for the old paper look; dust auto-placement; and an automatic light tuner, where proposing one change per round is safer. Everything I checked is in the round reports under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Music/02fc5154-76f5-5aac-a505-860164e7e921/scratchpad/redesign/`.
